532929|2026-03.headline: Brigade FY26 pre-sales fell 5% to INR 7,424 crore on approval delays; FY27 pre-sales guided to at least 20% growth, aiming for INR 9,000 crore.
532929|2026-03.overview: FY26 pre-sales were INR 7,424 crore, down 5% YoY, as launches slipped: 8.3 million sq ft launched against a 12 million sq ft plan, with about 3.3 million sq ft pushed into FY27 (mostly Chennai). Q4 pre-sales were INR 2,521 crore (up 44% QoQ by value) from 4 million sq ft of launches. Consolidated FY26 revenue rose 11% to INR 5,909 crore with EBITDA of INR 1,638 crore (28% margin), and PAT after minority interest was INR 644 crore. Operating cash flow weakened because of higher construction spend, and management expects it to rise in line with sales growth. Management says the approval issues are largely behind it, and it has guided FY27 launches of about 11.5-12 million sq ft.

segments.name: Real Estate (FY26)
segments.commentary: Turnover INR 4,002 crore (+11% YoY) with EBITDA INR 525 crore. Q4 turnover INR 1,026 crore with EBITDA INR 142 crore. Management says operating POCM margins are in the high-20s to around 30%, while reported margins are diluted by revenue recognition mix.

segments.name: Leasing (FY26)
segments.commentary: Turnover INR 1,303 crore (+12% YoY) with EBITDA INR 906 crore (+18%). Q4 turnover INR 337 crore with EBITDA INR 228 crore. Split: office INR 877 crore, retail INR 220 crore, management business INR 206 crore. Normalised EBITDA margin is above 80%; facility management (about INR 200 crore a year) runs at about 15%.

segments.name: Hospitality (FY26)
segments.commentary: Turnover INR 604 crore (+13% YoY) with EBITDA INR 207 crore. Q4 turnover INR 160 crore with EBITDA INR 60 crore. Q4 occupancy 78%, ADR up 8% QoQ, RevPAR up 13% QoQ; FY26 RevPAR +6% on ADR +7%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 pre-sales: at least 20% growth over FY26, aiming for about INR 9,000 crore, conditional on current sentiment and market conditions holding.

North Bengaluru project is delayed by bylaw changes requiring redesign.

Office: Whitefield JV with Bain (50:50, pure equity partners) on 10.8 acres opposite ITPL, with about 2 million sq ft of office and a 250-key 5-star hotel, targeted for completion in about 40 months after approval. Leasing: about 3 million sq ft of new completions expected in FY27. WTC Bengaluru: Amazon vacated about 630,000 sq ft, with about 100,000 sq ft already leased.
demand_pricing: Pre-sales mix FY26: sustenance 57%, launches 43%. Q4 launch share of pre-sales about 55%. Geographic split (Q4 and FY26 approx. same): Bengaluru 65%, Hyderabad 20%, Chennai 15%.
Conversion of site visits steady at 10-12% across cities; NRI buyers around 10% of pre-sales value; some markets showing longer conversion cycles.

FY26 average realisation up 9% YoY to INR 12,107 per sq ft. Like-for-like price increase high single digits (8-9%); management plans 7-9% annual price increases after launch. Upcoming launch APR around INR 10,000 per sq ft vs inventory above INR 12,000 per sq ft; overall APR increase of 13% was partly mix-driven.

Ticket-size mix: ultra-luxury about 30% of portfolio, expected to decline. Most FY27 launch tickets below INR 3 crore; affordable up to INR 75 lakh, mid-segment up to INR 1.5 crore, premium up to INR 3 crore.
Unsold inventory about 7.5 million sq ft. Residential buyer base: GCC and IT are the largest; IT services about 26% of leasing portfolio.

Leasing: about 1.1 million sq ft leased in FY26; GCCs 58% of the lease book; top anchor tenants (above 1 lakh sq ft) are 65% of the portfolio. Lease rent escalation expected at 10-15% for Amazon's vacated space at WTC Bengaluru. Rental collections 99%.
Commercial monetisation (strata sales) annual run-rate about INR 550 crore; Twin Towers to be exited in FY27, keeping about 100,000 sq ft of common amenities.
Hospitality demand anchored in domestic travel; foreign arrivals and MICE were hit by Middle East tensions.

qa_highlights.question: Plan to fill WTC Bengaluru after Amazon exit, and expected rental uplift?
qa_highlights.answer: Amazon vacated about 630,000 sq ft; about 100,000 sq ft already leased on a couple of floors. Leasing is expected floor-wise or 2-3 floors at a time over the next couple of quarters, with 10-15% rent mark-to-market (up to 20% for half-floors).

qa_highlights.name: Cumulative GDV available for launch over two years and land replenishment?
qa_highlights.question: What is the cumulative GDV available for launch over the next two years, and what is the land replenishment strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Rolling four-quarter pipeline of 11.5 million sq ft and INR 11,900-12,000 crore GDV. Land bank of 57 million sq ft, of which about 75% is residential. Replenishment focused on Bengaluru and Hyderabad, moderately Chennai.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 9,000 crore pre-sales guidance conservative given unsold inventory and launch conversion history?
qa_highlights.answer: Management accepted it is somewhat conservative. It cited Chennai launches selling more evenly across construction, and launch slippage into H2 leaving less time to sell in-year. Management aims to push inventory sales and pull launches forward.

qa_highlights.question: Quarter-wise launch phasing and approval status for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Hyderabad about 1 million sq ft in Q3 and another 1 million in Q4; Morgan Heights 1 million sq ft relaunch in Q1; Bengaluru launches in Q2-Q3. The primary approval issues are considered resolved.

qa_highlights.question: Cash flow trajectory and collections trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Collections were flat as launches were deferred early in FY26; that cash is now converting. Operating cash flow is expected to grow in percentage terms close to sales growth, a few hundred bps lower.

qa_highlights.question: Reported margin weakness in resi and leasing, and when will it improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Resi reported margins reflect completion-based recognition of older, earlier-sold projects that did not capture recent price increases; POCM operating margin is around 30%. Leasing is above 80% on a normalised basis; reported margins are diluted by about INR 200 crore of facility management revenue at about 15% and about INR 35 crore of fit-out recoveries, plus a Q4 accounting gross-up.

qa_highlights.question: How should sales velocity be viewed against the INR9,000 crore presales guidance, given Q1 sales of about INR1,050 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects higher sales velocity once launches start in Q2, so the quarterly run-rate should rise materially.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timing, occupancy at completion and rental EBITDA contribution of the commercial launches, and what is steady-state leasing revenue and leverage?

Leasing is targeted within 6 to 8 quarters of OC. FY26 office leasing revenue was about INR765 crore, with about 20% revenue CAGR expected over 5 to 6 years.

qa_highlights.question: What are the near-term hotel trends, and what occupancy or ARR gains are expected for FY27 including the Kochi rebranding?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 ADR up 7%, occupancy 76% vs 74.5%, and about 10% of event/MICE business lost to West Asia disruption. Management expects MICE recovery in Q3. Kochi occupancy is back in the 70s in Q2 and ADR is expected to rise 15% to 20% post rebranding.

qa_highlights.question: Are the Hyderabad Neopolis 2 and Whitefield-Hoskote launches still on track for Q4, and what is the WTC Bengaluru leasing outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Hyderabad launch is being advanced to Q3 or sooner; Whitefield-Hoskote is now a Q3 launch. WTC Bengaluru (1.13 million sq ft building, Brigade holds 0.71 million sq ft) is about 50% leased with about 375,000 sq ft vacant; large RFPs were postponed due to West Asia, so leasing is shifting to 20,000 to 40,000 sq ft deals at 10% to 15% mark-to-market rent increases, with closure targeted in 3 to 4 quarters.

qa_highlights.answer: Morgan Heights is about 0.7 million sq ft of the 6.7 million sq ft unsold, attributable value about INR650 crore. Roughly 1 million sq ft of the shortfall is Morgan Heights and about 1 million sq ft reflects re-phasing of sales within projects, with FY27 presales guidance of INR9,000 crore maintained.

qa_highlights.question: How is PPAP handling raw material inflation from the West Asia conflict, and what is the margin impact?

532937|2026-03.headline: Kuantum Papers Q4 FY26 EBITDA rose 22% QoQ to INR48 crore (15.90% margin) on NSR of INR3,700/MT, despite input cost pressure.
532937|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 operational income was INR301 crore, up 4% QoQ, driven by NSR improvement to INR3,700/MT, while input costs rose about INR2,000/MT amid the West Asia conflict. EBITDA reached INR48 crore (margin 15.90%, up 234 bps QoQ) and PAT INR14 crore (margin 4.75%, up 137 bps QoQ). Management guided to volume growth to about 2,30,000 MT and EBITDA margin of 18-20% over the next few years, with PM3 upgrade and pulp (DDS) commissioning slated for mid-June to July 2026.

segments.name: Notebook paper
segments.commentary: Share fell from about 22% of sales before the September GST change to about 7-8% now; management intends to exit the segment after machine upgrades, citing reversal of input tax credit at nil GST.

segments.name: Copier, high-end printing, specialty paper
segments.commentary: Copier share is growing steadily; Maplitho and size grades target high-end printing; specialty grades targeted at 20-30% of production volume.

segments.name: Paperboard
segments.commentary: Management noted MIP for paperboard continues with a one-year extension; paperboard was not discussed in detail.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top line expected at INR1,400-1,500 crore, rising gradually to INR1,600 crore; FY28 INR1,600-1,700 crore (management's medium-term view: INR1,600-1,700 crore).
Volumes to rise from about 1,62,000-1,63,000 MT to about 2,30,000 MT, a 40-50% increase, at utilisation above 90-95%.
EBITDA margin target of 18-20% over the medium term.
Operating cost reduction of 5-8% of total manufacturing cost once AI/digital projects are fully implemented, expected across machines by FY27-FY28.
Peak long-term debt of INR650-675 crore by end-2027, reducing INR100-200 crore a year thereafter; annual repayments of INR170-180 crore over the next 2-3 years.
Remaining capex of about INR125 crore to be spent in FY27; no new capex planned beyond current projects, though another expansion may be considered in about two years.
Tissue paper project deferred, not shelved, until debt is under control.
Wheat straw prices expected to ease after rice sowing starts in early June; Q1 season expected to be lean with pricing pressure.
capex_capacity: PM2 rebuild completed March 2026, capacity raised to 75 TPD; PM1 rebuild in December 2025 added about 20 TPD on average in Q4.
PM3 upgrade delayed due to German imported parts; now planned by mid-June/July 2026 (previously around May).
Displacement Digester System (DDS) for wood pulping under extensive testing, commissioning targeted by mid-June; pulp capacity to come on stream by PM3 commissioning (July).
Two-stage recausticizing plant and 80 TPD synchro sheeter commissioned; overall utilisation above 92% on PM1, PM2 and PM4 (OE levels).
Cost of PM3 upgrade not expected to escalate versus the earlier INR140-150 crore estimate.
demand_pricing: Pricing firmed in Q4 on higher demand, but May price hikes partly reversed; management says it holds prices at about INR69,000-70,000/ton.
Low-priced imports persisted through FY26, lowering domestic prices; West Asia freight disruption reduced import volumes in Q4, with risk of China/Indonesia trade diversion.

Anti-subsidy application expected to be processed by FY-end (March 2027); anti-dumping application on writing and printing paper typically takes 1.5-2 years; MIP for writing/printing paper still under review.
Global pulp prices at about USD600-700/ton, expected to stay in that range given new capacity additions.
Wheat straw prices up about 50-60% YoY, with the fuel-use competition now unwound; wood chip prices broadly stable.
Chemical input costs up about 3-5% for some chemicals; the company is absorbing rather than passing these through.
Dealer network of about 90 committed dealers plus about 20 irregular dealers; Gulf and North African export markets being developed.

qa_highlights.question: Are import pressures visible now, and will they hurt pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volumes from China and Indonesia did not arrive in Q4 due to West Asia freight disruption; the impact may return later, and the industry is pursuing Gulf export opportunities. Comment restricted to white paper, not paperboard.

qa_highlights.question: Current debt and capex plans for FY27-FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Long-term debt was INR720 crore on 31 March 2026; peak debt of INR650-675 crore by end-2027. Remaining capex of about INR125 crore in FY27 and no new capex planned beyond existing projects.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of PM3 and pulp capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: PM3 delayed due to German parts, now targeted by mid-June; pulp upgrade to come on stream alongside PM3 in July 2026.

qa_highlights.question: How will the new capacity be absorbed, given the demand environment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 95%+ utilisation; cited the dealer network, Gulf and Northern Africa markets, and a 25-30% specialty grade mix as offsets.

qa_highlights.question: How much opex can be cut from AI and capacity additions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 5-8% of total manufacturing cost reduction once AI systems are deployed across machines, progressing machine by machine and mill-wide, with completion targeted by FY27-FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company refinance or reduce cost of funds?
qa_highlights.answer: Average long-term cost of funds is about 8.5%; management is exploring FCNRB and cheaper funding options. Buybacks are not being considered for now.

Leverage is high: long-term debt of INR720 crore at about 8.5% average cost, with annual repayments of INR170-180 crore.
Lean season expected in the next 2-3 months with historical pricing dips; management expects reversal around September.
Input costs (chemicals, wheat straw, pulp) remain elevated; the company is absorbing chemical cost increases.
Notebook exit reduces the top line and may affect volume in the near term.

532937|2026-06.headline: Kuantum Q1 FY27 operational income rose 36% YoY to INR304 crore, but EBITDA was flat at INR40 crore (13.2% margin) as input costs outran price gains.
532937|2026-06.overview: Paper sales volume grew 35% YoY to 42,922 metric tons, and blended NSR improved about INR3,400/ton QoQ. Cost per ton rose about INR4,200 QoQ on raw material, chemical and fuel inflation linked to the West Asia conflict, so EBITDA stayed broadly flat YoY and PAT was INR6 crore. Management cut its FY27 top-line expectation to INR1,300 crore-plus from the earlier INR1,400-1,500 crore and pushed the 16-18% EBITDA margin target to the year-end. PM3 rebuild completion, pulp capacity additions and anti-dumping applications were the main operational updates.

segments.name: Paper (writing & printing, copier, maplitho)
segments.commentary: Realisation around INR68,000-69,000/ton per management, targeted to reach INR72,000-75,000 in 4-6 months. Specialty grades are just under 20% of mix (18-19% stated), target 30%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top line revised to INR1,300 crore-plus, versus earlier INR1,400-1,500 crore guidance; management said realisations are running below earlier expected levels.
EBITDA margin at least 16-18% by year-end; management says Q3 onwards is when these margins should be visible, not Q2.
FY28 top line expected INR1,400-1,500 crore; FY29-30 conservatively INR1,500 crore at current pricing, INR1,600-1,650 crore if pricing rises to about INR75,000/ton.
Peak debt about INR760-770 crore; scheduled repayments about INR170-175 crore per year for the next 2-3 years; debt to fall below INR300-350 crore within 3 years.
AI-led opex reduction target of 4-5% by March 2028.
Pulp capacity to rise to about 410-415 TPD from 365 TPD.

Native starch system commissioned on PM2 and PM3.
Folio ream wrapping machine installed in the finishing house.
PM3 shut for major rebuild; management expects commissioning within about a week of the call (mid-August 2026), completing the upgradation programme.
Pulping capacity of about 200 TPD each for agro and wood, said to be sufficient for all four machines.
EC clearance for PM3 upgrade filed and awaited.

demand_pricing: Demand supported by education, publishing and office consumption; management expects demand to stay supportive.
Chinese imports diminishing, attributed mainly to shipping and container cost issues; imported copier/maplitho price seen at $610-620/ton near port.
Anti-dumping and anti-subsidy duty applications filed for writing and printing paper, covering 40-140 GSM; management hopes for a favourable decision, assumed 5-year duration.
Maplitho hit by inverted duty structure after GST change; management says Kuantum is reducing notebook paper exposure and passing GST losses to customers.
Management says pricing held flat QoQ into Q2 with no discounting; dealer channel inventory described as lean.

Revenue guidance cut and inconsistency with earlier FY28-30 projections.

Pending EC clearance for PM3 and pending anti-dumping and anti-subsidy duty decision.
Debt of about INR760-770 crore at peak and interest burden on PAT.

532937|2026-09.headline: Kuantum Papers Q2 FY27 revenue fell 8% QoQ to INR279 crores and PAT was INR2 crores, as PM 3 shutdown and input costs hit a lean quarter.
532937|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 operational income was INR279 crores, down 8% QoQ, as the PM 3 rebuild (28 June to 21 August 2026) cut volumes by about 6,000 tons. EBITDA was INR35 crores at a 12.4% margin, down 84 bps, on lower realisations and higher raw material and fuel costs linked to the West Asia conflict. PAT was INR2 crores (0.8% margin). H1 FY27 revenue rose 16% YoY to INR533 crores, but H1 PAT was only INR9 crores because depreciation and finance costs rose. Management guided to a 7% to 11% price increase over Q3 and Q4, of which about 4% was taken in late September.

financial_highlights.change: lower due to higher depreciation and finance costs

segments.name: Writing and printing paper (core, four PMs)
segments.commentary: Q2 production was 40,600 tons, with the remaining machines running at 100% utilisation. Management said orders were booked in advance and all output was sold. Specialty paper is about 17% to 18% of the mix, against a target of 25% to 30% in 12 to 15 months.

segments.name: Paperboard / kraft
segments.commentary: Management said a minimum import price (MIP) is already notified for kraft and paperboard varieties. No segment financials were given.

guidance_outlook: Price increases of 7% to 11% targeted by end of year, across Q3 and Q4. About 4% was taken in late September and is being sustained. The next hike is expected after Diwali.
H2 FY27 EBITDA margin guided at about 14%. Management also said industry margins should recover to 18% to 20% in FY28. Analysts' 17% to 18% H2 figure was not confirmed.
Revenue target of over INR1,300 crores for FY27 reiterated. Management said Q3 should be far better than Q2, with lost volume of about 6,000 tons to be regained.
Cost savings of about 1.5% to 2% on total chemical consumption expected from the single-vendor TCM chemical solution.
Depreciation of about INR80 crores per year. Debt repayment of INR180 crores in FY27 is on track, with a similar amount in FY28. Management said deleveraging will begin after the next two years.
Target of about 1 crore clonal saplings a year in the next two to three years. Current production is 17.93 lakh saplings in the quarter.
capex_capacity: PM 3 commissioned 28 August 2026, rebuilt in 59 days against a 65-day plan. All four paper machines are now upgraded, adding a film press, I-table, table vision, web break monitoring, calendaring and automatic starch cooking.

Marketable output is about 600 tons per day at the optimised product mix, against a design capacity of 675 tons per day on an anchor GSM of 64. Orders are shifting to 52 to 58 GSM, which lowers tonnage.
Double Displacement Digester system improved wood pulp yield by 1% and cut steam use from 1.8 to 0.8 metric tons per tonne of pulp.
Environmental projects (lime kiln and CNCG gas handling) are in progress, with about INR139 crores of CWIP, to be completed in Q3 FY27. Management said there is no further major capex planned.
Environmental clearance has been applied for and is at an advanced stage. The 20 MW turbine generator and a 30 TPH boiler were overhauled during the quarter.
demand_pricing: Q2 was seasonally lean and the industry faced cost inflation. Management said Q2 had almost no price increase, with the first hike taken in the last week of September.

Imports have fallen because of higher ocean freight from the Gulf conflict, and exports have also fallen, so domestic supply is more balanced. Anti-dumping duty applications on writing and printing paper are with the government, with 3 to 6 months expected for completion.

Wood (about INR12,000/tonne) is expected to stay flat or fall as availability improves. Wheat straw prices are temporarily elevated after unseasonal rain and a labour shortage, and are expected to normalise after Diwali.

Starch is about 2% to 2.5% of paper cost. Sulphuric acid from West Asia added about 2% to sales cost. Fuel costs rose about 3% to 3.5%. Input coal costs rose about 2.5% to 3%. Coal mix is about 85% coal and 15% agro.
Chinese capacity is being cut (Chenming and Nine Dragons closures), and Indonesian exports are steady.

qa_highlights.question: What is the West Asia war impact on costs, and what was the wood-cost offset?
qa_highlights.answer: Sulphuric acid and chemicals added about 2% to sales cost, and fuel about 3% to 3.5%. Raw material cost and consumption fell 15% to 17% versus Q1, but no absolute figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: What was the Q2 production loss from the PM 3 shutdown?
qa_highlights.answer: About 6,300 tons lost, mainly from PM 3. Management put the EBITDA impact at about INR40 crores, though the transcript does not say whether this is per tonne or total.

qa_highlights.question: Will price hikes last, and what H2 margin is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects hikes to hold for at least two quarters. H2 FY27 EBITDA margin guided at about 14%. Analysts cited 17% to 18% for H2, and management did not dispute that figure.

qa_highlights.question: Why has CWIP risen to INR139 crores, and what is the capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: The balance is for auxiliary efficiency items and environmental projects (lime kiln and CNCG), to be completed in Q3 FY27. Management said no further major capex is planned.

qa_highlights.question: What are the debt and depreciation outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Peak debt is about INR700 crores. Depreciation is about INR80 crores a year. Debt repayment is INR180 crores in FY27, with a similar amount in FY28. Deleveraging is expected after the next two years.

qa_highlights.question: Will capital be returned to shareholders, through buybacks or a higher promoter stake?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the focus is on cash flow for debt repayment, and there are no plans for changes to the equity capital structure.

risks_watch: Price hikes of 7% to 11% depend on market acceptance and on the anti-dumping decision. Management said the market's acceptance is not unlimited.
Coal supply is constrained because allocated coal is being diverted to the power sector. Open-market coal is available but more expensive.
Mix shift to 52 to 58 GSM is cutting tonnage below the 675 TPD design capacity, and output is now about 600 TPD. Management said it is targeting revenue over tonnage.
Debt of about INR700 crores and higher depreciation and interest will weigh on PAT for the next two years. H1 PAT was INR9 crores.
Watch for environmental clearance, Q3 price realisations, completion of the lime kiln and CNCG projects, and the anti-dumping and MIP outcome for writing and printing paper.
Wheat straw and fuel costs are expected to normalise after Diwali, but management also said input costs are rising structurally.

key_quotes: We are proud to share that with this commissioning, all 4 paper machines have now been successfully upgraded and modernized in line with our mill upgradation plan.
We are expecting prices to increase in the range of 7% to 11%.
So these are only efficiency initiatives, which were defined along the way.

532940|2026-03.headline: J. Kumar FY26 revenue rose 1% to INR5,723 crore with EBITDA flat at INR823 crore; management guides 15% top-line growth in FY27.

Q4 FY26 revenue fell 3% YoY to INR1,585 crore and PAT fell 5% to INR110 crore. 532953|2026-03.headline: V-Guard Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 14.1% YoY to INR1,755 crore and PAT 23% to INR112 crore, with FY26 EBITDA margin at 8.8%.
532953|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was strong, with revenue up 14.1% YoY to INR1,755 crore and EBITDA excluding other income up 19.3% to INR171 crore, while FY26 revenue grew 7% and EBITDA rose 2.6% to INR527 crore. Growth came almost entirely in the second half after a weak summer in the first half. Management is pursuing price hikes of roughly 13% to offset input cost inflation linked to the West Asia conflict, with about 75% landed so far. Net cash rose to INR231 crore and the board recommended a final dividend of INR1.5 per share.

segments.commentary: Largest revenue contributor; Q4 revenue grew 15.9% YoY. Wires face rising competition from new entrants, though management sees the category as low-margin and scale-dependent.

segments.name: Consumer Durables (Fans, Water Heaters, Kitchen Appliances, Air Coolers)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 4.1% YoY; fans and air coolers declined while water heaters and kitchen grew strongly. TPW fans are short of supply due to a plastic raw material shortage.

segments.name: Sunflame (Kitchen Appliances)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 8.6% YoY; the CSD business is still slowing, but non-CSD grew about 16%. GT integration is complete and sales integration is still underway.

guidance_outlook: Management aims for 10-12% volume growth and 1-2% price growth (about 15% total) over time, with higher price growth likely in FY27 due to cost inflation.
EBITDA margin: management says at least 10% is the target for the next year if summer is good, but declined to commit to 11-12%; cited prolonged high cost as a reason for caution.
Expects a good growth year for Consumer Durables on a low base, and a strong start to FY27 given Q4 momentum and a supportive summer forecast.

Price hikes of about 10-12% (some up to 15-20% industry-wide) face retailer pushback; the company gave case-by-case support in regions where summer has not started.
South India summer demand is strong (sales started early March/April); non-South is mixed due to rain, with East a key market for summer products.
Channel financing covers about 35% of the debtor book (customer-linked, not category-linked); collections were strong in the March quarter.
Kerala is about 15-16% of revenue; no impact seen so far, with summer in Kerala supportive. Non-South contributed 48% of FY26 revenue; South grew 16.2% and non-South 11.8% in Q4.
Competition: wire entrants and lighting peers are entering; management expects consolidation to be slow and sees the top 4-5 brands per category as the survivors.

532953|2026-06.headline: V-Guard Q1 FY27 revenue rose 23.5% YoY to INR1,810 crore and EBITDA margin widened to 10.5% from 8.4%.
532953|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 23.5% YoY to INR1,810 crore, with about 14% price and 9% volume contribution per management's blended split. EBITDA excluding other income rose 54.5% to INR191 crore, and PAT rose 76% to INR130 crore. Gross margin held at 36.9%, flat YoY, as management says roughly 75-80% of input cost inflation has been passed through. Management raised FY27 growth expectations to above 15% and reaffirmed a 9-10% EBITDA margin, while noting wires volumes were nearly flat under a large price increase.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR155 crore a year ago

segments.name: Electronics (stabilizers, UPS, solar)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 22.8% YoY with all major categories contributing; solar is growing fastest on a small base, and solar pumps for Maharashtra government are only a couple of crore so far.

segments.name: Electricals
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 27.7% YoY, aided by higher copper prices; wires saw very high price growth with near-flat volumes, while ex-wires grew at high double digits and switchgear, modular switches and pumps grew volumes robustly.

segments.name: Consumer Durables (fans, water heaters, kitchen, air coolers)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 19.2% YoY; induction cooktops spiked, other kitchen categories grew healthily, fans grew reasonably (pedestal fans short on inventory), and air coolers lost share due to weak North demand and competitor price delays.

segments.name: Sunflame
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 18.3% YoY on a low base; management says integration is complete and a sales acceleration programme has started, with margin recovery expected to be more gradual than top-line recovery.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth expected to be more than 15%, with management saying it may be 'a bit more than 15%' given price growth; no specific number given.
EBITDA margin to be maintained at 9-10% ('we should be okay this year in terms of margins').
Long-term target of 15% growth, with normal-year mix of 10-12% volume and 2-3% price growth.
Capex to average INR150-170 crore per year over the next two years, below the earlier INR200-250 crore range.
Advertising spend to reach about 2.5% of revenue for FY27, with spending resumed from around May 15.
Pricing actions about 80-85% complete; some smaller categories still need price increases in the current quarter, and management does not expect large further hikes.
Wires competitive intensity expected to slow growth for some unorganised-sector players by 1-2% vs market, with no major impact in the first one to two years.
capex_capacity: Capex guidance revised: INR150-170 crore per year on average for the next two years, versus the earlier INR200-250 crore range referenced by the analyst.
Own manufacturing now above 65% of products (previously sourced), a key driver of gross margin improvement.
Investment phase in capability (technology, systems, R&D, renewables, lighting) expected to last another two to three years before plateauing.
Lighting launch planned in FY27; solar rooftop next-generation battery (BESS) launch planned in the next two to three months.
Gegadyne (battery start-up) has moved from R&D to commercial supply to small customers; V-Guard may source batteries from it.
demand_pricing: Pricing: management cited a blended split of about 14% price and 9% volume within 22-23% revenue growth; category price increases range from 5% to 18%, with some categories cited up to 30%.
Wires: very large price increases led to near-zero volume growth as customers deferred purchases; value growth held up and margins were maintained.
Copper purchase mix shifted to roughly 95% domestic from 70-80% earlier, which helped working capital through supplier credit.
Management described the 12-14% price increase over four months as unprecedented since 2006 and said consumers have accepted it so far.
Air coolers lost share as some competitors delayed price increases and the North zone was weak.
Solar rooftop: focus is B2C residential and small SMEs; BESS seen as the next large opportunity at about INR1.5-2 lakh per home.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 22-23% growth is price vs volume, and how much of the input inflation has been passed through?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended growth split is about 14% price and 9% volume; about 80-85% of pricing actions are complete and roughly 75-80% of inflation has been passed through, with the gross margin expected to hold.

qa_highlights.question: Why is South growing faster than non-South for the fourth quarter in a row?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributes it mainly to weather: South had a good summer while North was disrupted by rain. It also said it took pricing ahead of competitors in non-South markets.

qa_highlights.question: Is the capex guidance still INR2-2.5 billion a year?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Capex is expected to average INR150-170 crore a year over the next two years.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 growth and margins be higher than the medium-term guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 growth is expected to be more than 15%, with the 15% figure kept as the long-term aim. EBITDA margin is expected at 9-10%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is payables so high on the balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was a one-off: copper purchases shifted to domestic suppliers who give credit, instead of imports paid by LC, and payables are expected to normalise.

qa_highlights.question: Why not gain share in wires by passing on less price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said wires are a commoditised, utilitarian product with low margins, so a price war would be lose-lose and hard to end.

risks_watch: Wires price war from new entrants and a possible festive-season launch; wire volumes near zero and customer deferment.
Sustainability of working capital gains, as the high payables are described as one-off and net cash of INR670 crore may normalise.
Sunflame margin recovery is expected to be slow given pricing transmission lags in CSD and non-South general trade.
Further commodity volatility from the West Asia conflict and shipping constraints; management says a few smaller categories still need price action.
Ad spend at 2.5% for FY27 vs 2.2% in Q1, and the budget was set on January prices, not current input costs.
Cost base has risen sharply over five years; management expects extended investment for two to three more years.
532953|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the quarter and margins, with the word 'shock' used for price inflation. Cautious and evasive on categories, state-level data and wire-category volumes, which were not disclosed. Management is wary of predicting the FY27 growth rate given volatile commodity prices.
key_quotes: We have delivered double-digit EBITDA margin this quarter.
So in a normal environment, yes, we should grow at 10% to 12% volume growth and 2% to 3% price growth.
So the problem with this price war is that you will start it, but you won't be able to end it.

rows.why: Q1 EBITDA margin rose to 10.5% from 8.4% and own manufacturing is above 65% of products, but management guides only 9-10% for FY27 and says ad spend rises to 2.5%, Sunflame recovery is gradual and the high payables are one-off.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Lighting launch and solar rooftop BESS launch are planned, but no new plant or line capacity was announced and capex is cut to INR150-170 crore a year versus INR200-250 crore earlier, with utilisation not disclosed.

rows.why: Management revised capex down to an average of INR150-170 crore a year for the next two years, and utilisation was not given, so no new capex programme is signalled.

rows.why: FY27 revenue growth raised to 'a bit more than 15%' from Q1 growth of 23.5% (about 14% price, 9% volume), with pricing actions 80-85% complete.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management flagged wires price-war risk from new entrants, a possible festive-season launch, West Asia commodity volatility and ad spend rising to 2.5% from 2.2%, though EBITDA margin guide of 9-10% was held.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: FY27; solar rooftop BESS in next 2-3 months
rows.why: Lighting launch is planned in FY27 and a solar rooftop next-generation battery (BESS) launch is planned in the next two to three months, targeting about INR1.5-2 lakh per home.

rows.label: Payables and net cash normalisation
rows.why: Management called the high payables a one-off from copper sourcing shifting to ~95% domestic from 70-80%, and net cash of INR670 crore (vs INR155 crore a year ago) may normalise.

rows.label: Sunflame margin recovery
rows.why: Sunflame revenue grew 18.3% on a low base and integration is complete, but management expects margin recovery to be more gradual than top-line recovery given CSD and non-South general trade pricing lags.

rows.label: Wires price war and festive launch
rows.why: Wires volumes were near flat after very large price increases, and management says a price war would be lose-lose, with a possible festive-season launch from new entrants.

tone.note: Management was confident on the quarter, margins and raised growth outlook, but cautious on wire volumes, category and state data and FY27 growth precision; analysts probed price vs volume split, payables and the capex reset.

532967|2026-03.headline: Kiri Industries Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 29% YoY to Rs.241 crore, but reported EBITDA was hit by Rs.114 crore of non-cash year-end adjustments.
532967|2026-03.overview: Standalone Q4 FY26 revenue from operations rose 29% YoY to Rs.241 crore, with management citing volume recovery, better dye intermediate realisations and lower legal costs. Management said adjusted EBITDA was about Rs.35 crore, but Rs.114 crore of non-cash closing-period mark-to-market adjustments were booked, which weighed on reported EBITDA. Consolidated Q4 revenue rose 22% to Rs.251 crore and finance cost fell to Rs.8 crore from Rs.54 crore a year earlier. The DyStar award was monetised in FY26 and the copper and fertiliser project (Indo Asia Copper) moved into engineering, ordering and civil works, with commercial operations guided from April 2027 to March 2029.

financial_highlights.metric: Standalone adjusted EBITDA (Q4 FY26, post year-end adjustments)

financial_highlights.value: Rs.79 crore (~10% margin); Rs.69 crore cited later in call

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA incl. India JV (FY26)

financial_highlights.change: from Rs.54 crore in Q4 FY25

financial_highlights.metric: Share of profit from associates and JVs (FY26)
financial_highlights.value: Rs.188 crore (Rs.58 crore Lonsen Kiri, Rs.129 crore DyStar up to Q2 FY26)

segments.name: Dyes and Dyes Intermediates (standalone)
segments.commentary: Dyes Intermediates contributed 52% of revenue, Dyes 33% and Basic Chemicals 15%. Management targets over Rs.1,000 crore standalone revenue in FY27, about 20% growth.

segments.name: Lonsen Kiri JV (40% stake)
segments.commentary: Contributed Rs.58 crore to FY26 share of profit. Management said the JV generated about Rs.1,100 crore of sales and expects it to cross Rs.1,300 crore in FY27.

segments.name: Indo Asia Copper / copper and fertiliser project
segments.commentary: Pre-operative; FY26 costs were capitalised and management said it is EBITDA and PAT neutral. No copper revenue is expected in FY27.

guidance_outlook: Standalone EBITDA margin target of 10% to 15%; management said 12% for the current year would be satisfactory.
Dyes standalone revenue target above Rs.1,000 crore in FY27 (about 20% growth); JV revenue expected above Rs.1,300 crore.

Copper and fertiliser project: commercial operations to start unit by unit from April 2027, with full operation by March 2029. Earlier guidance of Rs.20,000-25,000 crore revenue was reframed as roughly Rs.40,000 crore-plus across the project at current pricing.
Capex: about Rs.4,500-5,000 crore by March 2027, another about Rs.5,000 crore in FY28, and Rs.2,000-3,000 crore by March 2029, totalling about Rs.13,000 crore including interest during moratorium.

Debt: minimal debt in FY27 (under Rs.1,000 crore); capex debt of about Rs.4,000-5,000 crore and working capital of Rs.3,000-5,000 crore in FY28, taking total debt to Rs.8,000-9,000 crore. Expected interest rate 8.5-9%, with a three-year principal moratorium.
Government incentives of about 30-35% of eligible capex over 10 years, or roughly Rs.3,000-3,500 crore a year, are in final approval stage.
Fertiliser trading under Indo Asia Fertilizer to begin from next quarter of FY27; copper trading not yet started.
No dividend for FY26 and none to be declared this year; buyback undecided.
capex_capacity: Copper rod, tube and refinery engineering under Tata Consulting Engineers; key machinery and utility packages ordered; long-lead equipment ordering ongoing.
Utilities work under way including oxygen facility and sulfuric acid plant; desalination, renewable integration and logistics facilities in planning.
Civil construction across the site about 25-30% complete. About Rs.2,500 crore already spent or committed in advances, machinery and similar.

Copper concentrate requirement for the primary line is about 1.5 million tonnes; more than 1 million tonnes is under non-binding tie-ups, with the balance targeted by next year. Rock phosphate is said to be 100% tied up.
Financial closure not yet done but said to be near; disclosure expected within a few months.
demand_pricing: Management sees China's tightening of key dye intermediates from environmental compliance and production curbs as supportive of Indian producers' realisations.
Textile customers (over 95% of dyes and chemicals customers) are extending payments, which lengthens Kiri's payables; average payable cycle quoted as 90-120 days.
Management said copper will remain import-dependent until 2030-2035 despite domestic capacity additions, with EV and AI data-centre demand rising.
Secondary copper capacity additions in India are linked to global availability of ingots and blister as exporting countries ban concentrate exports; scrap supply is also rising domestically.

qa_highlights.question: Is the April 2027 phase-one start and Rs.20,000-25,000 crore revenue outlook still valid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said operations start unit by unit from FY27-28, with Rs.40,000 crore-plus revenue cited for the project at current pricing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Rs.160 crore tax provision and net DyStar proceeds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Rs.150 crore has been paid, on the view that most of the award is a judicial capital receipt rather than taxable.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Rs.114 crore adjustment booked and will it recur?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it relates to mark-to-market on temporary parking of surplus funds in debt, equity and hybrid instruments within India, and it will not recur every quarter or year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the interest rate and moratorium on the debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Expected rate 8.5-9%, with principal repayment starting three years after drawdown and interest serviced from day one.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company pay dividends or buybacks?
qa_highlights.answer: No dividend this year and none to be declared; buyback has not been decided and cash is being retained to fund growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the backup if plant utilisation is low?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt servicing requires about 50% utilisation; below that it would be a problem, while sales are not seen as a constraint.

risks_watch: Non-cash mark-to-market adjustments of Rs.114 crore in Q4 depressed reported EBITDA; the company says they are non-recurring, but reported and adjusted figures diverge materially.
Copper concentrate tie-up is only non-binding for over 1 million tonnes against a 1.5 million tonne requirement; the balance is still open.
Debt build-up to Rs.8,000-9,000 crore in FY28 at 8.5-9% interest; servicing depends on about 50% plant utilisation, per management.
Tax treatment of the DyStar award (Rs.150 crore paid) rests on an expert legal opinion.
Receivables from textile customers are stretching and pushing out payables, which raises working capital needs.
Financial closure is still pending and the incentive approvals are awaited.
532967|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the copper and fertiliser project timeline and on dyes recovery, but defensive and repetitive when asked about the Q4 EBITDA swing, the Rs.114 crore adjustment and shareholder returns. Management declined to commit on buybacks and gave no firm date on financial closure.
key_quotes: So, the EBITDA for the year ended is 79 crores on a standalone basis and 127 crores on the consolidated basis.
And if it doesn't happen, even if the plant operations remain below 50%, still we would be able to service the interest and service the debt.
But this year, the dividend has not been declared and is not going to be declared.

532967|2026-06.headline: Kiri Industries Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 63% YoY to INR 295 crore, with PAT of INR 270 crore driven mainly by INR 284 crore other income.
532967|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew 63% YoY to INR 295 crore on realisation-led growth in dyes, dyes intermediates and basic chemicals, with standalone material margin at 31.9% versus 23.5% a year earlier. Standalone EBITDA was only INR 17 crore (5.86% margin), so PAT of INR 270 crore was largely a function of INR 284 crore other income, mainly treasury gains and inter-corporate loan interest. Consolidated revenue rose 55% to INR 312 crore with EBITDA of INR 37 crore (7.84%), and the group is substantially debt-free after repaying Claronex Holdings' borrowings. The copper and fertiliser project moved into structured construction, with financial closure still incomplete (over 50% of debt commitments received).

financial_highlights.change: vs 23.5% in Q1 FY26 and 20.4% in Q4 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated EBITDA (incl. share of associates and JVs)

financial_highlights.change: interest on inter-corporate loans plus realised and unrealised treasury gains

financial_highlights.metric: Share of profit from associates (Lonsen Kiri, 40% stake)

segments.name: Dyes, dyes intermediates and basic chemicals (standalone)
segments.commentary: Realisations rose across Reactive Dyes, Vinyl Sulphone, H-Acid and certain basic chemicals; management said H-Acid prices are INR 800-900/unit versus INR 350-400 earlier. Average capacity utilisation was about 60% last quarter, targeted at 70-75% for FY27 if markets support.

segments.name: Lonsen Kiri (associate, 40% stake)
segments.commentary: Contributed INR 21 crore to consolidated profit in Q1 FY27. Management cited a JV result of about INR 71 crore EBITDA and INR 51 crore PAT on INR 368 crore revenue, as referenced by an analyst; Kiri supplies raw materials to the JV, with 60-70% of JV raw materials sourced from Kiri.

segments.name: Copper and fertiliser integrated project (under construction)
segments.commentary: Total project capital estimated at close to INR 12,000 crore, with INR 1,400 crore deployed to date, all equity so far. Downstream copper tube, rod and refinery phases are planned for Q1 FY28, FY28 and Q3 FY29 respectively.

guidance_outlook: Copper tube plant (35 KT) expected operational June 2027; 2.25 lakh tonne CCR rod plant (8 mm) expected August-September 2027, both stable by January 2028, using imported Japanese LME-grade cathodes.
Part refinery of 1.75 lakh tonnes (anode to cathode) targeted around January 2028, with scrap melting furnace by December 2027-January 2028.
Copper foil trial production targeted around March 2028 (10 KT Phase 1, 40 KT ambition under ECMS scheme); smelter, sulphuric acid plant and fertiliser balance of plant expected Q1 2029.
First copper revenue expected around end Q1 FY28 (May-June 2027); majority of copper operating revenue expected in FY30.
Management said the earlier FY28 revenue guidance of INR 20,000-25,000 crore no longer holds; the numbers are dynamic and depend on vendor timelines.
Debt repayment expected to start in 2029 given moratorium; cash flow expected to ramp stepwise over FY28-FY30.
No dividend declared; no Board decision yet, per management.
capex_capacity: Total copper project capital estimated at close to INR 12,000 crore, excluding additional infrastructure spend; outflow expected over the next two years.
Financial closure incomplete; more than 50% of debt commitments received, balance in process, with complete closure hoped within a few months.
Copper concentrate: MoUs of about 1 million tonnes secured against about 1.5 million tonnes needed at full utilisation; firm contracts typically converted around October each year.
Captive jetty (for bulk imports of copper concentrate, phosphate and ammonia), desalination facility, raw material conveying system and power infrastructure in progress; site near Pipavav Port.
MCB Copper-Gold mine: development not started; 70% off-take structured for Kiri, but Celsius is contesting the off-take in court.
demand_pricing: Reactive Dyes, Vinyl Sulphone, H-Acid and certain basic chemical prices strengthened in Q1 on tighter global supply and Chinese environmental compliance measures.
Demand is mixed across product categories; input costs rose with crude oil-linked raw materials, with pass-through supporting margins.

Management said existing H-Acid and Vinyl Sulphone capacity could drive about INR 2,000 crore of dyes revenue at 75-80% utilisation if current prices hold, versus about INR 1,200 crore cited as the current base.
Copper: management sees sales as not a constraint because India consumes about 1.8 million tonnes a year with about two-thirds imported; customer quality approvals still required.
Management said sustaining margins depends on passing through input cost movements.

qa_highlights.question: Will the earlier FY28 revenue guidance of INR 20,000-25,000 crore still hold given staggered tube and rod commissioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR 20,000-25,000 crore FY28 figure does not hold; projections are moving with vendor delivery timelines. It added that sales are not a constraint since the output would substitute imports.

qa_highlights.question: When will copper revenue start and when will it be fully ramped?
qa_highlights.answer: First copper revenue expected around May-June 2027 (Q1 FY28), with commercial operations from Q2 FY28; majority of operating revenue expected in FY30.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Kiri's standalone profitability low when Lonsen Kiri earns strong margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Kiri supplies raw materials to the JV, which captures finished-product margins; the JV also makes products Kiri does not, so the combined value chain should be assessed. Lonsen Kiri is operated by Kiri management with no plan to replicate its products in Kiri.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a plan to raise equity to reduce debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said equity dilution is a plan B option with investor interest tested, but the Board prefers deferred dilution after execution to capture more value. Debt repayment begins in 2029 due to moratorium.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the MCB Copper-Gold mine and the off-take?
qa_highlights.answer: Development has not started; design complete. Shareholder disputes and Celsius litigation are ongoing and sub judice, so management declined to speculate and said Kiri remains a lender.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a stake sale or MMCI interest?
qa_highlights.answer: No current talks on a 40% stake sale in Lonsen Kiri. Management said it would be 100% interested in an MMCI mine stake, subject to the litigation outcome.

risks_watch: Copper project timing: first copper revenue targeted May-June 2027 and tube/rod plants by June and August-September 2027, but management withdrew the INR 20,000-25,000 crore FY28 revenue guidance and said timelines depend on vendor delivery schedules.

Financing: financial closure is incomplete (over 50% of debt commitments received); equity dilution is a fallback option that management says has been tested but is deferred. Debt repayment starts in 2029 after moratorium.

Earnings quality: standalone PAT of INR 270 crore rests mainly on INR 284 crore other income (treasury gains and inter-corporate loan interest), while standalone EBITDA was only INR 17 crore. Track how much of other income recurs.

Raw material security: MoUs for about 1 million tonnes of copper concentrate against about 1.5 million tonnes needed at full utilisation; firm contracts are typically converted around October each year.
MCB Copper-Gold mine: development not started, 70% off-take structured for Kiri, but Celsius is contesting it in court; management declined to speculate on the outcome.

Dyes pricing and utilisation: margin sustainability depends on passing through crude-linked input costs; utilisation was about 60% last quarter with a 70-75% FY27 target conditional on market support.
key_quotes: So, that INR 20,000 crore-INR 25,000 crore of revenue in 2027-2028 doesn't hold. Let me first clarify that.
A complete financial closure has not been achieved yet. We are there on the debt raising. More than 50% commitments have been received.
But we continue to provide our commitment to the project. We continue to support the project.

On dividends and equity dilution it stayed noncommittal, with the Board keeping capital for growth.

532976|2026-06.headline: Jai Balaji Q1 FY27 revenue rose 24% YoY to INR1,683 crore; adjusted EBITDA up 46% to INR154 crore, PAT up 21% to INR85 crore.
532976|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 24% YoY to INR1,683 crore, with adjusted EBITDA up 46% to INR154 crore (about 9% margin) and PAT up 21% to INR85 crore (about 5% margin), attributed to price normalisation and operational efficiency. Ferroalloy and pig iron realisations rose sharply YoY, while DI pipe demand stayed subdued on slow government ordering and fund releases. Management declined to give volume or EBITDA guidance, citing uncertainty, but said pipe prices are at the bottom and cannot fall further. Expansion capex was revised up to INR1,112 crore from about INR1,000 crore, with completion expected by Q3 FY27 and the balance by end-2026.

segments.name: Pig iron
segments.commentary: About 19% of revenue; realisations up 16% YoY.

segments.commentary: About 14.8% of revenue. Management expects West Bengal sales to rise to 50-70% of TMT volume from 15-20% previously.

segments.commentary: Sponge iron 7.4%, billets 3.5%, coke about 7%, scrap and fines about 1% of revenue. Sponge iron and billet realisations were broadly stable.

Ferroalloy demand described as strong with repeat orders; management said 80-85% capacity is utilised.

qa_highlights.answer: Competition will persist until industry utilisation reaches 65-70%. Management said pipe prices are at rock bottom and Q1 pipe margins were similar to pig iron margins.

qa_highlights.answer: No. Management called pipe EBITDA guidance speculative given the 25-30% price fall and said it would reassess next quarter.

532977|2026-03.headline: Bajaj Auto Q4 FY26 revenue rose 32% to INR16,006 crores with EBITDA of INR3,323 crores at 20.8%, but management flags April-onward commodity inflation of 3.5-4% of revenue.
532977|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 set records for revenue, EBITDA and volumes, with 2W, 3W and exports each growing about 20% in volume and 30% in revenue. Margins held at 20.8% helped by a stronger rupee (realised INR90.6/USD vs INR86.5 a year ago), richer mix and operating leverage, offsetting net commodity inflation of about 40 bps and absorbed PM E-DRIVE subsidy loss on electric 3-wheelers. Management guided to a sharply weaker operating backdrop from April: domestic motorcycle growth seen at 7-9% near term versus about 20% in Q4, plus 10-15% supply loss, and commodity inflation of 3.5-4% of revenue, about 40% of which has been priced in so far. The board also approved a 100% payout of FY26 profit (dividend INR150/share plus a INR5,633 crore buyback at INR12,000/share).

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Crossed 6 lakh units for second straight quarter, +25% YoY, highest-ever quarterly export revenue; FY26 revenue USD2.2 billion (record). KTM exports from India ~17,500 units in Q4 vs near nil a year ago; Nigeria back above 1 lakh units in Q4 but FY26 flat vs FY25.

segments.name: Domestic motorcycles (2W)
segments.commentary: Industry grew ~11% in FY26 and ~20% in Q4. Bajaj 150cc+ share recovering; 10 Pulsar variants/upgrades launched Oct-Mar now 50% of sales. Q4 KTM+Triumph domestic volumes ~43,000 units, +43% YoY (record).

segments.name: Electric (2W + 3W)
segments.commentary: Now ~20%+ of domestic revenue with double-digit EBITDA margin for last two quarters; Chetak EBITDA-neutral. Chetak Q4 retails above 1 lakh (record), March above 50,000; share ~23%, up 170 bps QoQ. FY26 Chetak revenue INR4,000 crores, over 5 lakh units.

segments.name: 3-wheelers
segments.commentary: Electric 3W No.1 in registrations through Q4 and April; industry 3W growth 25%+ in Q4 and April. Commercial vehicles crossed 5 lakh units in FY26; Q4 volumes +28% YoY; CNG share close to 90%.

segments.name: Spares
segments.commentary: Sales INR1,700+ crores, +16% growth, record EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Bajaj Auto Credit (BACL)
segments.commentary: AUM nearly INR19,000 crores (roughly doubled); FY26 PAT INR665 crores vs INR58 crores; CRAR 19.5%; ROE ~23%; 1.8 million customers.

guidance_outlook: Domestic motorcycle industry growth estimated at 7-9% in the near term (based on April outcomes), versus about 20% in Q4; growth expected mainly from 125cc+ and 150cc+ segments, which management expects to grow about twice the industry rate.
Exports targeted at 2.2 lakh units per month in Q1 FY27 (from 2.0 lakh), with Gulf loss of about 5,000-6,000 units per month.
Material commodity cost inflation of about 3.5-4% of revenue (Q1 vs Q4); about 40% offset by pricing so far; management says the next price action may be the last, if needed.
Supply constraints (LPG, manpower, logistics) impaired April serviceability by 10-15%; expected to ease over time.

Buyback of INR5,633 crores at INR12,000/share needs shareholder approval; process expected to conclude by end-July with payout around second week of July; final dividend INR150/share (INR4,192 crores) after July AGM.
KTM turnaround results expected to show up in the latter part of 2026. KTM and BMAG to move to quarterly reporting with one-quarter lag.
New Pulsar 125cc and 150cc+ launches targeted from July.
capex_capacity: Chetak capacity now 50,000 units per month; management expects to max it out and says a substantive capacity increase is needed, with plan to be announced later.
Brazil plant capacity ~60,000 units per annum (about 50,000 usable), expected to be fully used within 12 months; further expansion considered by mid-year for FY27-28.
FY26 capex about INR500 crores, split equally between ICE and EV; over INR2,300 crores invested in BACL and BAIH BV.
Larger 3-wheeler capacity (7 and 9 series) is becoming a constraint; expansion underway.
demand_pricing: Price hikes effective 1 April across products; management says 30-40% of the GST-cut benefit could be rolled back, weighing on demand.
Realisation of USD/INR around 94-95 currently vs INR90.6 average in Q4; company is unhedged and realises at market.
Commodity moves: noble metals up 35-45%, aluminium up 35-45%, copper ~20%, steel ~15% in the current quarter.
Nigeria fuel prices up about 30%; Nigeria running at 35,000+ units per month for motorcycles plus 5,000+ 3W.
Brazil at 5th position in share in April; Latam 11 consecutive quarters of growth; Mexico and FTA outlook cited as upside.
Competitive pressure: management says 125cc bikes from China are a competitive threat in export markets.

qa_highlights.question: How has the price hike affected demand, and are exports seeing similar effects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said motorcycle industry growth fell from Q4 to April and that 30-40% of the GST benefit may roll back. Upper-half and 150cc+ demand remains strong, while Latam and Nigeria are healthy.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company hedged on currency?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Dinesh Thapar said the company is not hedged and realises at market rates.

qa_highlights.question: Will exports outgrow domestic volumes in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not forecast the split but said exports are on a strong footing, targeting above 2 lakh units per month in Q1, and that the 150cc+ domestic segment is also performing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan to lift Chetak beyond the ~30,000/month run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is 50,000 units per month and management expects to max it; a larger capacity expansion is under study and will be discussed later.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 125cc affordable motorcycle launch this year, and what is the PLI amount?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to name a model but said new 125cc and 150cc+ Pulsar launches are coming from July. CFO said PLI for FY26 is about INR900 crores, still being aggregated.

qa_highlights.question: How much margin pressure remains from the 3.5-4% commodity inflation, and what is the margin tolerance?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the aim is to hold margins at steady state, that the estimate has been refreshed three times in four weeks, and that pricing may be the last lever, with cost savings and discretionary spend cuts used first. Currency at INR94-95 is a partial cushion.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 7-9% industry outlook for the next few months or the full year, and is 3-wheeler growth structural?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 7-9% covers the next few months, not the full year, with a base effect in H2. It said 3W industry growth is 25%+ and structural, driven by non-metro mobility, shared ticketing and larger 3W formats.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving other operating income, and what are the milestones for the buyback?
qa_highlights.answer: Other operating income is driven by PLI on electric scale-up, export incentives and BGO oils royalty. Buyback needs shareholder approval because it exceeds 10% of free reserves (about INR3,500 crores); process expected to finish by end-July, with payout around the second week of July.

risks_watch: Commodity inflation of 3.5-4% of revenue in Q1 and possibly more; pricing may be exhausted after the next round; figures are reviewed monthly.
Domestic motorcycle growth could slow to 7-9% as GST benefit rolls back, with a base effect in H2.
Supply constraints of 10-15% (LPG, manpower, logistics) and Middle East disruption (Gulf loss about 5,000-6,000 units per month).

Buyback of INR5,633 crores needs shareholder approval; cash-flow and approval timing to monitor.
Management's rupee tailwind (INR94-95) is unhedged and could reverse.

532977|2026-06.headline: Bajaj Auto Q1 FY27 revenue crossed INR17,000 crore (INR17,244 cr, +37% YoY) with EBITDA of INR3,596 cr at 20.9% margin despite ~4.5% commodity inflation.
532977|2026-06.overview: Standalone volumes hit a record over 1.4 million units (+29% YoY) and PAT was a tad under INR3,000 crore (+42% YoY), with EBITDA margin up 10 bps QoQ and 110 bps YoY. Management said ransomware, LPG curtailment, West Asia logistics issues and labour shortages cost about 10% of volume, and that the company was tracking above 1.5 million units before these disruptions. Commodity inflation of about 4.5% of revenue was only about half offset by pricing, with the balance absorbed by a weaker rupee (realised USD-INR 94.4 vs 85.6 a year ago), mix and discretionary cost cuts. Management flagged broader cost inflation (proprietary parts, electronics, logistics, labour, energy) that Q2 will reflect more fully, and declined to quantify it.

segments.commentary: EV two- and three-wheelers at ~30% of domestic revenue with double-digit EBITDA; Chetak volumes +65% YoY (industry ~+70%), first EBITDA-positive quarter; EV scooter capacity ~50,000 units/month, targeting ~60,000 near term.

segments.name: Three-wheelers (ICE and e-autos)
segments.commentary: ICE three-wheeler share ~70%; e-autos doubled and are 44% of L5 segment; Q1 record billings and retail; capacity constraints limited sales of some models.

guidance_outlook: Exports to move beyond 250,000 units per month from this quarter onward (was ~200,000 a few quarters ago).
Capacity expansion of ~25%, from ~7 million to 9 million+ units per annum over the medium term, focused on EVs (two- and three-wheeler), high-end motorcycles and wide-body three-wheelers.

capex_capacity: Current capacity ~7 million units per annum across businesses, expanding to 9 million+ units in the medium term (work already started).
EV two-wheeler (Chetak) capacity ~50,000 units/month, expected to rise to ~60,000 through productivity gains with vendors.

qa_highlights.question: Why are sub-125cc motorcycles weak despite GST cut, and is there a shift from ICE to EV?

qa_highlights.question: What are EV capacity plans and where is EV profitability?

532978|2026-06.headline: Bajaj Finserv Q1 FY27 consolidated PAT rose 18% to INR 6,297 crore on total income up 19% to INR 42,037 crore.
532978|2026-06.overview: Consolidated total income grew 19% to INR 42,037 crore and PAT grew 18% to INR 6,297 crore, per management. Lending subsidiaries (Bajaj Finance, Bajaj Housing) posted strong growth, with Bajaj Finance PAT up about 27.6%. Insurance profits fell sharply as lower realised capital gains and the GST impact on Life acquisition costs hit reported earnings, while Bajaj General's combined ratio rose to about 104.7% on Ind AS-basis reporting. Management also announced approval to set up a reinsurance company.

segments.name: Bajaj General Insurance
segments.commentary: GWP up 11.3% to INR 5,789 crore, in line with industry GDPI of 11.1%; ex-crop and government health, GWP grew about 10% vs industry about 12%, with motor tactically reduced. Underwriting loss about INR 130 crore vs INR 116 crore; annualised ROE 17.3% ex-surplus capital at 200% solvency.

segments.name: Bajaj Life Insurance
segments.commentary: Retail protection 12% of retail business, growing 60% YoY; group protection up 95%. GWP up 35% on renewal premium growth of about 18%; persistency dipped in certain cohorts. Solvency 285%. AUM INR 1,43,744 crore, up almost 10%.

segments.name: Bajaj Finance and Bajaj Housing Finance
segments.commentary: Bajaj Finance new loans up 20% to 1.61 crore; GNPA 0.96%, NNPA 0.39%, CRAR 20.9%, opex to NTI 33.4%. Bajaj Housing AUM up 24%, GNPA 0.29%, NNPA 0.12%, CRAR 21.59%, PAT up 23% to INR 715 crore.

segments.name: Bajaj Finserv Direct (Bajaj Markets)
segments.commentary: Bajaj Markets disbursement about INR 2,269 crore (vs INR 1,209 crore last year); operating revenue INR 107 crore, up 32%, including about INR 15 crore trail revenue; 103 unique partners. Management targets breakeven in Q3 or Q4 FY27 on a quarterly basis.

segments.name: Bajaj Finserv Health
segments.commentary: About 6 million healthcare transactions vs 5.6 million last year, but revenue declined slightly due to partnership restructuring under RBI NBFC business-conduct rules. Provider network of about 1.3 lakh doctors, 15,000+ hospitals, about 7,000 lab touch points. Breakeven targeted for Q3 or Q4 FY28.

segments.name: Bajaj Asset Management
segments.commentary: AUM INR 31,444 crore, up 26%, 26th-ranked MF company; equity mix 63%; SIP book up 66% and SIP folios up 69%. Management targets INR 1 lakh crore AUM in about three years as path to profitability.

guidance_outlook: Bajaj Finserv Direct expected to break even on a quarterly basis in Q3 or Q4 FY27 and on a full-year basis in FY28.
Bajaj Finserv Health expected to break even in Q3 or Q4 FY28, full-year breakeven the year after.
Bajaj Finance expects opex to NTI to improve by about 25 to 40 bps in FY27.
Bajaj General expects reported combined ratio to remain best in industry despite pricing pressure; Ind AS transition from 1 April 2027 expected to release large discounting benefit on TP liabilities.
Capital needs: Health about INR 200-300 crore over next 6 quarters; AMC modest; largest chunk to ALTs and reinsurance company (phase 1 domestic, phase 2 international after 3-year rating process).
capex_capacity: Board approved setting up a reinsurance company; regulatory approvals to be sought, capital not yet quantified.
Alternate investments business commenced with PMS launch; real estate and AI AIF launches expected in the coming quarter.
Insurance companies move to Ind AS from 1 April 2027 after IRDAI forbearance; acquisition costs to be amortised rather than upfronted.
Bajaj General paid high dividend and bought back shares in prior quarter, reducing capital by about INR 3,515 crore.
demand_pricing: Industry general insurance soft pricing; management says Bajaj General combined ratio deterioration is about 1 pp vs 5% or more at peers, and it outperforms market by 16-18%.
Bajaj General reduced motor exposure tactically due to elevated pricing pressure; motor own damage loss ratios rising industry-wide.
Crop business tenders expected to be higher than last year; government health contract 2+1 with lives covered likely lower than last year's base.
Life product mix: ULIP about 45%, par 22-25%, non-par plus annuity 22-25%, retail protection 12%; 34% of customers onboarded with term plans and 22% of NOPs with riders.
Bajaj Markets: 50-plus lenders on platform; 35 products; personal loans lead, gold and home loans growing fast.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of Supreme Court ruling on motor third-party compensation for homemakers and reserving?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR 30,000 figure may not apply; TP ultimate loss ratios assumed are conservative and build in buffer, and homemaker cases are very few. Industry is seeking a TP price hike. GIC has filed a review petition.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of monsoon and natural catastrophes on motor, commercial and crop; road to profitability for subsidiaries?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said soft market means pricing below average, but Bajaj General's CR deterioration is only about 1 pp. Treaties are robust and NATCAT reserves are maintained. Breakeven timelines: Finserv Direct Q3/Q4 FY27, Health Q3/Q4 FY28, AMC targeting INR 1 lakh crore AUM in 3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did group protection grow nearly 100%, and how do annuity and non-par relate; how is GST impact absorbed?
qa_highlights.answer: Tarun Chugh said MFI revival and 20+ new partners added in 15 months drove growth; annuity and non-par share a chassis, non-par was reconfigured after persistency hit. Margin expansion came from riders at same commission, product mix and cost savings under Bajaj Life 2.0.

qa_highlights.question: Trajectory of crop and government health tender businesses?
qa_highlights.answer: Tapan Singhel said crop tenders this year would exceed last year; government health is a 2+1 contract so renewal is automatic, though base may be somewhat lower than last year.

qa_highlights.question: Reinsurance capital requirement?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramandeep Sahni said the project is at drawing-board stage; phase 1 domestic needs limited capital, phase 2 international after about 3-year ratings process needs more; not yet quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Ind AS transition impact and rider attachment?
qa_highlights.answer: Effective date 1 April 2027 after one-year forbearance. Key impacts: acquisition cost amortisation for both insurers; GI TP liabilities discounting could release large amount; onerous contract recognition could benefit GI. Riders attached to 22% of NOPs.

qa_highlights.question: Motor own damage loss ratio drivers and FY27 strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Avais Karmali said the rise is industry-wide and management is slowing motor on risk selection; no segment-level breakdown given, as pricing is micro-segmented geography-wise.

risks_watch: Soft general insurance pricing and monsoon/NATCAT losses could raise industry loss ratios and pressure Bajaj General margins.
Ind AS transition from 1 April 2027 and regulatory clarifications on onerous contracts and discounting remain open; quantification pending.
Supreme Court motor TP homemaker ruling; GIC review petition pending; TP price hike still awaited.
Life persistency dips in certain cohorts; GST impact on margins; lower realised capital gains depressed profit.
Bajaj Finserv Direct and Health breakeven timelines depend on partner restructuring under RBI digital lending and NBFC rules.

rows.why: Operating revenue INR 107 crore (+32%) and disbursement INR 2,269 crore (vs INR 1,209 crore) with management 'certain' of quarterly breakeven in Q3 or Q4 FY27.

532993|2026-03.headline: Sejal Glass Q4 FY26 consolidated income rose over 72% YoY to INR 116.85 crores, with EBITDA margin at 17.5% and PAT at INR 11.42 crores.
532993|2026-03.overview: Management reported strong Q4 and FY26 consolidated growth, with income crossing INR 400 crores for the year and margins expanding on product mix and operating leverage from integrated acquired facilities. The UAE business, over 70% of revenue, faces a regional slowdown and supply-chain disruption, though management guided to stable monthly run-rates of AED 10.2-10.5 million and an order book of about AED 60 million. India is being scaled up through the Glasstech acquisition, which reached EBITDA breakeven in the last month of FY26. Management guided FY27 consolidated revenue of about INR 500 crores and a 17.5-18% EBITDA margin, with new value-added products expected to contribute 5-7% of revenue this year.

segments.name: UAE business
segments.commentary: Monthly run-rate of AED 10.2-10.5 million; management expects about AED 31 million in Q1 FY27 and AED 35 million in Q2 if conditions improve. Q1 revenue guided to be in line with Q4. Over 70% of group revenue comes from UAE.

segments.name: India - Silvassa (existing)
segments.commentary: Capacity utilisation: tempering 64%, IG 30%, lamination 87%. Silvassa alone earns above 17-18% EBITDA margin. FY27 Silvassa revenue expected around INR 90 crores.

segments.name: India - Glasstech (Taloja and Erode)
segments.commentary: Utilisation: Taloja tempering 33%, IG 21%, lamination 8%; Erode tempering 13%, IG 3%. Glasstech FY26 revenue about INR 40 crores (post-acquisition operations from May/June 2025). Reached EBITDA breakeven in the last month; expects at least 10% EBITDA margin in Q1 FY27. FY27 expectation about INR 110 crores.

segments.name: New products (railway, fire, bullet-proof, digital, decorative)
segments.commentary: Railway tenders started (level 1 and level 2 orders won; bidding for Vande Bharat and AC coaches). Expected to be 2-3% of revenue from railway. Fire-rated glass (signed with Spain partner), standard and digital products to hit market in Q3 FY27; all new products 5-7% of FY27 revenue, 15-20% next year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue target of about INR 500 crores (about 25% growth), with India about 40% (about INR 200 crores) and UAE about 60%.
Management said UAE revenue may grow about 20% in FY27 if the current situation holds; growth above 40% is possible if UAE improves.
FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin guided at 17.5-18%; UAE facade business could weigh about 1% on consolidated margin; raw material pass-through of 80-90% of cost increases expected.
India EBITDA margin targeted at about 15% for FY27.
India Q1 FY27 revenue expected to grow about 20% QoQ; India/UAE mix targeted at 60:40 this year and 50:50 thereafter.
Management expects no cash tax outgo in India for the next two years.
Glass prices rose about 7-8% in the last two months due to energy/gas cost; company says increases are passed through to customers.
Warrant call (about 4 lakh warrants, 75% balance) expected within 18 months, to be used for acquisitions.
capex_capacity: UAE: machines already ordered but delayed by one quarter due to geopolitical issues; expected installation in Q2 or Q3 FY27, funded by a mix of internal accruals and local/UAE bank debt.
Silvassa targets: tempering about 75%, IG above 50%, lamination 90-95% in FY27.
Taloja and Erode combined targets: tempering above 50%, IG and lamination together about 30%.
Second acquisition in India is under due diligence; management said it will take some time.
Taloja operations began June 2025 and Erode July 2025 after overhauling, re-engineering and labour set-up (about two quarters).
demand_pricing: UAE order book about AED 60 million; management said slowdown in real estate, with supply-chain disruption, but orders are in pipeline.
UAE strategy shifting toward Africa and other GCC markets; first European order won from India this quarter.
Demand drivers cited: premium and mid-income housing, office and data-centre leasing, infrastructure (airports, metro, rail, healthcare), and energy-efficiency rules favouring IG and laminated glass.
Segment shift in India from plain tempered glass to laminated and IG glass, driven by safety norms and architect specifications; India is about 60% plain tempered.
Saint-Gobain collaboration gives price advantage of about 4-5% via credit notes on project orders, plus special sizes that reduce wastage.
Non-real-estate (OEM) business is small but carries better margins; Glasstech gross margins similar to consolidated.

qa_highlights.question: What is the UAE outlook, Q1 run-rate and margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the UAE order book is about AED 60 million and monthly turnover is AED 10.2-10.5 million; Q1 could reach about AED 31 million and Q2 AED 35 million. Raw material cost increases are about 80-90% passed on; margin impact about 1-1.5% at EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Are UAE debtors being paid on time?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said all payments and PDCs are being honoured on due dates, no customer has extended terms, and there are zero bad debts or delays so far.

qa_highlights.question: Why does India revenue look lower after including Glasstech?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said India ex-Glasstech was INR 63 crores in FY26; Glasstech's pre-acquisition figure included trading revenue, and consolidation, re-engineering and overhauling took about two quarters. Glasstech FY26 revenue was about INR 40 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the consolidated debt and debt reduction plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated debt is about INR 138 crores, of which about INR 70 crores is promoter-group funding and the rest is bank term loans on schedule. Some promoter loans were repaid in Q3 FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What is the gross margin path for standalone and consolidated?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated gross margins are better because UAE sales are mainly IG and laminated glass with no plain tempered glass. India gross margin is expected to improve as mix shifts, with COGS falling toward 61%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Saint-Gobain benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Price advantage of about 4-5% through credit notes on project orders, plus special sizes and sales support from Saint-Gobain's pan-India team.

risks_watch: UAE real estate slowdown and supply-chain disruption; a worsening situation could reduce margins beyond the guided 1-1.5% impact.
Glasstech utilisation remains low (tempering 13-33%, lamination 8%); FY27 INR 110 crore target depends on ramp-up.
