532993|2026-06.headline: Sejal Glass Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue INR117.95 crore, up 52.88% YoY; management guides FY27 revenue growth of minimum 25%, up to 40%.
532993|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 52.88% YoY to INR117.95 crore, with India up 67.03% to INR36.43 crore and UAE up 47.31% to INR81.52 crore. Consolidated EBITDA grew over 44% YoY to INR18 crore and PAT grew over 63% YoY to INR7.22 crore. Management cited a one-time-like INR1 crore people-cost hit from appraisals and a Taloja labour union agreement, plus UAE logistics and fuel-related cost increases, as drags on Q1 margin. Guidance was framed as a 25% minimum and up to 40% revenue growth for FY27, with EBITDA margin up about 1% and PAT margin of 9-10% targeted, mainly from Q3-Q4.

segments.name: UAE
segments.commentary: Revenue INR81.52 crore, up 47.31% YoY; utilisation ~71% on tempering base line, with 95% of UAE output sold locally and in GCC, Africa emerging. Order book about AED70-72 million.

segments.name: Railway / fire-safety / bulletproof verticals
segments.commentary: Railway was under 1% of Q1 revenue; fire-rated glass production to start Q3 FY27. Management targets 10% of revenue from these verticals next year, including railway.

FY27 EBITDA margin to improve by about 1% over upcoming quarters; PAT margin target of around 9% (CFO) to 9-10% (promoter) for FY27, mainly in Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated EBITDA up about 1% and PAT around 9%; order book referenced as India >INR50 crore and UAE ~AED70 million. Promoter said 25% is minimum growth, up to 40% upside, after an earlier TV comment of 50%.

qa_highlights.question: Current and peak capacity utilisation by plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Silvassa ~77%, Taloja ~55%, Erode ~15%, UAE ~71%. Targets: Silvassa 85-90% by year end, Taloja 75%, Erode 25-30%, UAE 85%.

qa_highlights.question: What caused the Q1 margin squeeze?
qa_highlights.answer: Appraisal and yearly increments plus a Taloja labour union agreement added about INR1 crore people cost; UAE logistics hit by June war disruption; raw material costs up about 1% due to diesel and energy surcharge.

qa_highlights.question: Why has UAE monthly sales stayed near AED10-10.5 million despite a AED60-70 million order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Tailor-made orders are released in size only when end customers are ready, so production timing lags order inflow. July UAE revenue reached AED11.87 million.

qa_highlights.question: How is the UAE capex funded and what are FY28 expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Funded from internal accruals plus a proposed ~AED7 million long-term bank loan. FY28 revenue growth expected at least 25%, too early for margin guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Railway and new vertical contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Railway under 1% of Q1 revenue; target 10% of revenue from railway, fire-safety and related verticals next year. Approved vendor for Kapurthala, Raebareli and Chennai railway facilities.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA growth lag revenue growth in FY26?

qa_highlights.question: Why did Cavite Biofuels post high losses in a peak season?

qa_highlights.question: Status of INR300 crore FGD retention money expected in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: More than INR200 crore realised; INR165 crore remains, with about one-third expected in June and the rest by August.

qa_highlights.question: What is the breakdown of other income and forex in consolidated results?
qa_highlights.answer: Forex fluctuation of INR103 crore in other income, of which about INR50 crore relates to Isgec Investments Pte Ltd (Singapore) and is classified in other expenses per accounting standards.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation (steel forgings, castings, chemicals, imports) and geopolitical disruption affecting logistics and margins; management says it is absorbing costs for now.

Philippines business: unsold, classified as continuing operations; sale timing uncertain and a prior deal fell through when the buyer could not pay. Ongoing depreciation of about INR150 crore for Cavite Biofuels in FY27.
Cancelled orders of INR550 crore in FY26 and FY26 revenue shortfall versus 7-8% guidance.
Negative net worth at Isgec Investments Pte Ltd and capital deficiency at Bioeq Energy Holding; funded via group shareholder loans.
Export receivables and currency risk in Africa and Southeast Asia; company says no significant money has been stuck with African customers.
Watch Q1 FY27: FGD retention collection (INR165 crore), Cavite utilisation ramp, order inflow after INR1,400 crore in April-May, and projects margin progress toward 5.5%.
533033|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the manufacturing margin range and FY27 growth, but candid that FY26 missed guidance and that the Philippines accounting and sale are uncertain. Management was evasive on Cavite Biofuels EBITDA and on sale price and timing, citing accounting constraints and geopolitical fluidity.
key_quotes: I want to be transparent about its composition. About INR80 crores of the PBT is from items related to the Philippines business.
So we are reasonably confident that 12% to 13% is going to be maintained.
We should be closer to 5.5% for FY27.
So we normally work with confirmed letters of credit. And these are denominated in dollars or euros, and we take forward covers against them.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Projects EBIT margin guided to about 5.5% in FY27 from 4.58% in FY26 on older projects closing and better-margin shorter orders; manufacturing held at 12-13% (12.46% FY26) despite input cost inflation.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Capacity additions are under construction across most manufacturing product lines and described as on schedule, with some new capacity expected to come online in FY27 and add depreciation; quantum not disclosed, and capacity was not quantified.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 standalone revenue guided up 10-12% with about INR500 crore from manufacturing and 3-4% from projects, backed by ~INR7,000 crore opening order book and INR1,400 crore of orders booked in April-May 2026.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is only 70% per the call, well below the 80%+ threshold, so no broad new-plant case; only a small INR25 crore Muzaffarnagar expansion was approved on 1 June 2026, and FY26 capex was INR153 crore.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Export order book about INR1,450 crore and INR1,400 crore of orders in April-May 2026 support the FY27 10-12% guide, but FY26 revenue of INR5,229 crore missed the 7-8% guidance, so an upgrade is conditional on order conversion.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY26 missed the 7-8% revenue guide (actual 4.2%), INR550 crore of orders were cancelled, and input cost inflation in steel forgings and castings is being absorbed through contingencies and back-to-back orders.

rows.label: Cavite Biofuels ramp to 85-90% utilisation
rows.why: Plant at 70-75% utilisation now, targeted 85-90% for the rest of the year barring 1-1.5 months of heavy rain; FY26 operating loss ~INR26 crore, and FY27 depreciation seen near INR150 crore.

rows.label: Philippines business sale
rows.why: Buyer being sought but no specific party in advanced talks and no letter of intent; a prior deal fell through when the buyer could not pay.

rows.label: FGD retention money collection
rows.why: INR165 crore of the INR300 crore FGD retention remains outstanding, with about one-third expected in June and the rest by August.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 12-13% manufacturing margin and 10-12% FY27 growth, but candid that FY26 missed guidance, and evasive on Cavite Biofuels EBITDA, sale price and timing; analysts probed the margin split and Philippines losses.

533033|2026-06.headline: ISGEC Q1 FY27 standalone total income up 51% to INR 1,585 crore, but PBT up only 10% to INR 123 crore; FY27 standalone revenue guided up 10-12%.
533033|2026-06.overview: Standalone total income rose 51% YoY to INR 1,585 crore and EBIT grew 15% to INR 157 crore, with PBT up 10% to INR 123 crore as Q1 FY26 had high forex-driven other income. Manufacturing EBIT margin was 12% and projects EBIT margin 5.25%. Consolidated PBT was INR 53 crore, held back by an INR 83 crore loss at the Philippines ethanol plant, which ran at about 65-70% utilisation. Management kept FY27 standalone revenue growth guidance at 10-12% and said it is conservative, citing carry-forward of order execution into FY28.

financial_highlights.change: about 45% higher vs INR 1,374 crore in Q1 FY26
includes INR 37 crore depreciation, INR 20 crore interest, INR 10 crore forex
vs INR 381 crore at 31 Mar 2026 and INR 408 crore at 30 Jun 2025
down INR 170 crore QoQ from INR 476 crore; INR 832 crore a year earlier

segments.name: Industrial Projects (standalone)
segments.commentary: Income up on improved execution per schedule; management expects roughly INR 1,000 crore per quarter in Q2 FY27 and projects EBIT margin of 5-6% for FY27. Export orders booked in Africa and Latin America.

segments.name: Manufacturing (standalone)
segments.commentary: Income lifted by dispatch of a roughly INR 130 crore US order that had been on hold; EBIT margin 12%, guided 12-13%. Steady-state consolidated manufacturing revenue guided at INR 750 crore plus per quarter.

segments.name: Isgec Hitachi Zosen
segments.commentary: Orders in hand INR 889 crore. FY26 revenue about INR 670 crore; management expects about 10% growth in revenue and profit in FY27.

segments.name: Saraswati Sugar Mills
segments.commentary: Revenue down due to lower cane availability last season (untimely rain); cane availability improvement steps under way for next season.

segments.name: Philippines ethanol (CBPI)
segments.commentary: Q1 loss INR 83 crore at about 65-70% utilisation; crushed about 84,000 tonnes of cane, sold over 8 million litres of ethanol. Management targets about 90% utilisation by December and a much lower loss in Q2.

segments.name: Eagle Press and Isgec Titan Metal
segments.commentary: Eagle Press about INR 150 crore a year; Isgec Titan Metal expected at about INR 150 crore in FY27 vs INR 102 crore in FY26.

guidance_outlook: FY27 standalone revenue growth guided at 10-12%; management says the figure is conservative with a bias to realism.
Manufacturing EBIT margin guided at 12-13% for FY27; projects EBIT margin guided to improve slightly within 5-6%.
Isgec Hitachi Zosen revenue and profit guided about 10% higher than FY26.
Manufacturing capacity expansion (approved INR 502 crore) to add up to about INR 1,200 crore annual revenue when fully complete; main benefit from FY28-29.

Bhartauli machine-building phase 1 (INR 73 crore) to complete in early September 2026, with about INR 225 crore annual revenue potential; billing expected only from Q1 FY28 as work-in-progress builds first.
Dahej skids and modules facility expected to complete around 31 May 2027.
Philippines ethanol depreciation expected about INR 95 crore in FY27 (WDV method); interest about INR 19-20 crore per quarter.
capex_capacity: Bhartauli (Haryana) presses plant: phase 1 INR 70-73 crore completing first week of September 2026; phase 2 (INR 218 crore) completion expected around end-CY2027 or Q1 CY2028.
Dahej (Gujarat) SEZ skids and modules facility expected to complete around 31 May 2027.
Casting factory expansions, tubing and piping shops at Rattangarh and standard mechanical press factory at Bawal are running largely on schedule, with some facilities completing in FY27.
Board-approved manufacturing capex INR 502 crore; separate corporate office building under construction in projects business.
Q1 capex about INR 47 crore, funded from internal accruals.
demand_pricing: Domestic demand strong across almost all product lines; export inquiry base described as healthy.
Export orders booked in Africa, Latin America and Southeast Asia; more than INR 750 crore of export orders booked in Q1.
Standalone orders of about INR 1,200 crore booked in July to date (Q2 FY27).
Management says INR 95/USD rupee improves competitiveness versus other bidders; export logistics costs, freight rates and transit times have risen due to the geopolitical situation.

Commodity prices (steel, copper, aluminium, nickel) stabilised but slightly above pre-war levels; war-related material cost increases have a small adverse effect on profitability, absorbed through contingencies.
Project mix shifting to shorter-duration (max 33-36 months, target 2-2.5 years) technology-intensive orders; avoiding long contract/site-erection-heavy orders.
Sugar machinery export orders up, particularly sugar refineries; management declined to detail the large export orders.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 top-line guidance only 10-12% despite strong execution and a larger order book, and what is the quarterly run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a good part of order execution carries forward into FY28, which is why guidance is 10-12%. Projects are expected at about INR 1,000 crore a quarter and standalone manufacturing at a similar level in Q2 FY27, with Isgec Hitachi Zosen about 10% higher than FY26's roughly INR 670 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is steady-state manufacturing revenue on a consolidated basis, and how big was the Q1 US order?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated manufacturing was about INR 800 crore in Q1 and is guided at INR 750 crore plus per quarter for the next quarter, rising a bit later. The delayed US order was about INR 130 crore; the customer had paid 95% two or three quarters earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Why is guidance conservative when Q1 alone adds about INR 570 crore of incremental revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it prefers a conservative guidance it can meet over an aggressive one. It agreed the numbers could be higher and said there is hope for better outcomes.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex and revenue potential of the expansions, and when will they be complete?
qa_highlights.answer: Board-approved manufacturing capex is INR 502 crore; the corporate office in projects is separate. Full completion could add about INR 1,200 crore annual revenue, mostly from FY28-29. Bhartauli phase 1 (INR 73 crore) completes in early September 2026 with about INR 225 crore annual revenue potential, but billing starts only in Q1 FY28 as work-in-progress builds; phase 2 (INR 218 crore) completes around end-CY2027 or Q1 CY2028. Dahej completes around 31 May 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the Philippines ethanol plant post an INR 83 crore loss, and when does it reach breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: The loss comprised about INR 37 crore depreciation, INR 20 crore interest, INR 10 crore forex and unrecovered fixed costs. Utilisation is 65-70%; management targets about 90% in December and a substantially lower loss in Q2, with the plant running on molasses until the next cane season starts in November.

qa_highlights.question: How much depreciation and interest does the Philippines business carry, and is shutting or selling it an option?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 depreciation is expected at about INR 95 crore on a WDV basis, so roughly INR 57-60 crore over the remaining three quarters. Interest is about INR 19-20 crore per quarter, paid to the parent. Management said it considers all options, but a shut asset would find no buyer, and it is hopeful the plant will begin to cover interest and costs.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone PBT grow only 10% when EBITDA grew about 64%, and what drove other income?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 FY26 other income was high due to dividends from subsidiaries (about INR 20-22 crore a year, now split across quarters), interest income and forex gains on Philippines loans. Forex will keep swinging other income up and down; management said operating income was the better measure this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the export order intake, and what are the execution timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: More than INR 750 crore of export orders were booked in Q1, from Africa, Latin America and Southeast Asia, with sugar refinery machinery up. Management cited INR 95/USD as a competitive help, offset by higher freight and transit times. Execution timelines are about 4-12 months for manufactured items, 14 months to 2.5 years for projects, 15-18 months at Isgec Hitachi Zosen and 6-9 months at Eagle Press.

risks_watch: Philippines ethanol plant: utilisation has been 65-70% and it must reach about 90% by December to cover roughly INR 40 crore a quarter of depreciation and interest for PBT breakeven; the Q2 loss reduction is the key check.
Execution timing of INR 130 crore order-on-hold type dispatches and Bhartauli phase 1 billing, which starts only in Q1 FY28, so revenue visibility from new capacity in FY27 is limited.

Export logistics and war-related costs: freight rates, container availability and transit times have worsened; commodity prices remain slightly above pre-war levels and absorption relies on contingencies.
Decline in other income (forex and dividend timing) can keep PBT growth well below EBITDA growth; there is no firm guidance on capitalisation or depreciation step-up for FY27.
Saraswati Sugar Mills revenue is expected to fall on low cane availability; cane availability steps are under way for the next season.
Management declined to quantify several items (large export orders, FY27 Philippines EBITDA at 90% utilisation, capitalisation), so these should be tracked in next quarter's disclosures.
key_quotes: So the order book, I agree, has improved substantially. But a good part of the order executions is going to carry forward to the next financial year.
It's better to give a conservative guidance and meet it rather than give an aggressive guidance and be uncertain about it.
We are being realistic with a conservative bias.
Now what we are taking maximum is something like 2.5 years at the most 33-36 months.

Management repeatedly declined to give numbers on the ethanol EBITDA outlook, export order sizes and capitalisation.

533047|2026-03.headline: IMFA Q4 FY26 production about 68,500 t and PAT rose to INR103 crore on realisations of about INR109,000/t, though forex MTM weighed on other expenses.
533047|2026-03.overview: Management described Q4 FY26 as operationally strong, with production of about 68,500 tonnes including roughly 2,200 tonnes from the KNR 2 acquisition (closed 27 February 2026, furnaces switched on in March). Realisations rose to about INR109,000/t from about INR87,000/t a year earlier, lifting PAT to about INR103 crore from INR47 crore. Reported other expenses were hit by a notional forex mark-to-market loss of about INR28 crore on hedges (actual loss about INR3 crore), with the company stating the underlying forex gain sits in revenue. Management guided Q1 FY27 margins and prices above Q4 and expects around 80,000 t of sales in Q1 versus a normal 65,000–67,000 t.

segments.name: Ferro alloys (ferrochrome)
segments.commentary: Export sales are about 90% of volume, all in dollars. Management targets a 60:40 export:domestic mix by around late FY27, with at least about 200,000 t allocated domestically over time. Domestic prices are cited at INR118,000–120,000/t and export realisations above INR120,000/t.

segments.name: Mining
segments.commentary: Chrome ore output was about 8 lakh t in FY26 (above 7 lakh t in FY25), with FY27 target of 10 lakh t. Mahagari underground output was 536,000 t, and the long-term plan is 12 lakh t, entirely underground, under an investment of close to INR1,000 crore.

segments.name: Power
segments.commentary: Existing power base is 200 MW thermal at Choudwar, 4.5 MW solar at Therubali and about 5 MW off-gas. Hybrid renewable of 135 MW is contracted: 70 MW from JSW Energy (around July 2026) and 65 MW from Enfinity Global (June 2027); the 40 MW earlier deal was cancelled. The company expects 35–40% of energy from renewables in FY28.

guidance_outlook: FY27 ferrochrome output indicated at about 400,000 t, rising to about 475,000–500,000 t in FY28 (KNR 1 and KNR 2 combined).

KNR 1 (100,000 t greenfield) furnaces to be switched on around 10–15 July 2026, with the second furnace around end-August/early September; annualised 500,000 t run-rate targeted by November–December 2026.
Ethanol project: commissioning in Q2 FY27 with output expected around end-August 2026.
Partially built 33 MVA furnace at KNR 2 (adds about 50,000 t) targeted for June 2027, subject to environmental clearance; firm timeline to be given with Q1 results.
EBITDA cost per ton to fall INR3,000–4,000/t on a weighted basis once KNR 1 and KNR 2 are fully running; steady state expected from Q4 FY27.

FY27 capex about INR450 crore (balance Kalinganagar, ethanol and Sukinda underground mines), funded by about INR170 crore unutilised term loan plus internal accruals; FY28 mines capex about INR700 crore, with the bulk likely in FY28.
Coal linkage pricing expected to be INR400–500/t cheaper, benefiting from H2 FY27.
Q1 FY27: sales about 80,000 t; prices and margins guided above Q4 FY26; Q2 prices expected to be similar to Q1.
capex_capacity: KNR 1 greenfield (100,000 t): cold trials and pre-commissioning from 30 May 2026; start delayed 10–15 days due to partial manpower demobilisation and heat.
KNR 2 acquired from Tata Steel, closed 27 February 2026; operating at about 70% utilisation per analyst. Furnace tally: 100,000 t acquired plus 50,000 t from the partially built 33 MVA furnace.
Ethanol plant: pre-commissioning July 2026, commissioning Q2 FY27.
Chrome mining: 10 lakh t in FY27, moving to 12 lakh t; Sukinda open-cast ore (3–4 lakh t) to taper into underground output of about 6 lakh t.
Possible third furnace at KNR 1 on land already held; decision deferred. The earlier 220,000 t phase 2 expansion is no longer being pursued.
demand_pricing: Global ferrochrome output fell about 9.4% to just under 16 million t in 2025, supporting firmer prices along with elevated cost structures.
South African power tariff: special rate of $0.62/kWh approved versus $1.36 standard (earlier $0.877). Management views the net effect on IMFA as neutral; the outcome is uncertain.
West Asia crisis: direct impact limited to higher freight and domestic logistics costs; container and shipping availability described as under control.

Hedging policy: about 25–30% of net forex exposure hedged, mostly forwards for 12–18 months. Rupee moved from about INR89.9 (31 Dec) to INR93.65–94.65 (31 Mar) and about INR95–96 at the time of the call.
Marketing: about 70–75% of volume under long-term contracts (monthly pricing for China, quarterly for POSCO and Japanese customers); the balance is repeat spot sales.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of South African power tariff relief and the global supply response on Asian ferrochrome competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said that if South African output rises, Chinese ore supply may fall, so net supply is roughly neutral; it flagged possible upside-sharing conditions and that the tariff may not be viable if prices drop.

qa_highlights.question: What is the total power requirement met by hybrid renewables and the cost saving?
qa_highlights.answer: Power need for KNR 1 and KNR 2 is about 100 MW; 135 MW is contracted (70 MW from July 2026 and 65 MW from June 2027). Renewable tariffs are at about grid parity, fixed for 25–29 years, and coal linkage savings of INR400–500/t are expected from H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Capex and debt plans for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex about INR450 crore, funded by about INR170 crore unutilised term loan and internal accruals. FY28 includes about INR700 crore for mines, with the exact amount not yet calculated.

qa_highlights.question: Hedging policy and the sharp rise in other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: About 25–30% of exposure is hedged for 12–18 months. The notional MTM loss is about INR28 crore against an actual loss of about INR3 crore, while the forex gain in revenue is about INR80 crore above budget for the year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the INR3,000–4,000/t EBITDA cost saving from KNR appear in current numbers?
qa_highlights.answer: The saving applies only once both KNR 1 and KNR 2 are running. Start-up costs and CTU fixed charges (about INR2–2.5 crore for the GNA RE corridor from 1 June) will ease over a few quarters, with full benefits from about November–December 2026 and steady state from Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for the export:domestic mix and H1 realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: The company aims for 60:40 export:domestic by about late FY27 (currently 90:10). Q1 FY27 sales are about 80,000 t, with prices above Q4; Q2 is expected to be similar to Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Plans beyond ferrochrome, including critical minerals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is pursuing critical minerals and rare earths adjacent to its mining skill set. It has bought tender documents for some blocks in Odisha and elsewhere but has not yet bid. No quantified timeline was given.

risks_watch: KNR 1 furnace commissioning slippage (currently 10–15 July) due to manpower and temperatures of 44–45°C.
Environmental clearance for the KNR 2 33 MVA furnace; the June 2027 target is not firm.
Rupee volatility driving notional forex MTM losses on the 25–30% hedged book; Q1 FY27 may see more if INR stays at about INR95–96.
South African tariff outcome and possible supply response; potential price pressure if South African output rises.
Start-up inefficiencies (heat-up of 10–12 days, DISCOM power cost until 80–90% load) affecting near-term EBITDA per ton.
Ethanol project delivery (Q2 FY27 commissioning) and the Tata Steel KNR 2 integration.
Cash and investment income declining after the acquisition (cash down to about INR400–450 crore).

It was candid about project slippage (KNR 1, ethanol) and about the notional nature of the forex loss, while giving few numbers on critical minerals and the South African tariff.

I would say that the fourth quarter of FY '26 has been a very good quarter operationally.
Of course, a lot of it is notional, not realized, not actual losses.

533047|2026-06.headline: IMFA Q1 FY27 posted record revenue and profit: output rose to ~80,000 t from ~65,000 t average, blended realisation just under INR120,000/t, FY27 volume guidance trimmed to ~380,000 t.
533047|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as the highest-ever quarter for both revenue and profitability, driven by firm ferrochrome prices and tonnage from the KNR-2 acquisition. Production was about 80,000 t against a prior average of about 65,000 t per quarter. Management trimmed FY27 volume expectations to about 380,000 t from 400,000 t, citing transformer loading limits and a gas cleaning plant (GCP) that needs work at KNR-2. KNR-1 first furnace tapping is expected around the third week of August, with a second furnace by end-September/early October. 533096|2026-03.headline: Adani Power Q4 FY26 reported EBITDA rose 27% YoY to INR6,498 crore and PAT 64% to INR4,271 crore, though continuing EBITDA grew only 9%.

533104|2026-03.headline: Globus Spirits FY26 P&A revenue rose 27% to INR164 crores, while Q4 manufacturing EBITDA was INR8.3/litre and the company dropped its equity raise.
533104|2026-03.overview: Globus Spirits closed FY26 with installed capacity of 334 million litres after the UP distillery commissioning, at 80% utilisation (adjusted for UP start-up). Manufacturing EBITDA was INR6.2/litre for FY26 and INR8.3/litre in Q4, while Q4 volumes dipped on an ENA shift and a one-time inventory build-up that management expects to clear in Q1. Consumer P&A grew 27% for the year (58% excluding Delhi), but Q4 P&A EBITDA loss widened to INR5 crores, partly due to INR3-3.5 crores of label registration costs. Management said internal accruals and debt refinancing (annual debt outflow cut from INR67 crores to INR14 crores for FY27) mean there is no immediate need for the equity raise.

Global ENA supply constraints from high energy costs are creating export opportunities.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company giving a P&A growth target for FY27?

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 P&A EBITDA loss widen to INR5 crores?

qa_highlights.question: Why did R&O growth slow and how much did Delhi affect it?

qa_highlights.question: What is the interest cost trajectory after Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 interest rose about INR3 crores because UP term loan interest stopped being capitalised; guided INR14-15 crores per quarter going forward.

qa_highlights.question: What are the net debt and working capital levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt is INR627 crores at Q4 exit; R&O working capital is 5-6 days and expected to rise slightly from Q1.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company plan to expand into new states?

533104|2026-06.headline: Globus Spirits Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13% to INR7,888 million, EBITDA up 33% to INR795 million, PAT up 49% to INR276 million (corrected figures).

Manufacturing (ENA/ethanol) volumes reached 56.11 million litres at a record 89% utilisation, with EBITDA of about INR6.5 per litre within the INR5-7 guidance band. Prestige and above (P&A) revenue grew 35% YoY to INR550 million but still posted negative EBITDA of INR13 million, while Regular and Others (R&O) grew 10% with UP volumes scaling rapidly. Management flagged glass and PET cost-push of 10-17% and seasonal agri inflation in Q2, but said it is hedged within the margin band. Net debt was INR650 crore versus INR660 crore in March 2026. Several figures were corrected during the call: revenue should read INR7,888 million, PAT INR276 million and growth 49%, and EBITDA per litre INR6.5.

R&O EBITDA margin guidance of 15-17%, with mix from lower-margin UP expected to pull margins toward 15-16% from the 17-18% of recent years.

West Bengal R&O re-entry expected within about 60 days of regulatory approvals, which management hopes come this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: How will ethanol demand drivers develop given the E20 controversy, and could ethanol for cooking matter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said E20 is government policy, the controversy has not hurt offtake, and demand is growing about 7.5% YoY with sticky month-on-month volumes. Cooking-fuel ethanol adoption will be slow in India without distribution and canisters.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company expecting Bihar prohibition to be lifted?

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of glass cost inflation on R&O and P&A?

qa_highlights.question: Will UK FTA lower Scotch costs and expand gross profit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a tailwind as inventory transitions, but benefits depend on suppliers revising base prices. Rupee depreciation of about 20% against the pound limits the net impact, and the company is not a market maker on Scotch prices.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of R&O in West Bengal and how is the market structured?

qa_highlights.question: How much growth can be achieved without capex, and at what utilisation is new capex needed?

qa_highlights.question: What are the net debt and manufacturing margin trends?

qa_highlights.question: Why does the IMFL brand mix shift across states, with some brands rising and others falling?

qa_highlights.question: What is the UP ramp-up path and what is the margin outlook for R&O?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify quarterly UP additions but said UP is the next big bankable R&O opportunity, with a FY29 guideline already set.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company balance volume growth, input inflation and shareholder returns?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said manufacturing margin is protected by FCI fixed-price supply, maize hedging, and monthly pass-through in the flexi-price E&A business. P&A is self-funded from cash flow, with no further capacity expansion planned.

533106|2026-03.headline: Oil India FY26: consolidated income Rs 38,981 cr (+3% YoY), PAT Rs 7,551 cr (+7%), with Rs 11.5/share dividend repeated.
533106|2026-03.overview: Oil India's annual investors' meet (25 May 2026, transcript filed 29 May) covered FY26 results, a record 74-well drilling year and a 1.6x GRM uplift at subsidiary NRL. Consolidated EBITDA was Rs 13,498 cr (+5%) and PAT Rs 7,551 cr (+7%) despite crude realisation falling to $69/bbl from $78. Production was 6.64 MMtoe, with about 0.1 MMt lost to a 10-15 day economic blockade. Management reiterated the 9 MMTPA NRL expansion by March 2027, a roughly 100-well-a-year drilling plan, and offshore exploration reliant on the Samudra Manthan Mission for deep-water wells.

financial_highlights.change: ~60% drilling, ~25% capital projects, ~13% investments in subsidiaries/JVs
Down from $78; lowest in last 5 years

segments.name: Upstream (Oil India)
segments.commentary: Production 6.64 MMtoe (3.45 MMt oil, 3.15 BCM gas); daily crude peaked at ~81,354 bpd, with management citing 82,200+ bpd as of late May. Record 74 wells drilled (22 exploration, 52 development) and 307 workovers. 2P reserve replacement ratio 1.20 (vs 0.94) on 231 MMt reserves, 31-year reserve life.

segments.name: Midstream (pipelines)
segments.commentary: Numaligarh-Siliguri product pipeline expanded from 1.72 to 5.5 MMTPA, completed at Rs 750 crore vs Rs 860 crore approved outlay; PM inaugurated 13 March 2026. Duliajan-Numaligarh gas pipeline expanded from 1.2 to 2.5 MMSCMD, mechanically complete, awaiting a ~7-day NRL shutdown to commission.

segments.name: Downstream (NRL, 100% subsidiary of Oil India Ltd, 3 MMTPA)
segments.commentary: Record 103% crude throughput, 99.1% availability, 87.25% distillate yield and 727 TMT MS output; GRM 1.6x prior year. Navratna status conferred Dec 2025. Expansion to 9 MMTPA targeted for March 2027, with polypropylene unit on track; expansion capex ~Rs 46,000 crore including ~Rs 7,200 crore for PPU.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Mozambique force majeure lifted Nov 2025; two LNG trains of 13 MMTPA targeted for end-2028 or early 2029, with ~$1.8 billion committed and ~$300 million cost escalation pending CCEA approval. Russian assets (Taas, Vankor) have returned ~$1 billion in dividends. Libya 95/96 major commercial discovery.

segments.name: New energy and others
segments.commentary: Oil India Green Energy Ltd (wholly-owned) has ~2 GW renewable capacity in JVs pipeline and 2 CBG plants under construction, with 2 more awarded or in tender, against a target of 25 by 2030. 49 KTPA bamboo 2G ethanol plant inaugurated Sept 2025; NRL green hydrogen plant of 2.4 KTPA (Rs 138 crore) due by end-2026.

guidance_outlook: Production: 4 MMtoe achievable with ~100 wells drilled per year; long-term target 12 MMtoe by 2030 (from 10).
Gas: 3.35 BCM guided for FY27; ~5 BCM targeted by FY28 once Duliajan feeder line and DNPL expansion are commissioned.
NRL: CDU/VDU ~mid-July 2026 (~400 TMT output after that, mostly diesel), DHDT about a month later, PFCC/RPTU by Dec-Jan, full 9 MMTPA by March 2027 (stabilised by March 2028).
Capex: rollover of ~Rs 10,000 crore a year for ~100 onshore wells per year, plus shallow-water offshore drilling.

Offshore: deep-water well targeted for spud around June 2027; four-plus-four deep-water wells at ~Rs 1,200 crore each (Rs 4,800-5,000 crore), contingent on Samudra Manthan Mission sponsorship. Shallow-water wells ~Rs 800 crore each.
NRL excise duty: ~Rs 3,000 crore accrued in FY26, with 50% NE excise benefit and no sunset clause at 9 MMTPA; management expects calibration if FOB HSD prices fall.
capex_capacity: Drilling: 74 wells in FY26 (record); released drillable location inventory ~218 vs ~45 earlier; average Assam shelf depth ~4,300 m.

Offshore: deepest well (6,000 m, Kerala-Konkan) at ~3,400 m; Andaman well 3 drilling complete and testing; KG DSF appraisal well underway; gas occurrence in Andaman well 2 under appraisal with 600 sq km 3D seismic.
Feeder/evacuation: Duliajan feeder line (3.5 MMSCMD) authorised; PNGRB approval Feb 2026, mechanical completion FY28, offtake up 40%.
Gas capacity: production ~8 MMSCMD, ramp-up path to 13-15 MMSCMD with 15-18 pure gas wells identified.
Crude import pipeline Paradip-Numaligarh (9 MMTPA) 92% physically complete as of 30 April 2026; 99% ROU acquired.
demand_pricing: Realisation: crude at $69/bbl in FY26, lowest in 5 years; government moves on royalty and post-wellhead cost realisation cited as cash-flow support.

New well gas: 1.5 MMSCMD allocated to NRL, priced at 20% premium over APM, but only accrues once NRL is commissioned and allocation is confirmed; allocation priority runs CGD, fertiliser, refinery/petchem, then power.
Gas to NE CGD: ~50,000 SCMD allocated to NE Gas Distribution and Purbabharati Gas Distribution as NRL reseller.
Product demand: management cites 7-8% growth in refined product consumption; NRL export via Indo-Bangladesh pipeline optional, not the basis for 9 MMTPA.
Competition/partners: TotalEnergies signed technology service agreement (Nov 2025) for offshore seismic and exploration support, with a say in investment decisions.

qa_highlights.question: What is the offshore exploration capex and how will the capability gap be addressed?
qa_highlights.answer: Shallow-water well ~Rs 800 crore; deep-water wells ~Rs 1,200 crore each, four plus four wells (~Rs 4,800-5,000 crore), contingent on Samudra Manthan sponsorship. Government also identified Rs 3,200 crore for four stratigraphic wells jointly with ONGC.

qa_highlights.question: NRL excise duty benefit in FY26 and impact of recent duty cut?
qa_highlights.answer: ~Rs 3,000 crore accrued in FY26; no sunset clause on 50% NE excise benefit at 9 MMTPA. Management expects excise to be recalibrated against HSD FOB prices if they fall.

qa_highlights.question: NRL 9 MMTPA viability, and terms of the TotalEnergies arrangement?
qa_highlights.answer: Viability rests on domestic demand (7-8% growth) and NE/mainland logistics, with Panchgram, Singimari and Jogighopa depots and Siliguri tankage. TotalEnergies is a service agreement, with Total able to weigh in on investment decisions.

qa_highlights.question: NRL timelines, first product output, and capex spent/remaining?
qa_highlights.answer: Mother units by end-July; ~400 TMT output after that, mostly diesel. Full 9 MMT by March 2027, stabilised March 2028. Expansion capex ~Rs 46,000 crore including PPU (Rs 7,200 crore).

qa_highlights.question: FY27 production, gas and capex outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: 4 MMT with 100 wells; gas 3.35 BCM in FY27 and ~5 BCM 18 months out. Rollover capex ~Rs 10,000 crore per year.

qa_highlights.question: Current production exit rate and gas ramp path?
qa_highlights.answer: Current crude ~82,200 bpd, a record. Gas ~8 MMSCMD now; management says 13-15 MMSCMD possible with new pipelines, with first accrual only on allocation and commissioning.

qa_highlights.question: Mozambique incremental equity outflow?
qa_highlights.answer: ~$1.8 billion already committed; ~$300 million escalation pending CCEA. Further phases to be assessed after FID.

risks_watch: Samudra Manthan Mission notification and sponsorship mechanism still pending; deep-water capex is uncertain until notified.
NRL expansion timeline: DNPL commissioning depends on a 7-day NRL shutdown deferred by Middle East crisis; CDU/VDU mechanical completion due mid-July 2026.
New well gas premium (20%) depends on government allocation; accrual timing tied to CGD saturation in NE.
Excise benefit (~Rs 3,000 crore in FY26) may be recalibrated if product prices fall.
Production risk from economic blockades (lost ~0.1 MMt in FY26) and natural decline of 10-12% a year.
Mozambique cost escalation (~$300 million) awaiting CCEA approval.
key_quotes: Dr. Ranjit Rath, Chairman and Managing Director, Oil India Limited and Chairman of Numaligarh Refinery Limited.

The idea is that through a mechanism while the data collection in terms of 2D and 3D seismic data will be sponsored by the Government, the Government would also sponsor the deep water and ultra deep water wells which we intend to drill in our exploration acreage.

So, we would really come to know once it is notified, how many numbers of wells government is going to sponsor 100%, how many wells government is going to sponsor 50% or precisely how the mechanism would be.
So, excise to my opinion is going to get calibrated based on the overall FOB of HSD which is the driving force for the refinery transfer price which happens between NRL and the OMCs.
Now the question is this New well gas needs to be allocated by government.
533106|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on production records, NRL commissioning and offshore ambition, repeatedly stressing government support and "on track" delivery. Cautious or evasive on Samudra Manthan Mission mechanics, deep-water well sponsorship terms, and NRL excise recalibration, which management repeatedly deferred until notification or government approval.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides 4 MMtoe production in FY27 (vs 6.64 MMtoe reported in FY26 total incl. gas, so the guide is on an oil-equivalent basis still to be reconciled) on 100 wells, with gas at 3.35 BCM and 82,200+ bpd crude exit rate, but 10-12% natural decline and blockade risk are headwinds.

tone.note: Management was confident on production records, NRL commissioning and the 9 MMTPA by March 2027 target, but cautious and deferring on Samudra Manthan sponsorship mechanics and NRL excise recalibration; analysts pressed on NRL 9 MMTPA viability and Mozambique incremental equity.

533106|2026-06.headline: Oil India Q1 FY27 standalone PAT rose to INR2,870 crore from INR813 crore, on record EBITDA of INR4,605 crore and crude realisation of USD98.73/bbl.
533106|2026-06.overview: Standalone operating revenue hit a record INR7,958 crore and EBITDA a record INR4,605 crore, with margin above 54%. Crude output was 0.95 MMT, up 11%+ YoY, and daily output peaked at 10,921 MT on 27 June, later 11,017 MT on 3 August. Subsidiary NRL ran at 105% capacity utilisation with a GRM of USD35.95/bbl (about USD33 ex-inventory gain), and consolidated PAT was INR4,026 crore. Management guided to roughly 1 MMT crude per quarter and about 3.9–4 MMT for FY27, and gas evacuation hinges on DNPL/IGGL connectivity.

segments.name: Upstream (standalone crude and gas)
segments.commentary: Q1 FY27 production was 1.707 MMBoE, with crude at 0.95 MMT (+11%+ YoY) and gas up 0.4% QoQ. Gas off-take has been constrained at about 2.93 BCM by evacuation limits, and management targets 3.8 BCM next year and about 5 BCM by FY29.

segments.name: NRL (refining, material subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Capacity utilisation was 105%, distillate yield 87%, and GRM USD35.95/bbl vs USD5.02 a year earlier. Management said about USD2 of the GRM was inventory gain, and OMC discounts under SAED were netted off.

guidance_outlook: Crude production: about 1 MMT per quarter from now on, roughly 3.9 MMT for FY27 with a possible touch of 4 MMT; FY29 target of about 4.2 MMT from main producing areas, with upside from near-field exploration.
Capex: FY27 budget is INR8,600 crore (to be revised at the next review); Q1 spend was about INR3,050 crore, including INR1,230 crore on exploratory drilling.
Wells: FY27 target of 100 wells (42 exploratory, 57 development), up from 74 in FY26; a further 10% rise is intended for FY28.

NRL: CDU/VDU, DHDT and SRU to be commissioned by Oct–Nov 2026, remaining units by 31 March 2027, reaching about 75% of 9 MMT rated capacity by Q4 FY28; Paradip–Numaligarh pipeline mechanical completion targeted October and commissioning by December 2026.
Gas: 200 m connection within the NRL campus (2–3 months) to link DNPL with IGGL; DFL feeder line about 20% complete; big jump in evacuation expected from Q1 FY28 and about 5 BCM by FY29.
GST on royalty: about INR2,500 crore (excluding interest) is already provided; payment to be made, with no prospective interest. The Assam land tax is a contingent liability with no P&L impact.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex about INR3,050 crore: survey INR450 crore, exploratory drilling INR1,230 crore, development drilling INR700 crore, capital equipment and projects INR350 crore, subsidiaries/JVs/overseas INR350 crore. FY26 actual capex was INR13,026 crore.
Wells drilled in Q1: 17 (7 exploratory, 10 development). Drilling history: FY25 22 exploratory and 35 development; FY26 22 exploratory and 52 development.

Andaman: Vijayapuram-1 spend about INR1,000–1,050 crore; hydro-frac testing in August; fourth Andaman well by a jack-up rig targeted for December 2026; 600 sq km of new 3D seismic to be processed by October.

Deep water (Mahanadi and KG): 4,200 line km and 5,300 sq km of 3D acquired; first deep-water rig expected June–July 2027, second by March 2028. Government reimbursement of up to INR675 crore per well is proposed under the Samudra Manthan scheme.

NRL expansion: about INR30,000 crore spent to date, with INR34,000–35,000 crore expected for the refinery project and another INR7,200–7,300 crore for the PPU project. NRL debt is about INR19,000 crore.
demand_pricing: Crude realisation was USD98.73/bbl and gas USD7.19/MMBtu; new-well gas is priced outside APM, and incremental volumes will all be new-well gas.

NRL's GRM is about USD33 excluding the roughly USD2 inventory gain. Diesel and petrol discounts to OMCs under SAED ran at INR13/l to INR3/l for petrol and INR10/l to nil for diesel during the quarter, and have reappeared as a monthly recalibration.

Gas off-take from BCPL is stable at about 1.25–1.35 MMSCMD (about 4.25 MMSCMD returned to the grid by Oil India). NEEPCO is cutting gas use in favour of hydro, and excise benefit fell as government calibrated excise to hold retail prices.
NRL operating cost is about USD4.5–5/bbl, targeted to fall to about USD3.5/bbl as expansion units stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current crude run-rate, and can production sustain the 10,921 MT/day level?
qa_highlights.answer: Director Operations said the company expects about 1 MMT per quarter from here, citing workover, well intervention and optimisation; output reached 11,017 MT/day on 3 August.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for gas ramp-up from 2.93 BCM to about 5 BCM?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 and H1 FY28 would be flat to slow; the big jump is expected from Q1 FY28 once the 200 m NRL link and DFL/IGGL are complete, with about 1.5 MMSCMD of extra headroom from DNPL capacity expansion and 3.5–4 MMSCMD of evacuation planned.

qa_highlights.question: What is the normalised NRL GRM, and what is the exploration capex outlook given the government support?
qa_highlights.answer: NRL GRM was about USD35 including about USD2 inventory gain (about USD33 ex-gain). Exploration: 100 wells targeted in FY27 and a 10%+ rise intended thereafter, with deep-water programme funded in part by government schemes.

qa_highlights.question: What is the NRL expansion status and the Paradip–Numaligarh pipeline timing?
qa_highlights.answer: CDU/VDU mechanically complete, with three units to be commissioned by Oct–Nov 2026 and the rest by 31 March 2027; pipeline ROU is secured except about 8 km, with commissioning by December 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt position across the group?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone: USD1.4 bn loan for Mozambique. Singapore subsidiary: USD500 mn bond due May 2027. NRL: about INR19,000 crore. Total group debt about INR37,233 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did contract costs rise, and what is the GST-on-royalty payment outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Contract cost rose by about INR146 crore QoQ to INR615 crore, mainly offshore G&G costs. About INR2,500 crore GST on royalty (excl. interest) is already provided, to be paid with no prospective interest; the Assam land tax is a contingent liability.

risks_watch: Gas evacuation remains the binding constraint: BCPL and NEEPCO off-take is seasonal and the DFL/IGGL and 200 m NRL link are still pending.
NRL's GRM is inflated by SAED-linked discounts and an inventory gain of about USD2/bbl; the normalised GRM is about USD33 and the discount level is calibrated monthly.
Andaman Vijayapuram-1 and -3 testing is still pending; a write-down or capitalised-cost review is possible after the September decision.
Assam land tax case is being withdrawn via the state legislature; the contingent liability is removed only once withdrawal is effective.
Q2 gas volumes could dip with monsoon and tea-garden seasonality from October; exploration cost (G&G) inflated opex in Q1.

Cautious and hedged on gas evacuation timelines, which management tied to pipeline completion, and some answers were given loosely or deferred. Frequent line disconnects and unclear figures in Q&A reduced precision on several numbers.

533148|2026-09.headline: JSW Energy Q2 FY27: revenue up 24% YoY to ₹6,658 crore and PAT attributable up 50% to ₹1,056 crore, with 1.4 GW commissioned since April.

qa_highlights.question: Are the Mahanadi expansion PPAs utility-type, given Chhattisgarh discom rules requiring in-state capacity?

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp QoQ jump in Utkal EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 had outages and lower availability, limiting merchant sales; Q2 PLF was ~82% with long-term PPAs with Karnataka and Assam, and better merchant sales added to fixed-cost recovery.

qa_highlights.question: Tenure of the 25% fixed-rate debt?

rows.why: Net generation up 17% YoY to 17.5 BU, renewables generation up 25% (wind) and 36% (solar) on ~1.5 GW added, and power demand growing ~11% in Q2 with October month-to-date at 21.2%; curtailment of ~4.8% of generation is a drag until permanent GNA for ~60% of affected capacity by end-Q3 FY27.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reaffirmed the 3 GW FY27 target and 2.5-3 GW annual pace but declined to give run-rate EBITDA or forward numbers; Q3 merchant book is fully booked at ~₹6.9/unit or better, which could support a raise if Q4 pricing holds.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Risks include 1.6 GW of remaining FY27 RE execution, ~225 MU Q2 curtailment (₹59 crore), imported coal at ~US$115/t (+28% YoY), and ~75% floating-rate debt where a further 75 bps hike lifts cost of debt to ~8.5% from 8.28%.

rows.why: 1 GWh standalone BESS in Rajasthan and Kerala to be commissioned in FY27 under ESAs, Halol wind blade facility already producing since June, Chitradurga facility due Q3 FY27, and solar-plus-battery for evening-peak sales planned.

rows.label: Group RTC/captive demand and MoU conversion

rows.label: Permanent GNA for curtailed capacity
rows.why: About 60% of curtailed capacity moves from temporary to permanent GNA by end-Q3 FY27, which should cut the ~225 MU Q2 curtailment (₹59 crore) loss.

rows.why: Net debt/TTM EBITDA is ~4.94x, down from ~5.2x in FY26, and cost of debt fell 51 bps YoY to 8.28%, though the rate-hike sensitivity could reverse part of this.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 3 GW FY27 RE target, 2.5-3 GW annual pace, and Q3 merchant booking, but guarded on run-rate EBITDA, Bhutan project cost, and merchant pricing beyond Q3; analysts pressed on Chhattisgarh in-state PPA rules and RE project economics.

533150|2026-03.headline: Godrej Properties Q4 FY26 bookings hit record INR10,163 crores (+21% QoQ); FY27 booking guidance set at over INR39,000 crores.
533150|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 posted record quarterly bookings of INR10,163 crores on 4,789 units and 7.3 mn sq ft, matching the prior best quarter and growing 21% QoQ. FY26 bookings reached INR34,171 crores (+16% YoY), 105% of guidance, and collections hit a record INR19,965 crores (+17% YoY). Q4 total income rose 47% to INR3,895 crores and net profit rose 70% to INR650 crores, with FY26 PAT at INR1,850 crores (+32%). Management guided FY27 bookings above INR39,000 crores and collections above INR24,000 crores, both about 20% growth, and reiterated a 20% ROE target by FY28. Management flagged the Middle East conflict and AI-related sentiment as near-term demand risks, while saying April footfalls and conversions held up.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said NCR's FY26 dip was due to slipped launches (Gurgaon approvals, Ashok Vihar) and expects NCR to return above INR10,000 crores. It sees AI worries as overdone and reasonable for guidance, and said the launch calendar is skewed to H1 and built bottom-up with buffers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost impact of the Middle East war on demand, NRI inflows and construction costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand dipped in March but has since normalised somewhat; the Dubai-related shift to Indian property is expected to play out over time. Input costs are estimated to rise 5% to 6% at most, with a 0.1% to 0.2% quarterly margin impact, and forward contracts cover most inputs.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company keep pursuing BD above its INR20,000 crore guidance, and when will FCF turn positive?
qa_highlights.answer: BD depends on opportunities, and the balance sheet can support more than guided levels. At INR20,000 crores of BD, FCF should be positive; at FY26-like levels, breakeven. FY28 is expected to be strongly FCF positive.

qa_highlights.question: Why did imputed EBIT margin fall to about 24.5% in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a large Bengaluru 50-50 JV project (about INR4,000 crores of sales) and a fall in economic interest to 88% from 93%. PAT margin was at the top of the 10% to 15% guided range for a third year.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the dividend being introduced, and what does it signal about cash generation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said surplus cash will rise as BD investment normalises relative to cash generation, so dividends will be made consistent and growing. The FY27 dividend is modest.

qa_highlights.question: Will the FY27 collections and revenue recognition step up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the major revenue step-up in FY28 as OCs arrive, with about INR2,900 crores of revenue already linked to OCs. Economic interest has compounded at 55% a year over five years.

533150|2026-09.headline: Godrej Properties Q2 FY27 bookings fell 6% YoY to INR8,008 crore, but sustenance sales rose 83% to INR5,054 crore and collections hit INR5,318 crore.
533150|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 bookings were INR8,008 crore from 3,658 units (6.2 mn sq ft), down 6% YoY and 7% QoQ, while H1 bookings grew 7% to INR16,669 crore. Sustenance sales were the standout at INR5,054 crore. Collections rose 31% YoY to a record Q2 of INR5,318 crore and operating cash flow was INR1,584 crore. Reported P&L fell sharply: EBITDA down 72% to INR171 crore and net profit down 62% to INR154 crore, which management attributed to back-ended deliveries and JV exit accounting (Mahalunge, Orris). Management guided H2 bookings of INR22,500-25,000 crore and a strong Q3 launch pipeline.

Only about one-third of the annual launch pipeline was launched in H1; launches are picking up from October.

About 80% of Q3 approvals were secured before the quarter began; the residual is expected shortly after Diwali. For Q4, about 80% of approvals are targeted between end-November and mid-December, with the rest by mid-January.

Business development is opportunistic; threshold returns are a 20% IRR and a 15% bookings-to-net-profit margin. Bangalore and Noida are priority additions, plus select Mumbai micro-markets (South Mumbai, Western suburbs, Thane).
demand_pricing: Management said prices are holding up: less than 1% increase in some NCR projects, about 2% in South and Mumbai projects, and about 0.5% in the rest of the portfolio.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA and net profit fall sharply despite higher sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajendra Khetawat said the Mahalunge JV became a 100% owned project after the partner exit, so the bulk of profit had been recognised earlier through DM fees and overheads, which led to near-equal sales and cost of sales. The Orris settlement also picked up losses on consolidation in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: How long will sustenance sales stay high and what is the launch vs sustenance mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Gaurav Pandey said H2 launches will likely outperform sustenance, and the 60-40 launch-sustenance mix is a guide that can flip if launches slip. Sustenance strength reflects a deliberate push after Gurgaon and Mumbai launches slipped.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company exceed its H2 sales guidance and how much can it add to pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Pirojsha Godrej said the top end of the H2 range (INR25,000 crore) would imply a 40% five-year compounded booking growth. He said the company will not hold back if opportunities arise beyond the 15-20% FY28 growth target.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the H2 launch pipeline has approvals?
qa_highlights.answer: About 80% of Q3 requirements were secured before the quarter, with the rest expected after Diwali. For Q4, management targets about 80% approvals by mid-December and the rest by mid-January.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook on BD and competitive intensity for land?
qa_highlights.answer: Pirojsha Godrej said competition is ongoing but opportunities meeting return thresholds are available, and BD will remain opportunistic. Gaurav Pandey said one or two deals could close in the quarter if terms fit.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company near FCF-positive status in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Gaurav Pandey said there is a high probability of being FCF positive in Q4 under aggressive internal scenarios, while noting this is not an obsessive target. FY28 is described as almost certain for operating cash flow guidance.

533151|2026-03.headline: D. B. Corp Q4 FY26 consolidated ad revenue rose ~6% YoY to INR 4,067 mn; FY26 total revenue flat at INR 24,408 mn.

For FY26, reported figures were flat versus FY25 because of the prior-year election advertising; excluding that, print ad revenue grew 6.3% and EBITDA 7.1%, with margin up 66 bps to 28%. Management said April 2026 ad growth was strong double-digit and guided to a strong single-digit growth for FY27. Newsprint prices are rising, with management expecting a further 6-8% increase in Q1 FY27.

segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 circulation revenue stable at INR 1,162 mn; average copies about 39 lakh, down roughly 1-2% (about 1 lakh) from prior quarters. Management said competitors are losing more copies in several markets.

qa_highlights.question: Will other income or state election effects lift next quarters, and is an 18% or 16%+ EBIT margin target planned?

qa_highlights.question: Print growth and sector-wise breakdown for FY26?

qa_highlights.question: Where is the INR 120-140 cr capex going and why buy rented properties?

qa_highlights.question: Why was there no dividend, and are buybacks planned?

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Google-related revenue issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Publishers have jointly filed a case with the Competition Commission of India against Google and others; no outcome yet.

Domino's delivered 2.5% LFL in Q1 FY27 against 11.6% in the prior-year quarter, and management expects Q2 FY27 to be better than Q1. Cost pressure rose: LPG, cheese, oil, labour code and minimum wage hikes were partly offset by pricing and efficiencies, leaving the net margin headwind at about 20 bps QoQ. Management held FY27 capex guidance of INR 750-900 crore and the 200 bps EBITDA margin expansion target, with about 100 bps viewed as ahead of track.

segments.commentary: LFL growth 40-45%; about 90 stores, with 7 cities above INR 100K ADS for the full quarter. Target ADS is above INR 100K; gross margin still scaling and marketing spend high (about INR 100 crore revenue base invested to reach INR 1,000 crore).

qa_highlights.question: What is driving Popeyes LFL acceleration from 9.2% to 45%, and where does it normalise?

It declined to forecast normalisation, saying 45% is not a target to hold forever.

qa_highlights.question: Why has per-store employee cost not risen despite minimum wage hikes?

qa_highlights.question: What is the dine-in strategy and expected outcome?

Early Wednesday results show reversal of trend; first goal is to hold dine-in and takeaway LFL flat.

qa_highlights.question: Can LFL reach 5-7% for the rest of FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, citing a two-quarter average of 2.5% (Q1 FY27) and 11.6% (Q1 FY26), which gives over 7%. It said Q2 FY27 will be better than Q1.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company maximise free cash flow?

qa_highlights.question: How is the EBITDA margin target progressing given cost inflation?

qa_highlights.question: What happened to Domino's margins QoQ after the MOV cut and cost inflation?

533156|2026-06.headline: Vascon Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue fell to INR152 crores (from INR221 crores) and PAT to INR2 crores (from INR22 crores), on EPC execution delays.

Consolidated EBITDA was INR10 crores versus INR34 crores in Q1 FY26, which included an INR18 crores one-time investment gain; adjusted for that, EBITDA was about INR15 crores at roughly 6% margin. Management said the EPC segment stayed profitable at about 9% EBITDA margin, while real estate booked INR4 crores revenue and a INR4 crores EBITDA loss. Management guided to a recovery from Q3 and reiterated the FY27 revenue target of INR1,200 crores, while net debt rose to about INR152 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 INR1,200 crore revenue target still valid?

533169|2026-03.headline: Man Infra FY26 consolidated PAT after minority interest of INR201 crores; FY27 launches targeted at INR5,500 crores GDV and sales ambition of over INR5,000 crores across FY27-FY28.

Q4 FY26 sales were about INR438 crores and collections about INR279 crores, with consolidated PAT after minority interest of INR43 crores on total income of INR187 crores. Management guided to a 35-40% rise in revenue recognition in FY27, driven by about 1 million sq ft of launches and near-complete projects, and reiterated a Vision 2030 goal of doubling GDV to over INR35,000 crores. Balance sheet was reported as net debt-free with net worth of about INR2,266 crores and liquidity of about INR686 crores against debt of about INR58 crores.

533169|2026-06.headline: Man Infra Q1 FY27 consolidated PAT rose 29% YoY to ₹72 crore on revenue up 8% to ₹218 crore; management reiterates 25%+ FY27 PAT growth guidance.
533169|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as a strong quarter, citing consolidated revenue from operations of ₹218 crore (+8% YoY) and profit after tax attributable to shareholders of ₹72 crore (+29% YoY). Cash and cash equivalents rose to ₹768 crore at June 2026 from ₹686 crore at FY26-end, with borrowings of ₹78 crore, which management said are mostly partner contributions in joint ventures. Pre-sales in the quarter were about 85,000 sq ft, or roughly ₹290 crore, which management acknowledged is low, attributing the gap to launches that have not yet happened (Marine Lines, Berkeley House). Management kept its FY27 PAT growth guidance of over 25% and its target of ₹5,000 crore cumulative pre-sales over two years, and reiterated a ₹35,000 crore group GDV goal by 2031.

guidance_outlook: FY27 PAT growth guidance of over 25% over FY26 reiterated; management said it sees this as comfortable at the bottom line.
Cumulative pre-sales target of ₹5,000 crore over the next two years reiterated; management said it might exceed this if markets stay strong.
Group GDV target of over ₹35,000 crore by 2031 reiterated, with management expecting it to be achieved earlier.
Management aims for a bottom line near ₹500 crore in roughly 2-3 years; it said a significant jump would start this year.
Launch pipeline of about 1.1 million sq ft carpet and ~₹6,600 crore GDV planned this year (two launched so far: Marina Vista and O2 High Street).
Management said it expects to add ₹2.5-3,000 crore GDV per ₹200 crore of capital, with ~₹3,000 crore of cash generation over three years.

Most of the ₹78 crore is partner contribution treated as debt-like funding used for project cash flow, not external institutional borrowing. Future projects may be 100% owned.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company expand beyond MMR into cities such as Pune or Delhi?
qa_highlights.answer: Not for the next couple of years. Management cited per-sq-ft margins in Mumbai exceeding prices in other cities and limited projects elsewhere, and said it is confident in Mumbai.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ₹5,000 crore two-year pre-sales target still achievable given ₹290 crore in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said real estate sales are lumpy, with launches driving ₹1,000 crore-plus months. Marine Lines (₹3,000 crore-plus GDV) and Berkeley House (₹1,000 crore-plus) are not yet launched, and it expects a turnaround by December and March. It said the target could be exceeded if markets stay strong.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the US (Miami) business, its margins, cash flows and forex approach?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the first two villas are complete, one sold and one held as show house until around March next year. The third villa is priced around $15 million. Ritz-Carlton presales are about $25 million, completion targeted December 2030, and about $35 million has been transferred so far, with principal expected back by 2031 according to management. It said the dollar moved from ₹75 to ₹95 and margins are equal or higher than India.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY26 cash flow negative and will it turn positive in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to new acquisitions and working capital for ongoing projects during a slow sales year. It said the upward trajectory has started with Q1 PAT growth and the launch pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: What are the margin profiles of ultra-luxury projects, and how is the DM model's economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ultra-luxury margins per sq ft are higher, with tickets of ₹1 lakh per sq ft and above and Mount Mary/Pali Hill sales around ₹20,000-25,000 per sq ft. Bottom-line percentage stays around 20-25% across projects. DM projects return about 2.5-3x invested capital, with under 10% of GDV invested.

533179|2026-06.headline: Persistent to acquire Nagarro at EV €1.27bn (€81/share cash) and signed a ~$650M, 6.5-year net-new deal adding ~$125M annual value.
533179|2026-06.overview: Management held a Sunday call (28 June 2026) announcing two items: a net-new strategic deal with an existing large US-headquartered customer worth roughly $125M annually and about $650M over 6.5 years, and a voluntary public takeover offer for Nagarro at €81 per share in cash. The Nagarro offer implies an equity value of about €1bn and EV of €1.27bn, funded by a committed €1.4bn Barclays bridge facility, with a 50% plus one share minimum acceptance. Persistent has already secured 21% via a share purchase agreement, and management board members intend to tender about 13-14%. Closing is expected around Q4 CY2026 or early Q1 CY2027, subject to regulatory approvals. No Q1 FY27 financial results were discussed on this call.

financial_highlights.metric: Nagarro EBIT margin CY25 / Q1 CY26

financial_highlights.value: 140% to undisturbed close (25-26 June); 94% to 3-month VWAP

segments.name: Persistent (standalone)
segments.commentary: Five-year revenue CAGR of about 23.9%, with North America about 81%+ of revenue and Europe about 8-8.5%. Team of 27,500 across 21 countries.

segments.name: Nagarro (target)
segments.commentary: 5-year revenue CAGR of 18.4%, with about 35% of revenue from North America and about 18,500 staff (13,500 in India). Strengths cited in SAP, Siemens, OpenAI reseller and industrial/consumer verticals; management says constant-currency growth was over 5% recently.

segments.name: Combined group
segments.commentary: Pro forma about $2.9bn revenue, 46,000+ staff across 40+ countries; mix of North America 62%, Europe 22%, Rest of World 16%. Management targets European revenue of 15%+ and $5bn aspiration by FY31.

guidance_outlook: Leverage (net debt / combined EBITDA) at close expected at 1.9x-2.5x depending on acceptance, reducing to about 1x by FY2030.
Transaction expected to be cash EPS accretive and reported EPS accretive in Year 1 excluding one-time transaction expenses.
Goodwill vs other intangibles split about 70:30; intangibles amortised over 8 years.
Acquisition-related bridge interest at Euribor plus 175-250bps, roughly 4.1%-4.8% (4.1%-4.5% quoted in Q&A).
Revenue and cost synergies to be detailed only after regulatory approvals; management says margins will be maintained or improved.
New large deal is accretive to revenue and margin from Q2 onwards with no major ramp-up needed.

Public offer timeline: BaFin filing within 4 weeks, offer clearance in 10 working days to 2 weeks, 4-week acceptance period plus optional 2-week extension; Persistent AGM late July to seek shareholder approval. Squeeze-out possible over about 2 years; no domination agreement intended for 2 years.
capex_capacity: Transaction is fully debt-funded via a committed €1.4bn Barclays bridge facility, which also covers Nagarro refinancing if required, backed by a Persistent parent corporate guarantee.
Management said it does not intend a QIP or further dilution; private equity participation at asset level is being considered but no decision taken.
Management said it has moved from capex-heavy models to an opex model, funding working capital to support cash generation.
demand_pricing: Net new large deal from an existing US-headquartered technology customer: ~$125M annually and ~$650M+ over 6.5 years; customer name not disclosed under NDA.
Persistent has two $100M+ accounts, with a third approaching; the combined entity has 180 logos above $1M (Nagarro's largest customer under $50M) and over 350 $1M+ accounts.
Customer overlap between the two companies is in the single digits, with fewer than 10 significant overlapping customers.

Management said T&M model will decline over time but is not dead; Nagarro's T&M share was cited as 65-68% by analysts. Cannibalisation of T&M revenue acknowledged, with SASVA platform cited as a response.

qa_highlights.question: Has there been incremental due diligence on Nagarro's books given BaFin queries, and why is the multiple at a premium?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said legal and tax diligence on BaFin queries (carve-out from Allgeier and accounting principles) found no impact on performance; the premium was described as reasonable for a control transaction.

qa_highlights.question: Will Nagarro run independently for two years post-closing, and why no cash-plus-share structure?
qa_highlights.answer: Persistent will work with management and aim for a squeeze-out over about 2 years, with no hurry. Management said a share swap was not feasible under German public-to-private dynamics; no QIP or dilution planned.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ramp and margin profile of the large deal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is net new with little ramp needed, end-to-end product engineering and support, accretive from Q2, at a fairly healthy margin above company average.

qa_highlights.question: How will the combined entity sustain growth given Nagarro's slow growth and the long tail of accounts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to cross-selling of ERP/CX and mining of 180 $1M+ logos, with tail-account rationalisation possible to release SG&A. It said Nagarro's recent growth was affected by distraction from its take-private process.

qa_highlights.question: Decision tree on acceptance: what if below 50%, and what follows above 50%?
qa_highlights.answer: Persistent holds 21% via SPA; management board commitment of about 13-14% takes it near 35%, with another 35-40% considered broadly committed. Management sees 50%+ as very likely; majority gives control of the supervisory board.

risks_watch: Regulatory approvals (including RBI and various EU jurisdictions) and BaFin clearance of the offer document; close targeted Q4 CY26 to early Q1 CY27.
Acceptance level versus the 50%+1 minimum; leverage moves between 1.9x and 2.5x depending on acceptance.
Nagarro's revenue flat for about two years, with several vertical declines (horizontal tech, energy/utilities, telecom, travel) flagged by analysts.
Integration of a two-year squeeze-out path with minority shareholders; synergy plan and value-creation plan not yet shared.
Cash conversion and debt servicing of roughly €1.4bn of acquisition debt, plus the T&M model and AI cannibalisation risk.
533179|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and assertive on strategic fit, growth and margin ambitions, but deliberately evasive on specifics pending regulatory approvals (no synergy numbers, value-creation plan, or customer names). Pushback was given to analysts on Nagarro's EBIT margins and the premium paid.
key_quotes: This is not a consolidation play. This is an expansion play for us bringing together, as Anand rightly pointed out, people, capabilities, markets which are all complimentary to us
we believe we have paid a reasonable premium for a control transaction.
we do not believe that the combined entity will be at any significant lower margins than what Persistent has today.
We don't intend doing any QIP, just to be clear for everyone. We don't intend diluting our stake at this point in time.

rows.why: Management says margins will be maintained or improved and the new ~$125M annual deal is accretive to margin from Q2 at above company average, but synergy numbers are withheld until regulatory approvals and combined EBITDA margin is ~15.6% for Persistent vs Nagarro 13.9%.

rows.why: Net-new ~$125M annual (~$650M over 6.5 years) US deal accretive from Q2 with little ramp, and Persistent run-rate revenue above $1.7bn; Nagarro revenue is flat for about two years, so growth is mainly deal-driven.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management says it has moved from capex-heavy to opex model, no QIP or further dilution planned, and the €1.27bn EV deal is funded by a committed €1.4bn bridge rather than new plants.

rows.when: post close, Q4 CY26 to early Q1 CY27
rows.why: Management guides cash and reported EPS accretion in Year 1 excluding one-time transaction expenses, but gave no organic revenue guidance and no Q1 FY27 results were discussed.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Leverage of 1.9x-2.5x at close on ~€1.4bn acquisition debt at Euribor+175-250bps (~4.1%-4.8%) raises interest cost and execution risk; Nagarro revenue flat for ~2 years and T&M share 65-68% faces cannibalisation.

rows.why: Signed ~$650M over 6.5 years (~$125M annually) with an existing US technology customer, accretive from Q2 with little ramp needed and a margin above company average.

rows.label: Nagarro take-private closing
rows.when: Q4 CY26 to early Q1 CY27
rows.why: Voluntary offer at €81/share (EV €1.27bn), 21% already secured via SPA plus ~13-14% board tender intent, with 50%+1 minimum acceptance; management sees 50%+ as very likely, subject to RBI and EU approvals.

rows.label: Leverage down to ~1x by FY2030
rows.why: Net debt/combined EBITDA of 1.9x-2.5x at close, expected to reduce to about 1x by FY2030 as cash generation repays the €1.4bn bridge debt.

tone.note: Management was confident on the $125M net-new deal, accretion and the 50%+ acceptance path, but evasive on synergies, value-creation plan and customer names pending approvals; analysts pushed on Nagarro's EBIT margins, the premium paid, and T&M cannibalisation.

533179|2026-09.headline: Persistent Q2 FY27 revenue rose 20% YoY to USD 487.6M, but EBIT margin fell to 15% and reported PAT dropped 25.4% on Nagarro deal costs.
533179|2026-09.overview: Revenue grew 7.8% QoQ and 20% YoY in USD to USD 487.6M, the 26th sequential quarter of growth, with rupee revenue of Rs 46,639M (+30.3% YoY). EBIT margin was 15% (down 100 bps QoQ and 130 bps YoY) as wage hikes and a 90 bps amortisation hit from the large software deal offset ESOP and currency tailwinds. Reported PAT of Rs 3,515.1M (7.5% margin) was hit by about 3.1% from Nagarro transaction costs, while operating PAT rose 5% YoY to Rs 4,951.5M. Bookings slowed: TCV was USD 633.5M and ACV USD 481M, with management citing deal slippage and a decision-making slowdown linked to Middle East dynamics. The Nagarro acquisition is progressing, with about 94% of shares tendered and closing guided to Q4 CY26 or Q1 CY27.

segments.name: North America
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 22.5% YoY in USD terms.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Revenue declined 8.5% YoY, attributed to one acquired key client ramping down and one fixed-price engagement completing its planned ramp-down; management called these client-specific.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 19.4% YoY; rest of world grew 67% YoY on a smaller base.

segments.name: Software, High-Tech and Emerging
segments.commentary: Grew 28.5% YoY, driven by the large software deal from last quarter and the new Software Reinvention offering.

segments.name: BFSI
segments.commentary: Grew 16.2% YoY, supported by a vendor consolidation win at a large financial services client.

segments.name: Healthcare and Life Sciences
segments.commentary: Grew 12% YoY; management said growth should resume, citing a slowdown from a couple of customer-specific dynamics.

guidance_outlook: EBIT margin aspiration of 16-17%; management said it is an aspiration, not guidance, with no year-end target committed.
Nagarro deal closing expected by Q4 CY26 or Q1 CY27; remaining RBI, Austria and Spain FDI approvals expected within 4-8 weeks.
Nagarro acquisition one-time expenses of about USD 50M in total over 3-4 quarters; about USD 19-20M incurred in Q2 and USD 25-30M more to come.
Post-closing, intent to squeeze out minority shareholders (about 94% acquired) and an estimated 5-6 months to integrate the two companies.
Acquisition debt cost assumed at 5-6% net; USD 1.25B debt and equity raise planned to replace the Euro 1.4B bridge loan, including USD 450M equity or equity-linked instruments.
Transaction-related one-time costs may be treated as an exception for ESOP vesting conditions (12% revenue growth and 12% EPS growth), subject to shareholder approval.
capex_capacity: Headcount rose by 958 QoQ to 29,598 at end of Q2 FY27.
Utilisation fell 70 bps QoQ to 85.8%, reflecting proactive hiring for large-deal ramp-up; utilisation drag was about 20 bps on EBIT margin.
Trailing 12-month attrition was 11.9%, down from 12.3% in Q1.

The large software deal (about USD 650M over 6.5 years) carries about USD 4M per quarter of added amortisation on third-party licences and cloud spend, a 90 bps EBIT margin hit that management expects to ease as spend is optimised and revenue scales.
Internal AI IP (SASVA, iAURA, Gen AI) development cost includes significant people cost plus tools; management said it can rise QoQ with new feature development.
demand_pricing: Q2 bookings were USD 633.5M TCV and USD 481M ACV, versus Q1 TCV of USD 1,146.2M and ACV of USD 536.8M which included the USD 650M large deal; management said some deals slipped and decision-making slowed in recent weeks, linked to Middle East dynamics.
Top 5 customers grew 38.9% YoY, top 10 grew 29.9%, top 20 grew 25%, top 50 grew 24%, top 100 grew 21.6%.
Customers above USD 20M annual revenue rose from 12 to 13, above USD 10M from 25 to 34, above USD 5M from 56 to 60, and above USD 1M from 191 to 280.
BFSI demand themes: vendor consolidation, data modernisation for AI and legacy (mainframe) modernisation; management did not give formal guidance but said all segments should grow well.

Software Reinvention Services targets AI-native product development and cost reduction of legacy products; in one case, a marquee software client's product run cost fell 45%.
