Nagarro target: about 200 USD 1M+ customers with only 10 overlapping with Persistent's, per management's diligence view.

qa_highlights.question: Is high token cost pushing enterprise clients to IT services vendors, and is BFSI an early AI adopter?

qa_highlights.question: Will the 90 bps large-deal amortisation hit persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Vinit Teredesai confirmed it will stay in the base for the next two to three quarters and gradually reduce as cost is optimised and revenue grows.

qa_highlights.question: Is the USD 650M large deal included in last quarter's TCV, and why are Q2 bookings softer?
qa_highlights.answer: Sandeep Kalra said the deal was included in Q1 TCV of USD 1,146.2M and ACV of USD 536.8M, which included USD 125M ACV from it. Q2 ACV of USD 481M and TCV of USD 633.5M were described as a reasonable clip, with some slippage and no productivity-driven decline.

qa_highlights.question: Will software licence costs stay at current levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Sandeep Kalra said it is a mix of licences embedded in deal products and Persistent's own tool investment; levels should be assessed on overall profitability as the reinvention practice grows.

qa_highlights.question: Is margin recovery expected post wage hike, and what is the year-end target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated a 16-17% aspirational margin range, not guidance, with optimisation and deal growth as the levers.

qa_highlights.question: What are quick wins from Nagarro after closing?
qa_highlights.answer: Sandeep Kalra said a synergy plan can only be built after closing; a cooperation agreement already allows cross-selling. Nagarro has about 200 USD 1M+ customers with only 10 overlapping with Persistent's.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost of acquisition debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Vinit Teredesai said 5-6% on a net basis, depending on timing; the Nagarro revolver is about 5 banks at SOFR-linked pricing and is being refinanced.

qa_highlights.question: What is the breakdown of the USD 50M one-time costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Vinit Teredesai said costs cover investment banking fees, bridge loan commitment fees, legal, regulatory filings, travel and funding costs; about USD 19-20M was incurred in Q2 and USD 25-30M is expected over the next 3-4 quarters.

segments.commentary: Q1 wind output was muted by delayed monsoon and a weak first part of the wind season; new 9.9 MW wind capacity partly offset the shortfall. Turbine performance described as nominal with no significant availability issues.

segments.name: Solar (C&I)
segments.commentary: 7 MW solar plant commissioned December 2025 and contributing. A further 17.6 MW solar is under implementation; management targets commissioning by end September 2026 with the 7.8 MW wind repowering.

segments.name: Netherlands holding entity / Croatia asset
segments.commentary: Liquidating a 100% step-down Netherlands subsidiary with no assets; the Croatia asset (about 10.5 MW) stays with the company. Related top-line about EUR 1 million per year (about Rs 9 crore).

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue and EBITDA guided to be equal to or better than FY26, with a higher bar contingent on the monsoon and wind; Q2 said to be better than Q1.
Margins expected to be sustained as O&M costs are largely fixed.
FY27 capacity additions: about 17.5 MW solar and 7.8 MW wind, plus 3.3 MW wind already added, totalling about 11 MW wind and about 15 MW solar this fiscal (per management).
Blended interest rate targeted at around 9% going forward, from 9.1% now; approaching IREDA for a further 15 bps reduction on the Beta loan.
FY28: 15-20 MW of repowered assets expected; broader capacity plan to be clearer by mid-Q3 FY27.

Promoter share pledge expected to be fully released by end of FY27 per CFO; full promoter loan final due September 2027 (the CFO said installments run to September 2027 and about 40% of the loan repaid).
capex_capacity: Commissioned 3.3 MW wind at start of Q1 FY27, following 6.6 MW at end of FY26 (9.9 MW incremental wind); 7 MW solar commissioned December 2025.

Under implementation: 17.6 MW (about 17.5 MW) greenfield solar and 7.8 MW wind repowering in Clarion (Tamil Nadu); both expected by end September 2026 after delays from a change of state government and approvals.
Next repowering phase: about 17.5 MW in Gamma next year, plus about 2.8 MW more at Clarion; first stage around 28 MW total repowering, selected on lowest-wind machines.
Potential for another 20-25 MW by leveraging existing assets; existing wind sites could host at least about 100 MW of hybrid solar, subject to land and Tamil Nadu hybrid policy notification.
Targets 1 GW total capacity (earlier 2028 target), with inorganic (mostly wind) and organic growth; no firm acquisition yet.
demand_pricing: Net PPA rate about Rs 4.75 per unit across corporate and government (Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu), net of transmission cost; solar differs.
Management says no material receivables above 90 days other than the Andhra Pradesh delayed-interest amount.
Industrial (group captive) customers must hold 26% equity in new projects, providing some funding.
Management says demand is not the constraint; funding is the constraint ('we need Vitamin M').
BESS currently not required in Tamil Nadu; battery storage regulation expected to be clarified within 2-3 months per management; future solar expected to include battery storage.

qa_highlights.question: Plan to reach 1 GW given the share price near Rs 10 and limited capital options?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says it is still working towards 1 GW, with brownfield and acquisition options; serious conversations did not proceed; expects something to move in FY27 but declined to give valuations or details.

qa_highlights.question: How does the current wind season compare with last year?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 was significantly worse than last year; Q2 to date is matching last year's pace; the season is seen as similar to two years ago.

qa_highlights.question: Debt and interest guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Interest about Rs 13-14 crore per quarter; blended rate 9.1%; about Rs 90-100 crore repayment this year, total debt about Rs 535 crore at year-end; new debt for repowering expected next year.

qa_highlights.question: Andhra Pradesh delayed interest receivable and provisioning?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 20 crore outstanding on delayed PPA interest; Rs 6.5 crore provided (about 30%); APERC non-functional, so recovery is pending.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company expand through debt alone, and how is capital being raised?
qa_highlights.answer: Only about 20-25 MW more can be done through leverage on existing assets; further growth needs equity; talks with PE investors and promoters are ongoing with no firm outcome.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 guidance conservative given capacity additions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says guidance is conservative because of wind uncertainty; it expects to exceed FY26 thanks to added capacity, but by an amount dependent on the monsoon.

risks_watch: Wind dependence: Q1 volumes were weak, and FY27 top line depends on monsoon and wind; Q2 recovery is not yet proven.
Funding for 1 GW target remains unresolved; no firm equity, acquisition or partner announced, and the share price is near Rs 10.
Repowering and solar commissioning timelines have slipped (from June 30 to September 30, 2026) due to Tamil Nadu approvals.
Andhra Pradesh delayed-interest receivable of about Rs 20 crore, with Rs 6.5 crore provided; recovery depends on APERC becoming functional.
Promoter pledge release timing is unclear: earlier comments suggested full release by end FY27, while the CFO also cited September 2027 as the final loan due date.
Tamil Nadu battery and hybrid policy still pending, which affects economics of future solar and hybrid projects.
533263|2026-06.management_tone: Cautious on near-term volumes and candid that growth is constrained by funding; confident on margins and on the 9.9 MW wind plus 7 MW solar adding to profits. Evasive on acquisitions, valuations and promoter funding, saying talks are ongoing without detail.
key_quotes: Therefore, we have been able to come close to the corresponding quarter last year's numbers.
We need Vitamin M. We need Vitamin M.
So, we are still moving to expand, but it has been slower than what we anticipated.

533267|2026-03.headline: Cantabil FY26 standalone EBITDA rose 29% to INR264.3 crore at a 31% margin, with Q4 EBITDA up 34% to INR78.1 crore.
533267|2026-03.overview: Management reported record FY26 standalone revenue of INR852.6 crore (up 18%), PAT of INR95.8 crore (up 28%) and PAT margin of 11.2%. Q4 FY26 revenue grew 15% to INR253.5 crore, with EBITDA up 34% to INR78.1 crore and margin expanding to 30.8% from 26.6%. Management said same-store sales growth (SSG) was about 5% in FY26 and April 2026, and gross margin held near 60%. The company opened 91 stores in FY26 against 38 closures and relocations, and ended with 652 stores and 9.15 lakh sq ft.

financial_highlights.change: +18% YoY (text compares against FY21 figure of INR721.1 crore, likely FY25)
+15% vs INR219.8 crore in Q4 FY25
+34% vs INR58.4 crore in Q4 FY25
+30% vs INR22.5 crore in Q4 FY25 (margin vs 10.2%)

segments.name: Company-operated (COCO) and franchise stores
segments.commentary: Network of 652 stores covering 9.15 lakh sq ft; about 80% COCO and 20% franchise, with franchise mainly in Tier 3 markets. Average new store size rose to about 1,400 sq ft in FY26 from about 1,100 sq ft three years ago.

segments.name: Online (e-commerce)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 online revenue about INR11 crore vs about INR10 crore a year earlier (about 10% growth in value, about 13% in pieces per management). Management cited Myntra/Flipkart billing changes as a drag. A new 4-floor warehouse in the new corporate building serves online only.

segments.name: Footwear
segments.commentary: Footwear sales were INR14 crore in FY26 vs INR10 crore in FY25 (+40%), about 2% of sales; target about 3-4% by end FY27, mainly via online.

segments.name: Kids wear
segments.commentary: About 2-3% of total sales; management expects 4-4.5% next year as family stores (45% of FY26 openings) grow.

segments.name: Manufacturing (Bahadurgarh)
segments.commentary: Own factory capacity of 18-20 lakh garments, meeting about 25% of requirement, with job workers at about 35%; the factory is a specialised suit plant. Management says the 60:40 own-and-job-work to accessories mix will broadly hold.

guidance_outlook: FY27 targets: about 725 stores and INR1,000 crore revenue; about 90-100 gross store additions (about 70-75% net).
Gross margin: internal target of about 60% maintained despite input cost inflation; EBITDA margin of about 30% expected if gross margin holds.
SSG guided at 5-6% for FY27, with upside to 7-8% described as too early to call.
Marketing spend about 1.7% of sales, could rise to 1.8-2%. Opex as a percentage of sales expected to stay within about plus or minus 1%.
Store area growth targeted at 15-20% per annum (15% minimum). Capex per sq ft expected to fall with a new furniture and fixture design; capex about INR1,800 per sq ft.
Lease cost: about INR99-100 crore in FY26 (Ind-AS 116 basis), rising to INR108-110 crore in FY27.
Corporate office and warehouse move expected to save INR1.5-2 crore annually from Q2/Q3 FY27.
Working capital about 105 days in FY26 (vs 115 days prior year); inventory days about 109-110, with target to keep below 120.
capex_capacity: FY26 openings: 91 stores (about 1.1 lakh sq ft added); 38 closures or relocations (about 24-25 renewals and relocations, 13 performance-based).
About 45 stores in the pipeline as of the call.
New corporate office and warehouse building (11 floors; 4 for corporate, 4 for online warehousing, WMS-automated) is capitalised; building cost about INR50-55 crore excluding land.
Company is debt free and funds capex from internal accruals; about INR100 crore of capex has been planned, with a further expansion plan expected from Q3 FY27.
Bahadurgarh factory floor expansion is under way (part of INR10 crore CWIP). Management said manufacturing will rely more on job workers than on a new own plant.
Nepal: four stores (mix of multi-brand and EBO), run through a selling and distribution model; no other overseas markets yet.
demand_pricing: SSG about 5% in FY26 and in April 2026; May 2026 SSG described as decent. Management says it is on track for 5-6% even if rates rise by about 100 bps.

Average bill value up about 10% a year, attributed to inflation plus better product mix. Management did not share price-hike plans beyond saying prices depend on cost, with some input cost passed on to customers.
Q4 gross margin of about 57% (vs 53-54% a year earlier) was attributed to product mix, pricing correction and GST benefit.
Management says footfall is holding up with no impact seen yet from inflation.
Retail cost fell to 33% of sales from 34%. Backend corporate cost about 8% of sales.
Average rent per sq ft fell to INR115 in FY26 from INR120. Inventory above 1 year is about 25-30% of total; provisioning is 10% for 1-3 years and 50% above 3 years.
Management said it will not enter fast fashion (Zara-type) and will stay with basic and collection-led brands such as UNIQLO.

qa_highlights.question: Is SSG correlated with monetary policy, and what levers exist if rates rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SSG was about 5% in FY26 and in April 2026, and it expects to keep 5-6% even if rates rise about 100 bps, citing incentives, efficiency and marketing.

qa_highlights.question: Why is INR25 crore shown under loans?
qa_highlights.answer: It is an intercorporate loan to a non-related party at about 12% for one year, versus market returns of 6-7% on surplus funds; management said it could be closed in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the lease cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Lease cash outflow (principal plus interest, Ind-AS 116) was about INR100 crore in FY26; actual rental cost was about INR99 crore. It is expected to rise to INR108-110 crore in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is gross margin of 60% sustainable in FY27 despite input inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 60% gross margin is an internal target, with about 1% variance either way.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 gross margin of about 57%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited product mix, pricing correction and GST benefit, not procurement efficiency, and said the margin will be maintained.

qa_highlights.question: Is online growing, and how is it measured?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 online revenue was about INR11 crore vs INR9.9-10 crore a year earlier (about 10% in value and 13% in pieces). The platforms changed billing, which reduced reported value growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the inventory and working capital position?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital was about 105 days in FY26 (vs 115 days), inventory days about 109-110; management expects it to stay around this level.

risks_watch: Inflation and possible monetary tightening could reduce discretionary demand; management has not quantified the sensitivity.
Input cost pressure may hit gross margin, which management targets at about 60%; Q4 FY26 margin was flattered by mix and GST.
Store-addition pace: FY26 gross openings of 91 were above the plan, but the 675-store plan was missed on net count as closures and relocations offset openings.
Online channel growth lags the platform headline (about 10% in value vs 13% in pieces) because of billing changes at Myntra and Flipkart.
Deployment of surplus cash: INR25 crore is in a non-related intercorporate loan, and the company has not yet announced a specific expansion plan for the cash.
533267|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on FY26 records, growth and margin targets. Answers on SSG, gross margin and opex were direct; answers on FY28 inflation planning and the cash deployment plan were vaguer.
key_quotes: The margin, what we are targeting on a long-term basis is approximately 60%.
The moment we will be able to maintain that, our EBITDA margin, 30% will always be on the card.
We are targeting that 15% to 20%, 15% minimum.
Interest cost, we don't have because we are debt free.

rows.why: Management targets EBITDA margin of about 30% (vs 31% in FY26) and gross margin of about 60% (vs 60.4%), with opex within plus or minus 1% of sales; lease cost rising to INR108-110 crore from about INR100 crore and marketing possibly rising to 1.8-2% cap further expansion, so margin is held rather than expanded.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 91 stores opened in FY26 with about 45 in pipeline at the call, and FY27 guidance of 90-100 gross additions to reach 725 stores (from 652, about 11% net unit growth) with store area growth of 15-20%.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue target of about INR1,000 crore (about 17% over FY26's INR852.6 crore) with SSG of 5-6% and store count rising to 725 from 652.

rows.why: Company is debt free, funds capex from accruals, about INR100 crore capex already planned, and management flagged a further expansion plan from Q3 FY27; utilisation was not disclosed, so the trigger rests on cash and plan rather than capacity strain.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: SSG guided 5-6% for FY27 with upside to 7-8% described as too early to call, and Q4 EBITDA grew 34% to INR78.1 crore at 30.8% margin.

rows.why: Footwear sales grew 40% to INR14 crore in FY26 with a target of 3-4% of sales by end FY27 (from about 2%), and kids wear is targeted at 4-4.5% of sales next year (from 2-3%).

rows.label: Online channel growth lag from billing changes
rows.why: Q4 FY26 online revenue grew about 10% in value (about INR11 crore vs INR10 crore) and 13% in pieces, with Myntra/Flipkart billing changes acting as a drag.

rows.label: Surplus cash deployment (INR25 crore intercorporate loan at ~12%)
rows.why: The company is debt free and holds INR25 crore in a one-year loan to a non-related party at about 12% versus 6-7% market returns on surplus funds, which management said could be closed in FY27, with no specific expansion plan yet announced for the cash.

rows.label: Price increases to offset input inflation
rows.why: Average bill value rose about 10% a year and some input cost is passed to customers, but management did not share price-hike plans.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY26 records, 5-6% SSG, ~60% gross margin and 30% EBITDA margin targets, and direct on SSG, gross margin and opex; it was vaguer on FY28 inflation planning and the cash deployment plan, and analysts probed rate sensitivity and input cost pressure.

533267|2026-06.headline: Cantabil Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13% to INR178.8 crores and EBITDA margin widened to 33.2%, but PAT margin slipped to 9.1%.
533267|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew 13% YoY to INR178.8 crores and EBITDA grew 21% to INR59.4 crores, with margin up to 33.2% from 30.8%. PAT grew about 11% to INR16.3 crores, but PAT margin was 9.1% versus 9.2% a year ago. Management attributed the margin gain to product mix and price increases passed to customers, and said July demand was moderate with festive timing shifting into Q3. Management reiterated the INR1,000 crore FY27 revenue target and about 5% SSG for the full year, relying on new stores and a Q2 opening push of 28-30 stores.

financial_highlights.value: 667 stores, 9.42 lakh sq ft retail area

segments.name: Retail stores (standalone)
segments.commentary: Q1 opened 15 stores totalling about 27,000 sq ft; average Q1 opening store size 1,810 sq ft. Average store sales were INR1.26 crore in FY26, with mature stores at about INR1.5 crore and stores under 1-1.5 years near INR1 crore.

segments.name: Online
segments.commentary: Online share fell to about 5% in Q1 from 6% in FY26 because of a software and end-to-end integration change; management targets 8% for FY27 and says online is run above EBITDA level.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of INR1,000 crores reiterated, implying about 18-19% growth; management split this into 10-12% volume growth plus inflation pass-through.
Full-year SSG target about 5% (management also cited a 5-6% long-term aspiration), with about 3% from price and balance from volume.
Average annual gross margin target of about 60% and EBITDA margin of 30% or more maintained; PAT margin ambition 11-12%.
Store additions of 28-30 in Q2 FY27 and about 55,000-60,000 sq ft; average store size target around 1,500 sq ft by year end.
Working capital cycle guided at 100-105 days; finished goods inventory target 110-120 days.
Management expects volume growth to pick up in Q3 as Diwali falls on about 10 November, and says Q2 volume growth will be limited.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 openings of 15 stores (about 27,000 sq ft); Q2 plan of 28-30 stores and 55,000-60,000 sq ft.
Store sizes are rising: average opening store 1,810 sq ft in Q1 versus about 1,500 sq ft average over the last two years.
Franchise store count fell from 178 (FY23) to 130 as the company moves to larger formats that franchisees find hard to fund in Tier 3 towns.
Around 20-25 stores close each year on performance, market or franchise issues; management calls this normal.
Inventory ageing: about 75% under 1 year, 20% 1-3 years, about 5% over 3 years (mainly surplus factory outlet).
demand_pricing: Same-store sales growth of 4.04% in Q1; volume growth about 7-8% against about 13% area growth.
Raw material prices up about 10% (earlier 20-25%); management says the full cost is being passed to customers with no volume impact, though cotton is up 10-15%.
July was moderate; Raksha Bandhan moved to late August (versus 10 August last year), so festive sales shifted and management declined to comment on the current quarter.
Management says it will not pursue premiumisation; ASP is about INR1,100 and is to be held there.
Competition: new-age and D2C brands are said to share about 50-60% of their basic casual and formal ranges with Cantabil; management frames the difference as roughly 40% of the collection.
Repeat customers are close to 50%; management is not launching a points-based loyalty programme for now but will consider it.
Q1 gross margin rose on product mix plus inflation correction; management says gross margin will move up and down by quarter but the annual target holds.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin expand YoY and QoQ, and will it sustain?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a mix of product mix and inflation correction; it expects the average annual gross margin of about 60% to hold, with quarterly swings possible.

qa_highlights.question: Did the Haryana and UP minimum wage hikes hit employee costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; Haryana wages rose about 30-35% and that cost is in Q1. Management said the full quarter's impact is captured and there is no further large impact.

qa_highlights.question: What happened to the INR25 crore loan to a real estate developer?
qa_highlights.answer: INR10 crore was repaid in Q1; the remaining INR15 crore is due by about February. Management said such transactions will not recur.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR1,000 crore revenue target achievable and what drives it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target is on track, with new stores, SSG and online as drivers, and Q2 openings expected to recover the Q1 shortfall.

qa_highlights.question: Why has ROCE fallen and how are inventory days being managed?
qa_highlights.answer: Finished goods inventory days fell to 114 in FY26 from 121 in FY25; working capital days fell to about 100 from 110. Management aims for 110-120 days and says ROCE is about 40%.

qa_highlights.question: Why has franchise (FOCO) count declined?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said bigger store formats need larger investment, which franchisees in Tier 3 towns are not willing to make, and most stores are in Tier 2 and beyond.

risks_watch: PAT margin flat at 9.1% despite EBITDA margin gain of about 230 bps; watch depreciation and Ind AS effects from larger stores.
Volume growth of about 7-8% lags 13% area growth; management guides for a pickup only in Q3 with Diwali in November.
Festive timing shift (Raksha Bandhan late August) could weigh on Q2 SSG; management declined to comment on the current quarter.
Cotton and raw material cost pressure; management expects prices to correct but gave no basis, and pass-through is assumed to hold.
Franchise store count down from 178 (FY23) to 130 and falling, which slows the asset-light model.
Online share fell to 5% in Q1 during a software integration; the 8% FY27 target depends on this migration.
Working capital cycle guided at 100-105 days; inventory ageing needs monitoring.
Management was not forthcoming on the INR15 crore receivable beyond a February repayment date, and call quality limited several questions.

533269|2026-03.headline: VA Tech Wabag FY26: revenue up ~20%, PAT up 26%, order book INR 17,200 crore (over 4x revenue), net cash ~INR 950 crore.
533269|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue growth of about 20% year-over-year and PAT growth of 26%, with EBITDA margin at 13.3% and ROCE near 20%. Order intake was about INR 7,500 crore versus about INR 5,700 crore last year, taking the order book to INR 17,200 crore, up 26% YoY. Net cash (ex-HAM investment) was about INR 950 crore, up 35% from INR 700 crore, and the company has been net cash positive for 13 consecutive quarters. Management reiterated the 15-20% growth and 13-15% EBITDA guardrails, with a new five-year strategy to be published later in the year. Q&A focused on Middle East pipeline (Kuwait and Saudi orders expected), quarterly India-cluster profitability, lumpy EPC revenue, and the municipal platform and HAM plans.

segments.name: EPC vs O&M revenue mix
segments.commentary: EPC about 83% and O&M about 17% of revenue. O&M is about 40% of order backlog (~INR 6,500 crore), with contracts of 5-20 years; target is to lift O&M to 20% of the mix over 3-5 years.

segments.name: Municipal vs Industrial revenue mix
segments.commentary: Municipal about 80% and industrial about 20% of revenue. Management is adding industrial and mentioned BPCL, Reliance and Aramco-linked pursuits.

segments.name: India vs ROW
segments.commentary: Revenue split about 50:50 India and rest-of-world. Order backlog split about 58-60% India and 40-42% ROW.

segments.name: India cluster
segments.commentary: Key projects include Chennai 45 MLD TTRO (rehab plus O&M, INR 1,000+ crore), Chennai ADB-funded ring main, Kodungaiyur reuse O&M, Perur desalination (Southeast Asia's largest per management), Bangladesh and Nepal projects. Digha-Kankarbagh STP won GWI best wastewater project. Quarterly Indian profit fell from about INR 127 crore to INR 60 crore per the questioner; management said to judge on blended multi-year margins.

segments.name: Middle East and Africa cluster
segments.commentary: Management calls MEA the growth engine; Yanbu desalination mega order won. Al-Haer 200 MLD STP is 83% physically complete. guidance_outlook: Revenue growth guardrail of 15-20% CAGR and EBITDA margin of 13-15% reiterated; new five-year strategy and guardrails to be published later this year, expected to be better than current guidance.
Order book to remain above 3x revenue (currently over 4x); ROCE expected to cross 20% within a couple of years; O&M target 20% in 3-5 years.

Management expects revenue to rise in coming periods as new India orders (Kodungaiyur, Chennai ring main, BPCL, Reliance, BWSSB, DJB) convert; CFO said next year could be about 35% higher but is lumpy.
Kuwait order expected in the current quarter; Saudi order may go to the next quarter (management best guess).
Municipal platform (HAM-style) and industrial tenders expected to be finalised over the next quarter; no HAM bids confirmed yet.
capex_capacity: Asia's largest desalination plant (Tamil Nadu, 400 MLD per analyst question) expected to be commissioned around this time next year.
Al-Haer 200 MLD STP (Saudi) at 83% physical progress; commissioning expected after construction completion.
Bio-CNG first project signed; expected to supply around 3,500 homes' cooking gas or about 400 vehicles per day; management said revenue is not very large initially, with plans to replicate.
Modular plant design being used to replicate standard modules for faster build; ceramic membranes being pursued over polymeric membranes.
Asset-light model: management says gross and net block are among the lowest in the sector; technology captive (125+ patents), not licensed.
demand_pricing: Middle East: GCC opportunity estimated at about $5 billion per year over 10 years; management cites Saudi Vision 2030, FIFA World Cup 2034, Oman Vision 2040, and Kuwait pre-selection; UAE first order in progress.
Overall addressable market quoted at $75-100 billion over 5-7 years, plus $4-6 billion future energy (solar PV, semiconductors, data centres, green hydrogen) and about $10 billion O&M.
India: $20-25 billion opportunity cited; SAARC $5-10 billion; India treats only about 28% of sewage generated, per management.
Competitive positioning in Middle East: management claims it wins on life-cycle cost (capex plus opex) because it operates the plants it builds; won 3 of last 6 STPs in MEA.
Price variation clauses: present on most large Indian orders with 2.5-3+ year duration, covering only about 70% of cost; generally absent in international contracts.
Management says desalination water costs about 8 paise per litre and reuse about 5-6 paise per litre.

qa_highlights.question: How will revenue and growth shape up for the next five years, and how does WABAG benchmark against the top two players in India and globally?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reaffirmed 15-20% growth and 13-15% EBITDA guardrails; margin levers are scale, a higher international mix (currently 50:50), and O&M rising to 20%. A new strategy with updated guardrails will be published later in the year.

qa_highlights.question: Is WABAG building capability to move into higher-margin equipment products?
qa_highlights.answer: No, the company will not become an equipment maker; it focuses on process solutions, R&D on membranes and crystallisation, and lowest footprint, totex and power use.

qa_highlights.question: Who wins Middle East bids that involve several top competitors: price or technical?
qa_highlights.answer: Rohan Mittal said L1 pricing alone is not rewarded; PPP projects weigh life-cycle cost, and WABAG's edge is operating data, captive technology and end-to-end build-operate capability, claiming margins well above what competitors bid.

qa_highlights.question: What does asset-light mean for an EPC/O&M company?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said assets are people (about 2,000 engineers) and about 125 patents; the company does not own real estate, equipment or manufacturing, so its capital employed is very low relative to revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Will size constrain growth beyond INR 8,000 crore revenue, and will there be a strategic pivot?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said no diversification outside water is planned; the market is large enough. A small bolt-on acquisition for technology was confirmed as a possibility ('definitely, short answer is yes').

qa_highlights.question: Status of Kuwait and Saudi orders and FY27 order inflow expectation?
qa_highlights.answer: Preferred bidder for both per public tender openings; Kuwait expected in the current quarter, Saudi possibly next quarter. No explicit FY27 order target given.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Indian cluster profit fall and revenue look flat year on year?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said quarterly segment profit should be judged on blended multi-year margins because projects are in different phases and cost pools are shared with MEA; India backlog is 58% of total and new orders (Kodungaiyur, ring main, BPCL, Reliance, BWSSB, DJB) will drive revenue.

Quarterly profitability is lumpy: the India cluster's quarterly profit dropped to about INR 60 crore per the questioner, and management asked investors to judge on multi-year blended margins.

Mixed statements on quarterly reporting: investor requested quarterly (Q4) numbers in press releases; management did not commit.

533269|2026-06.headline: VA Tech Wabag Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 20.8% YoY to INR 887 crore, PAT up ~37% to INR 90 crore, order backlog record INR 19,400 crore.
533269|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was INR 887 crore (+20.8% YoY), EBITDA INR 116 crore (+21.7%, margin just over 13%) and PAT INR 90 crore (+~37%, 10.2% margin). Order intake exceeded INR 3,400 crore, 77% from international markets, taking the order book to a record INR 19,400 crore (over 4x revenue). Management said the company stayed net cash positive for the 14th consecutive quarter, and new wins included a 60 MIGD Kuwait desal plant and the third phase of Ajman STP in the UAE. Management guided 15-20% revenue growth for the year and reiterated a 13-15% medium-term EBITDA margin band, with FY27 more likely at 13-14%.

segments.commentary: EPC 82% and O&M 18% of revenue. India 48%, overseas 52%.

segments.name: Order intake

segments.name: Order book

segments.commentary: O&M revenue grew about 7% YoY in the quarter. Management said it will grow in line with project completions moving into O&M phase (Ghaziabad, Digha-Kankarbagh completed; Perur next year).

Working capital guided to stay in the 100-110 day range despite growth; long-term Wriddhi 2.0 strategy to be presented at the May FY27 investor meet.

Kodungaiyur: agreement signed, DPR submitted to the PE; refurbishment (1.5 years) to start any time, followed by 18.5 years of operation.
Kuwait 60 MIGD SWRO (with HEISCO) and Kutaisi (Georgia) project started; Ajman STP phase 3 is a design-build sewage biorefinery.
demand_pricing: Order intake was dominated by international wins: Kuwait desal (first project there), Ajman STP phase 3 in UAE, Vienna Water Works high-end drinking water, plus repeat Indian orders in Bengaluru and Delhi (Byramangala, Bellandur, Mitraon/DJB).
Bid pipeline: management cited about USD 2-3 billion across MEA and India (about INR 20,000-25,000 crore), with India about USD 1-1.5 billion. No order inflow target was given.
Management said the Middle East conflict has had no material impact on projects; it has written force majeure letters to customers covering price and time impacts.
Domestic traction is returning in industrial and municipal segments; management still sees larger deal sizes overseas.
Industrial share of backlog is about 12-13%, with an aim of 20-25% over time; traditional industrial is ~90% oil and gas.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall YoY, and were there one-off provisions in other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed margin differences to project mix (more EPC vs EP). It said other expenses included standard provisions for delay or anticipated default under a tighter policy, which can be reversed on collection. No one-off was described.

qa_highlights.question: What is the share-of-profit from associates (~INR 5.5 crore) and is it recurring?
qa_highlights.answer: It is mainly from HAM projects that moved from construction to O&M. Management said it includes construction-phase risk releases, so it may not recur at the same level.

qa_highlights.question: Is the forex gain operational and how does it affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said forex gains arise from transactions (invoices, collections, payments) and are treated as operational; translation gains go through reserves. It said it has a natural hedge and uses PCFC for residual exposure.

qa_highlights.question: Will the order backlog execute faster outside India?
qa_highlights.answer: International EPC cycles are 24-30 months versus about 36 months in India; the backlog is expected to execute over about 36 months overall.

qa_highlights.question: Is the TSGENCO receivable (~INR 140 crore) recoverable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the matter is sub-judice, the Supreme Court verdict is in its favour, and it would not give a timeline.

TSGENCO receivable (~INR 140 crore) still in arbitration with no timeline; Kodungaiyur refurbishment start awaits PE approval.

533271|2026-03.headline: Ashoka Buildcon Q4 FY26 standalone EBITDA fell 7% to INR168 crores; FY27 guidance calls for 20% revenue growth and 9.5-10.5% margin.
533271|2026-03.overview: Standalone total income fell 10% YoY to INR1,819 crores in Q4 FY26, with EBITDA of INR168 crores (9.2% margin, up 20 bps) and PAT of INR49 crores versus INR60 crores a year earlier. For FY26, standalone total income declined 17% to INR5,952 crores and EBITDA declined 6% to INR636 crores. Consolidated Q4 EBITDA was INR302 crores at a 15.1% margin. Management attributed the weak year to slower industry awarding, project delays, input cost inflation and fixed-cost under-absorption, and it guided to recovery in FY27 led by monetisation cash flows and a 20% revenue growth target.

533271|2026-06.headline: Ashoka Buildcon Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA fell 55% YoY to INR292 crores on HAM/BOT monetisation; FY27 revenue growth guidance cut to 10-15% from 20%.
533271|2026-06.overview: Standalone total income was flat YoY at INR1,320 crores, with EBITDA down 17% to INR126 crores (9.5% margin) and PAT up 3% to INR31.5 crores. Consolidated total income fell 21% to INR1,534 crores, mainly because of BOT and HAM asset monetisation in Q3 FY26, and consolidated EBITDA fell 55% to INR292 crores (19.0% margin). Management cut FY27 revenue growth guidance to 10-15% from 20% and EBITDA margin to roughly 9-9.5% from about 10%. qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone PAT fall about 50% while consolidated PAT rose 6%?
qa_highlights.answer: The increase came mainly from RMIL (copper) and overseas subsidiaries.

qa_highlights.question: What is the copper sourcing plan and the US subsidiary's role?
qa_highlights.answer: The US subsidiary is a sourcing arm with no direct revenue. It will run its own yards, feeding copper and battery scrap to India. Capex is limited because yards are leased.

qa_highlights.question: Will lower-cost US sourcing hurt lead EBITDA per kg, and would lead capex be delayed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said US scrap may cost more than Africa, but it still meets internal ROCE targets. Capex will not be delayed while scrap is available for the next 3-4 years.

RMIL utilisation is stagnant; reaching 65-70% depends on debottlenecking and new machinery orders.

533293|2026-06.headline: KOEL Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 16% to INR1,461 crore, but EBITDA fell 4% and margin contracted to 11.2% on commodity costs and export weakness.
533293|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew 16% YoY to INR1,461 crore, led by domestic power gen (+18%), industrial (+19%) and distribution & aftermarket (+20%), while international fell 11% to INR106 crore. Standalone EBITDA declined 4% YoY to INR165 crore and margin compressed to 11.2% from 13.5%, which management attributed to lower export volumes, elevated commodity costs and a lag between cost inflation and price realisation. Standalone net profit fell 9% to INR99 crore. Consolidated revenue rose 13% to INR2,000 crore, with consolidated net profit down 17% to INR111 crore. Management said pricing actions have been taken across most businesses and expects profitability to improve as they flow through over coming quarters.

533326|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue fell 13.3% to INR1,167 crore, but PAT rose to INR58 crore; INR700 crore contingency provision taken from free reserves.
533326|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR1,167 crore (down 13.3% YoY), with EBITDA of about INR116 crore (~10% margin) and PAT of INR58 crore (5% margin, up 206 bps YoY). FY26 revenue fell 14% to INR4,377 crore, EBITDA was INR450 crore (10.2% margin) and PAT INR194 crore (4.4%). The company created a INR700 crore contingency provision charged to free reserves, which led to a qualified auditor report; management says it has no cash impact. Management also outlined a "Texmaco 2.0" Vision 2030 plan targeting 2x top line and mid-teen-plus EBITDA margins, and disclosed a large South Africa wagon and locomotive order (about INR4,000 crore) with delivery by FY28.

financial_highlights.change: Charged to free reserves; no cash impact
FY26 lower than record prior year

financial_highlights.value: 8,964 MT in Q4 FY26; ~34,000 MT in FY26

segments.name: Railways / wagons (Kalindee)
segments.commentary: Freight car deliveries of 2,196 in Q4 and 8,372 in FY26 were hit by wheel-set availability and global supply chain issues. Management says about 70% of the wagon order book is from private customers.

segments.name: Bright Power (electrification)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 66% to INR610 crore in FY26 with a 10.8% EBIT margin; management called the growth phenomenal for the future.

segments.name: Foundry
segments.commentary: Volume was 8,964 MT in Q4 and about 34,000 MT for FY26, with the year affected by supply chain disruptions and US tariffs.

segments.name: Defence / digital / real estate (new verticals)
segments.commentary: Board approved INR200 crore capex for defence; envelope for overall new-business capex cited at INR1,500-2,000 crore. A real estate division is being set up around surplus land, and the Invariz.ai GCC is being built as a future commercial AI service.

guidance_outlook: Management expects top-line and bottom-line growth in FY27 versus FY26, but declined to give specific revenue or EBITDA numbers.
Vision 2030 / Texmaco 2.0 targets doubling top line and EBITDA margins in the mid-teens or above, to be achieved in 12-36 months.
Management expects part of the INR700 crore contingency provision to be released as claims are realised and visibility on contracts improves.
Capex for new businesses is expected to be within INR1,500-2,000 crore, to be disclosed progressively; net debt-to-equity is expected to stay below about 0.2.
Management expects the South Africa order (about 2,200 wagons, 30 diesel locomotives, 15-year maintenance) to be delivered by FY28, with revenue largely in FY28 per management's answer.
Management expects a wagon requirement of about 25,000-30,000 over 5-7 years, plus replacement demand of 10,000-14,000 per year.
capex_capacity: Board approved INR200 crore capex for the defence business; total new-business capex envelope estimated at INR1,500-2,000 crore.
Management says it makes about 11 types of wagons and has a track record in 16 countries across multiple gauges.
Management says the company is moving from vehicle-count metrics to a volume-to-value approach.
Finance cost of about INR120 crore for the year includes bank guarantee commission charges, not just interest.
demand_pricing: South Africa order: about INR4,000 crore, 2,200 wagons and 30 diesel locomotives by FY28, including a 15-year maintenance component. Pricing covers the full life cycle.
Management declined to say whether the South Africa order has raw material pass-through or is fixed price, citing its envelope structure and localisation.
Management expects a Indian Railways wagon tender of 1.5-2 lakh wagons in the near term, but has not yet seen bids called.
Private-sector wagon market share is about 40-45%, with private demand estimated at 12,000-15,000 wagons a year on a consistent basis.
Management named Europeans and Chinese competitors in international bids, along with local competitors.
Wheel-set availability is currently adequate with Indian Railways capacity, but a policy decision on imports remains open.

qa_highlights.question: What visibility is there on new Indian Railways wagon orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no bids have been called yet, but expects 1.5-2 lakh wagons in the near term, with the first stage of about 1.3-1.4 lakh wagons already awarded in 2022-23.

qa_highlights.question: Is the South Africa order mostly FY28 revenue, and is FY27 softer?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said revenue will largely come in FY28 as things stand, and also reiterated that it expects top-line and bottom-line growth in FY27 versus FY26.

qa_highlights.question: How much capex is needed for the new businesses and how will it be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Defence capex of INR200 crore has been approved; the overall envelope is INR1,500-2,000 crore, to be updated as projects progress, and management expects leverage to stay within range.

qa_highlights.question: Who will build the locomotives for the South Africa order, and what is the pricing structure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has accepted the award but could not disclose the locomotive partner or pricing structure yet, citing disclosure constraints.

qa_highlights.question: What are the defence plans and when is the first commercial order expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said technology tie-ups are at an advanced stage in areas such as autonomous vehicles, could not disclose specifics, and expects a positive step within this financial year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the scope and timing of the wagon tender from Indian Railways?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 25,000-30,000 wagons over 5-7 years, which may come in one go or in tranches, but could not give a timing for the tender.

Heavy reliance on large claims that are pending with customers; management asked for patience on timing.
Wheel-set supply and any government decision on imports could constrain wagon output.
Timing of the Indian Railways wagon tender remains uncertain; management could not give a date.

Execution risk on new verticals (defence, real estate, Invariz.ai GCC, metro) and the INR1,500-2,000 crore capex envelope.

533326|2026-06.headline: Texmaco Q1 FY27 revenue fell to INR753 crore but PAT rose 85.9% YoY to INR52 crore; order book INR9,923 crore.
533326|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue from operations was INR753 crore, hit by lower freight car and Rail & Green execution, while Bright Power electrical revenue grew 76.8% YoY to INR175 crore. EBITDA was INR81 crore (10.8% margin), flat YoY, and PAT rose 85.9% YoY to INR52 crore (6.9% margin) on lower finance costs. Management said the order book stood at INR9,923 crore at June 30, 2026, with private and export orders at 96.4% of freight car orders in Q1 FY27. Strategic updates covered the leasing JV with Trinity (Texmaco stake to fall from 50% to 34%), the Wabtec air brake JV, a South Africa order of about INR4,100 crore, and a 2030 vision of doubling the top line.

segments.name: Freight Cars (FCD)
segments.commentary: 1,054 freight cars delivered in Q1 FY27; execution lower on supply-chain stress tied to oil and gas prices. Private and export share of orders rose from 21% in FY25 to 79% in FY26 and 96.4% in Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Rail Infra & Green (formerly Kalindee)
segments.commentary: Revenue lower YoY; EBIT margin turned positive at 1.4% versus an EBIT loss in Q1 FY26.

segments.name: Bright Power (Electrical infra)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR175 crore, +76.8% YoY; EBIT margin 10.8%, up 150 bps YoY.

segments.name: Foundry
segments.commentary: Production of 5,148 tonnes in the quarter.

guidance_outlook: Core business EBITDA margin target of 1.2% to 3% over the next 1 to 3 years (as stated by management; the figure is ambiguous in the transcript).
Vision 2030: core rolling stock revenue of INR5,000-6,000 crore; aim to double the top line to about 2x by 2030 with a steady bottom line in the mid-teens.
New businesses could add 20% to 50% top-line growth in some years; management would not give absolute FY27 or FY28 numbers.

South Africa order (about INR4,100 crore, wagons plus 15-year maintenance, which is 30-35% of value): about 50-60% expected to execute in FY28; locomotive value to be additional and not yet finalised.
Management expects freight car output and supply-chain normalisation to improve from coming quarters; no volume target given.
capex_capacity: Leasing: about 35 rakes operating today; near-term readiness to invest in about 100 more rakes. Leasing JV with Trinity: Texmaco stake falls from 50% to 34%; capital allocation to be modest in percentage terms.
Capacity described as elastic (15,000-16,000 commodity wagons possible), but management is prioritising specialised wagons over volume.
South Africa: considering a locomotive plant and a wagon manufacturing plant; management declined to confirm the INR200-300 crore reported investment figure.
Wheelset supply from Rail Wheel Factory: enough stock for current export and private orders.
demand_pricing: Order book INR9,923 crore at June 30, 2026, with more than 6,000 wagons in hand (per CFO).
Q1 FY27 order wins include about INR5,200 crore, of which the South Africa order is about INR4,100 crore; some export orders are under execution.
Management expects no Indian Railways wagon tender near term; it expects orders to come from private and export customers.
Other expenses rose because export freight charges are booked there while the related income is in revenue (CFO).

qa_highlights.question: Wagon leasing: is the report of about INR1,800 crore investment for about 100 rakes over 3-5 years correct?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not confirm figures; it said the leasing JV is separate from Texmaco, with Trinity entry cutting Texmaco's stake to 34%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the South Africa order exposure correct: a locomotive and wagon plant costing INR200-300 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not confirm the numbers; it said it is open to facilities for localisation and that footprint matters more than investment amount.

qa_highlights.question: Execution timeline for the INR5,200 crore order and the maintenance share?
qa_highlights.answer: The South Africa order is about INR4,100 crore, not INR5,200 crore, and is executable mainly in FY28; maintenance is 15 years and about 30-35% of value.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue and EBITDA guidance for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: No absolute guidance; management pointed to a core EBITDA margin target of 1.2% to 3% and possible 20-50% top-line growth from new businesses.

qa_highlights.question: Why did freight car output fall, and is there a 2030 roadmap?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed oil and gas-driven supply-chain stress and said order book is healthy; it reiterated Vision 2030 (2x top line, mid-teens bottom line).

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook as the mix moves to private and export orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margin is hard to predict and that it expects to sustain and improve margins, without giving a number.

Dependence on the South Africa order, which is lumpy and where the locomotive component is not yet finalised or partnered.
No Indian Railways wagon tender yet; management says it is insulated for now.
Leasing and new-business capital needs, and the reduced JV stake after the Trinity entry.
Freight car volumes fell YoY; watch Q2 deliveries and whether the margin gain holds as execution resumes.
Management declined to give FY27 and FY28 revenue or margin numbers; a call for clearer guidance.

533333|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 162% to INR314 crore and PAT 118% to INR44 crore, helped by the CrudeChem (CCT) acquisition.
533333|2026-03.overview: Fineotex reported Q4 FY26 revenue from operations of INR314 crore, up 162% YoY, with PAT of INR44 crore versus INR20 crore a year earlier, driven by the newly acquired US oilfield chemicals business CrudeChem Technologies Group (CCT). International revenue rose to 70% of the mix and ROIC was stated at 31%. Management said Q4 is the base for future growth, is doubling CCT's manufacturing capacity, and targets a $200 million CCT revenue run-rate before 2028 and a blended EBITDA of 18-20%. Non-CCT textile volumes were said to be recovering, with textile specialty up about 8% YoY in Q4.

financial_highlights.change: Increased significantly, no prior figure given
Cited by analyst; not disputed by management

segments.name: Oil & Gas specialty chemicals (CCT)
segments.commentary: Management said oil specialty chemicals were about 55-60% of Q4 revenue by value, with annualised Q4 run-rate of about $90-100 million. Capacity is being doubled at CCT, with Midland expansion and new machinery ordered.

segments.name: Specialty textile chemicals (Fineotex, Ambernath)
segments.commentary: Textile share of total revenue fell to about 35-36%, though textile revenue grew in value. Textile specialty volumes were up about 8% YoY in Q4 and about 15% in volume per a later clarification.

segments.name: FMCG and hygiene chemicals
segments.commentary: No segment-specific figures were given on the call; management said other industries grew faster than textile.

guidance_outlook: CCT revenue target of $200 million, now brought forward to before 2028 from an earlier 2030 timeline; management declined to give FY27/FY28 revenue guidance.
Blended consolidated EBITDA target of 18-20%, which management said could be reflected within FY27; CCT EBITDA comfortably around 15%.
Stake: founders to sell a further 25% of CCT to Fineotex in January 2028, taking the holding to about 79-80% (currently about 53%).
Analyst-framed scale-up to INR3,000 crore top line in 3-4 years was not refuted; management said it would be surprised if not reached.
Working capital tolerated up to 90 days; management said current 79 days is at par with industry.
capex_capacity: CCT capacity doubling in progress; a large order of machines placed, with installation expected within a couple of weeks of the call.
Fineotex spent about $7 million capex post-acquisition and extended about $7 million more to CCT for further investment.

Subsidiary in Ras Al Khaimah, UAE, was set up for a plant but has not started; Middle East options are being explored, including inorganic routes.
demand_pricing: Management said the textile industry environment was stable with healthy demand; FY26 textile exports grew 2.1% YoY to $3.16 trillion (as stated on the call), with the India-US trade deal and UK and EU trade frameworks cited as tailwinds.
North American oilfield demand is rising, with Guyana, Suriname and Venezuela cited as new areas; management said the addressable market is about $3.5-4 billion.
Pricing: management said raw material cost increases are passed on to customers; inventory is held for 1-2 months. Logistics and freight costs were a challenge in Q4 and April.

Competitive moat is described as technical services, last-mile delivery, weather-specific customisation and customer qualification taking around 2 years; management said wallet share could rise 5x with existing customers.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the annualised Q4 run-rate is $90-100 million and it is confident of $200 million before 2028; EBITDA is expected to be comfortably around 15%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CCT revenue guidance for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give forward-looking numbers and said Q4 FY26 is the base set for going forward.

qa_highlights.question: What blended consolidated EBITDA is achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets a blended 18-20%, with the Fineotex operations historically at 18-28% EBITDA, and said this could be reflected within FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CCT stake roadmap?
qa_highlights.answer: The founders have agreed to sell a further 25% by January 2028, taking Fineotex to about 79-80%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital outlook and cash flow impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital is about 79 days, with management saying up to 90 days is acceptable. Management said the reported operating cash flow was reduced by a one-time acquisition-related entry in the accounts.

qa_highlights.question: What are CrudeChem's Q4 numbers and steady-state revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: CrudeChem Q4 revenue was approximately INR165-170 crore. Management agreed that a steady-state top line of INR600-650 crore was easily achievable, with no seasonality in the business.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a plan for revenue of INR3,000 crore in 3-4 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said organic growth plus CCT and Ambernath could reach 3-4x current scale, and it would be surprised if INR3,000 crore was not touched.

qa_highlights.question: What is the raw material and pricing situation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cost increases are passed on to customers, with no contracts, and the worst of the logistics disruption is behind them. It gave no quantified basket-level price change.

533333|2026-06.headline: Fineotex Q1 FY27 total income rose 165% YoY to INR 386.72 crore, with EBITDA of INR 59.14 crore at a 15.70% margin, driven by the US CrudeChem consolidation.
533333|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 consolidated total income was INR 386.72 crore against INR 146.62 crore a year earlier, mainly from a full quarter of the US operations (CrudeChem Technologies Group, CCTL). EBITDA rose 134.7% YoY to INR 59.14 crore, with margin at 15.70% versus 13.93% in the prior quarter, and PAT grew 92.67% to INR 48.21 crore. The Texas plant capacity was expanded to about 148,000 MTPA, with utilisation stated at about 63%. Management declined to give a fixed margin guidance, while reiterating USD 100 million (FY27) and USD 200 million (FY28) targets for the oil and gas segment.

segments.name: Oil and gas specialty chemicals (CCTL, US)
segments.commentary: Management said about 65% of revenue and about 55% of volume come from oil and gas, roughly INR 250 crore in the quarter. The Texas plant is now about 148,000 MTPA, and management said it is utilised at about 63%.

segments.name: Textile specialty chemicals (India, standalone business)
segments.commentary: Management said the base business is about INR 132 crore after deducting CCTL from consolidated revenue, against INR 137 crore in Q1 FY26, a 1-2% dip that it attributed to monsoon seasonality and competition. Management said pricing was passed on and that the textile business is flattish.

guidance_outlook: Oil and gas segment targets of USD 100 million in FY27 and USD 200 million in FY28, which management said are driven by order book and customer expectations rather than crude prices. Management said it expects the target to be reached by December 2028.
Management said it expects the Texas plant to be fully utilised within the coming few quarters, with scope to add a second shift.
Management said it has no fixed consolidated EBITDA margin guidance. It reiterated the aspiration of 18% margin but did not commit to it.

533344|2026-03.overview: FY26 showed a sharp pickup in sanctions (INR3,448 crores, over 4x FY25) and disbursements (INR1,235 crores, up 35%), with PAT up about 47% to INR319 crores. Asset quality improved materially: gross Stage III fell to INR190 crores and net Stage III to INR47 crores, with provision coverage on Stage III at 75%. AUM moderated to INR3,292 crores as low-yield legacy loans prepaid (INR1,105 crores of unscheduled prepayments), and Q4 profitability softened with RoNW at 6.24% and portfolio yield at 10.29%. Leadership change (MD and CEO R. Balaji resigned, effective after 30 June) and the absence of a dividend dominated investor questions.

segments.name: Infrastructure finance (renewable, transmission, DISCOM, oil and gas, roads, CBG, data centre)
segments.commentary: All FY26 disbursements went to private corporate borrowers; sanctions were mainly private, with one or two utility sanctions where returns are acceptable. Structured finance (value chain) is being built to lift yield over the medium term.

segments.name: Stage III / legacy resolution
segments.commentary: Major part of the INR190 crores gross Stage III is Danu Wind Parks, referred to NCLT; promoters have offered an OTS that will be considered on merits. About 73% of gross Stage III accounts by value transitioned out during the year.

guidance_outlook: Management expects at least 30% to 50% YoY AUM growth (disbursements minus repayments), with quality prioritised over quantity.
About INR2,000 crores of sanctioned amount is undisbursed; roughly INR1,500 crores expected in the next two quarters, with major portion in Q2 FY27.
FY27 disbursement target of INR4,000 crores is not yet set; budget is awaiting approval and is framed on yield and RoA, not volume.
Cost of funds expected to fall as fresh borrowings replace older, higher-cost debt; PFS base rate was cut by 60 bps in the last quarter.
No dividend declared; the board will review it next quarter. Management acknowledged a suggestion for a dividend at the annual meeting.
capex_capacity: Sanctions-to-disbursement gap is structural: infrastructure projects run 6 months to 3.5 years, so disbursement follows construction progress.
Liquidity of about INR1,800 crores on balance sheet; borrowing deferred until required, with ALCO matching disbursement needs.
Average tenure of new project loans cited at 5 to 7 years.
Prepayments of INR1,105 crores and total repayments of INR1,441 crores in FY26; prepayments were low-yield legacy loans and are not predictable.
demand_pricing: Management says new disbursements are at higher yields than prepaid loans, so portfolio yield is expected to improve.
Q4 FY26 portfolio yield fell to 10.29% from 11.27%, which management attributed to portfolio dynamics and calibrated growth.
Sole and multiple lending structures are being prioritised over consortium lending, though PFS also participates in consortium and co-lending on a case-by-case basis.
Net NPA stated at 1.49%, with gross NPA INR190 crores and net NPA INR47 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the gap between sanctions (about INR3,500 crores) and disbursements (about INR1,200 crores) so large?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said infrastructure projects are disbursed as construction progresses over 1 to 3 years, so sanctions convert to disbursement later. Past lack of a sanctioned pipeline also explains the current low disbursement.

qa_highlights.question: Why did R. Balaji resign, and is the FY27 disbursement vision still on track?
qa_highlights.answer: The company said the resignation was for personal reasons already disclosed; the MD and CEO remains until 30 June and a replacement process has started. The FY27 target of about INR4,000 crores was not committed and is pending budget approval.

qa_highlights.question: Why is borrowing cost high at around 9.5%, and what is the guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cost of borrowing is below 9.5%, that the treasury is pressing lenders for spread cuts, and that the base rate was cut 60 bps. Cost of funds should fall as new, cheaper borrowings replace older debt.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company declare a dividend, and what is the NTPC promoter impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Dividend has not been declared; the board will review it next quarter. Management said no formal intimation on the NTPC shareholding change has been received and no adverse impact is expected.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company holding cash rather than disbursing, and is this a fundraising issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it holds about INR1,800 crores of liquidity, will borrow only when needed to match asset-liability timing, and has about INR2,000 crores of pipeline to disburse over the next six months.

qa_highlights.question: What are the INR190 crores gross Stage III accounts, and what is the status?
qa_highlights.answer: Kalur Srinivas said the major portion is Danu Wind Parks, referred to NCLT, with the promoters having offered an OTS that will be considered on merits; updates will be given to exchanges.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for AUM growth over the next two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to at least 30% to 50% YoY AUM growth, stating that AUM means disbursements minus repayments, and said no fresh slippage has occurred in the last eight years of disbursements.

533344|2026-06.headline: PFS Q1 FY27 disbursements fell to INR 117 crores with PAT of INR 40.24 crores; management says Q2 sanctions exceed INR 1,200 crores in month one.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said losses were concentrated in sub-INR 30,000 tickets (about 5 lakh under INR 10,000 and about 8 lakh in INR 10,000-30,000), offset by higher-ticket additions. It described this as normal churn in a mature portfolio, not competitive loss.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company cut rates to win customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has different schemes at 12-23% yields and will step up lower-yield lending when needed, but sees no need now. Median-term ROI guidance of around 3.5% was referenced.

qa_highlights.question: AUM guidance for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone AUM guidance of 15%, given in Q1 as always; to be reviewed after Q1 or Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why set up gold lending in a subsidiary (Muthoot Money) rather than expanding the parent after RBI approval requirements were removed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to explain and said it is a board decision for the subsidiary.

qa_highlights.question: How does the new RBI LTV framework affect the company?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company has always followed RBI LTV limits, and the new framework allows up to 85% on EMI products. It is building software and has rolled out some products, with strategy to be reviewed after Q1.

533470|2026-03.headline: Rushil Decor FY26 consolidated EBITDA fell to INR 801 million (9.3% margin) after Q1 fire disruption; Q4 margin recovered to 12.4%.
533470|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a difficult year: a fire at the Andhra Pradesh MDF facility disrupted Q1 production, and resin/raw material inflation, export logistics issues and Middle East shipping disruption weighed on the year. Consolidated FY26 revenue from operations was INR 8,622 million with EBITDA of INR 801 million (9.3%) and PAT of INR 64 million. Q4 FY26 showed sequential recovery, with revenue of INR 2,309 million (up 6.6% QoQ) and EBITDA of INR 286 million (12.4% margin). Management implemented MDF price increases of 15% and Laminate price increases of 10% effective 1 April 2026, mainly to recover cost inflation.

financial_highlights.value: INR 159 million (6.9% margin) / INR 101 million (4.4% margin)

financial_highlights.change: Decline attributed to Q1 production loss and lower MDF exports

financial_highlights.value: INR 2,544 million; net debt to equity 0.39

segments.name: MDF
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 6,091 million and EBITDA INR 601 million (9.9%). Q4 revenue INR 1,668 million, EBITDA INR 233 million (14% margin); India MDF revenue up 37.3% YoY in Q4 and 12.5% for FY26; blended realisation up 9.7% YoY in Q4. Capacity utilisation 83% in Q4, 75% for FY26.

segments.name: Laminates
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 2,111 million (+6.1% YoY), EBITDA INR 182 million (8.6%). Q4 revenue INR 534 million, EBITDA INR 41 million (7.7%). Domestic revenue +21% YoY for FY26; blended realisation +7.5%, export realisation +13.7%. Utilisation above 91% in Q4 and above 89% for FY26.

segments.commentary: Both phases now operational with 28 lakh sheets per annum capacity (per analyst). Products sold to Russia, Portugal, Slovakia, Romania, Israel, Kosovo and others; brands VIR KLADS, VIR TOPAZ, VIR VAULT. Customer onboarding is long due to certification requirements. Management expects FY27 utilisation of 60-65%, rising to 85% in FY28.

guidance_outlook: Management declined to give numeric FY27/FY28 revenue or EBITDA guidance; four stated priorities: value-added products to 50% of MDF volumes and 60% of MDF revenue (FY26: 42% volume, 54% value), scaling Jumbo Laminates, raising utilisation to about 90% across the year, and aggressive cost optimisation.
Q1 FY27 capacity utilisation expected to be in the range of Q4 FY26 levels (about 83% MDF, above 91% Laminates).
MDF EBITDA margin currently about 8%; target of 10-12% for MDF, driven by value-added mix.
Laminate business EBITDA target of 10-12% on average, with wide range across Jumbo SKUs.
No new debt planned in FY27; scheduled repayment of around INR 50 crores in FY27.

Management estimated Jumbo Laminate potential revenue at 28 lakh sheets x 85% x INR 4,000 per sheet (about INR 950 crores at full utilisation, as per the analyst's arithmetic); management did not confirm the INR 900 crore figure and said it depends on product mix.
capex_capacity: Jumbo Laminate: both phases operational; one facility underwent a major machinery upgrade in April 2026, production ramping up.
Jumbo thickness range 2.1 mm to 18-19 mm versus 0.6 mm to 1.9 mm for conventional laminates; management cited average realisation around INR 4,000 per sheet.

Laminate utilisation above 91% in Q4 FY26 and above 89% for FY26.
Product mix (approx.): MDF 75%, Laminates 20%, WPC 5%; Jumbo expected to raise laminate share over time.
Management expects three new MDF plants industry-wide this financial year, implying oversupply pressure.
demand_pricing: MDF price hike of 15% and Laminate price hike of 10% from 1 April 2026; management said the hike only offsets cost, with no incremental margin intended.
Chemical prices up roughly 40% since the Middle East conflict began; net impact about 10% of selling price, or about 11% total cost increase per management.
Industry MDF demand CAGR cited at 15-18%; management assumes 650-800 cubic metres per year of new capacity can be absorbed, but sees oversupply near term.

Export: company is not exposed to the US tariffs; laminates are the bulk of exports (Europe, Russia, Western Europe, Baltics, CALA). MDF exports were lower due to Middle East dependence and a calibrated export approach.
Distribution network: 67 new direct distributors and more than 131 retailers and dealers added in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What will capacity utilisation look like in Q1 FY27 across plants?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 would be in the range of Q4 FY26 levels; MDF exports are under pressure, so domestic sales are being pushed, and a Jumbo facility machinery upgrade completed in April is ramping up.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue or EBITDA guidance for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: No numeric guidance; management instead listed four priorities: 50% value-added share, scaling Jumbo, 90% utilisation and cost optimisation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current net debt and FY27-28 debt outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt (after cash) went from INR 262 crore (Mar 2025) to INR 254 crore (Mar 2026), including about INR 9 crore euro FX impact; about INR 50 crore scheduled repayment in FY27 and no new debt planned.

qa_highlights.question: Jumbo Laminate realisation and potential revenue at full utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said realisation around INR 4,000 per sheet on average, with utilisation up to 85%; the analyst's 28 lakh sheets x 85% x INR 4,000 math was confirmed as correct, though management later said the calculation overstates output because higher thicknesses yield fewer sheets.

qa_highlights.question: Is the MDF price hike purely cost recovery or margin-accretive?
qa_highlights.answer: Purely cost recovery: chemical costs up about 40%, net about 10% of selling price, so total cost up about 11%; no additional margin is being earned.

qa_highlights.question: Steady-state MDF realisation and EBITDA margin for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Current MDF EBITDA margin about 8%; target 10-12% through higher value-added mix; value-added share missed target slightly in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Jumbo volume, revenue and margin targets for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation targeted at 60-65% in FY27 and up to 85% in FY28; Laminate-business EBITDA target 10-12% on average, with wide margin range by SKU.

qa_highlights.question: Industry demand-supply and MDF capacity additions?
qa_highlights.answer: Three new plants expected this financial year, implying oversupply; management was not aware of unorganised-sector capacity closures.

risks_watch: Oversupply from three new industry MDF plants in FY27 could pressure pricing and utilisation despite the 15% MDF price hike.
Raw material risk: chemical/resin costs up about 40% since the Middle East conflict; formaldehyde supplier and pricing details were not disclosed.
Export exposure to Middle East shipping disruption; MDF export volumes remain subdued.
Jumbo Laminates ramp is slow: long certification cycles; FY27 utilisation target of 60-65% is well below the 85% long-term assumption.
Euro FX exposure contributed about INR 9 crore to net debt increase; FY27 scheduled repayment about INR 50 crore.

533470|2026-06.headline: Rushil Decor Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 27.8% YoY to INR 2,920 mn, but EBITDA margin was 7.9% and PAT only INR 20 mn amid input cost and freight pressure.
533470|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 27.8% YoY, driven by normalised Andhra Pradesh MDF operations and a 65.3% jump in laminate revenue. Gross margin was 39% and EBITDA INR 182 mn (7.9% margin), but profitability was hit by elevated resin/chemical costs, higher freight and West Asia shipping disruption. Management said prices are now sustainable with no further hikes beyond the taken ones, and debt is on a schedule to be cleared around FY29 with no major capex beyond maintenance.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR 110 mn (+25% YoY), volume ~1.13 lakh sheets (+20.4%), EBITDA INR 23 mn (20.6%). Management puts utilisation at 29% on a 1 mm-equivalent basis against 28 lakh sheets capacity.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR 96 mn (+13.1% YoY), volume +6.9%, EBITDA INR 8 mn (7.9% margin).

guidance_outlook: Jumbo laminate utilisation aspiration: ~50-55% in FY27 and 70-75% next year; ~60% utilisation would give ~INR 75 cr revenue, 90% ~INR 140 cr (Phase 1 + Phase 2).

Jumbo utilisation 29% currently, aspiration 55-60% in FY27 (per call; reconcile with 50-55% stated later), 70-75% next year.

Laminate plant had a single-boiler constraint after Jumbo capacity was added in one plant, reducing output in Q1.

Resin prices up ~35-40% vs pre-war; wood prices flat; resin easing in July described as 'very marginal'.
MDF OEM share 35-40% of domestic volume; OEM and retail prices currently the same; no fixed-price long-term OEM contracts.
Export MDF held back by container shortage and high freight; orders in hand but customers must approve higher freight before shipment.

Laminate domestic volume growth 15-20%; export growth from new Far East customers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the MDF OEM vs retail split and how did it move in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: OEM is 35-40% of domestic volume, rest via distribution and retail; the mix in Q1 was the same as Q4 per management.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Jumbo laminate utilisation and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is 29% on a 1 mm-equivalent basis; capex was ~INR 90 cr for 28 lakh sheets; full-potential revenue ~INR 140 cr at 90% utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Why did MDF volume stay flat YoY and why were exports low?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the planned April shutdown, elevated chemical prices causing buyers to hold back, and West Asia disruption; exports were ~255 CBM due to container shortage and high freight.

qa_highlights.question: Will further price hikes be taken to offset input inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no hikes beyond 15% (MDF) and 10% (laminate); market will not accept more, so no guidance on further hikes.

qa_highlights.question: When will the consolidated EBITDA margin reach 10-12%?
qa_highlights.answer: Aspiration is this quarter, but realistically 1-2 quarters more.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path to full potential revenue (~INR 1,100 cr)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no FY27 revenue guidance; said laminate normal turnover ~INR 200 cr could reach INR 250 cr and Jumbo will take time, with no guidance given for the total.

risks_watch: Input cost pressure: resin up ~35-40% vs pre-war with only 'very marginal' easing in July; management says the market will not accept further price hikes, so margin recovery depends on resin and chemical prices.

qa_highlights.question: How exposed is the book to the West Asia conflict (SME, personal loans, rural, tractor, two-wheeler), and is the 20%+ FY27 AUM growth guidance inclusive of these risks?
qa_highlights.answer: No visible West Asia impact yet on SME, Rural Business Finance, tractor or two-wheeler portfolios; caution on Kharif fertiliser supply and urban unsecured lending. 20%+ AUM growth guidance stands but excludes unforeseen later geopolitical shocks.

qa_highlights.question: What are the near-term and Lakshya 2031 cost ratio expectations, and how was the ECL refresh's contingency buffer treated?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex to book guided at 3.75%-4% over Lakshya, reflecting tech and branch investment. Management said the ₹125 Cr macro-prudential provision was subsumed into the ECL model (Stage 1 and 2), not released, and that it will keep building macro-prudential provisions as needed.

qa_highlights.question: Why is fee income tepid relative to disbursement growth, and will it grow in line with AUM?
qa_highlights.answer: Fee income is about 1.7%-1.9% of assets and is range-bound; liquidity income and negative carry sit in interest cost, not MTM. Management guides to the combined NIMs+Fees range of 10%-10.5% rather than standalone fees.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Stage 1 provision at 80 bps apply to incremental FY27 book, and does it change the FY27 credit cost outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, new Stage 1 build-up will be provided at 80 bps as a permanent assumption change. Management said the FY27 credit cost outlook of 2%-2.2% is unchanged because lower roll-forwards should more than offset higher provisioning on book growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is the sub-2% credit cost under Lakshya 2031 driven by product mix or by Cyclops, and when does it arrive?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly Cyclops-driven customer selection, applied first to two-wheeler, tractor and SME. Management is confident of reaching 2% or below sometime in FY28, but could not pinpoint the quarter. Two-wheeler prime share is about 90%, up from 65%, and monthly originations rose from ₹650 Cr to about ₹1,000 Cr.

qa_highlights.question: Are disbursement yields above portfolio yields, and what drives yield improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: Disbursement yields are higher than portfolio yields. Personal loan yields are 2%-2.5 pp above the industry salaried average. Two-wheeler industry yields are 16%-18%. Yield improvement is coming from mix shift: home loan to LAP mix moved from about 80/20 to 55/45, with gold, micro-LAP and PL accelerating.

risks_watch: West Asia conflict: possible fertiliser supply constraint for Kharif, industrial gas tightness hitting SMEs, and higher oil prices pressuring urban unsecured lending (PL and SME).

533519|2026-06.headline: L&T Finance posted record Q1 FY27 PAT of ₹902 Cr (up 29% YoY) with RoA of 2.48% and credit cost easing to 2.54%.
533519|2026-06.overview: Consolidated PAT hit a record ₹902 Cr, up 29% YoY, while the consolidated book reached ₹1,29,634 Cr, up 27% YoY. Retail disbursements were ₹23,852 Cr, up 36% YoY, though management said it deliberately let go of about ₹1,000–1,200 Cr of potential disbursements to protect asset quality. Credit cost moderated 10 bps sequentially to 2.54%, and NIMs + Fees was flat QoQ at 10.47%, with NIM down 24 bps offset by higher fee and other income. Management reiterated Lakshya 2031 targets (RoA 3.0–3.2%, RoE 16–18%, credit cost ≤2% over the period) and set a near-term 2.8% RoA goal for Q4 FY27.
