Personal loans disbursements ₹4,380 Cr (up 126%, record), book ₹16,917 Cr (up 80%). Mortgage disbursements ₹3,401 Cr (up 22%), book ₹31,630 Cr (up 20%).

qa_highlights.question: Why did NIM fall while fee and other income rose, and is the NIMs + Fees trajectory sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Sachinn Joshi said NIM fell 24 bps to 8.54% as debt-equity rose to 3.97x from 3.73x and surplus liquidity of ~₹4,200 Cr was held; yields rose 1 bp. Surplus income was booked in fee and other income, so NIMs + Fees stayed at 10.47%.

qa_highlights.question: What guardrails govern Personal loan growth, and why were SME and Gold disbursements slower?
qa_highlights.answer: Sudipta Roy said PL is predominantly salaried, with Cyclops and credit parameters improving each quarter; the high growth reflects a low base. SME was cut in some cohorts due to West Asia war concerns; Gold origination fell in April on new RBI tiered-loan guardrails, with recovery in May–June.

qa_highlights.question: How will cost of funds move, and what is the funding strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Q2 up 5–7 bps and FY27 WACB of 7.35–7.40% vs 7.35% in FY26. Liquidity was cut to ~₹9,000 Cr at quarter end; PSL and domestic borrowing remain the main sources, with international funding deferred for now.

qa_highlights.question: How will the ~80 bps RoA gap to Lakshya be closed, and what is the insurance commission risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Sudipta Roy said ~20 bps comes from ARC drag fading over 2–3 years, 30–40 bps from credit and credit-administration cost, and a small part from expansion. Insurance commission changes were called an industry-wide issue; payments revenue expected only after 2–2.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the El Nino and monsoon risk to rural portfolio and asset quality?
qa_highlights.answer: Sudipta Roy said rainfall was ~14% below normal as of 10 July, versus an IMD projection of ~10% deficit, with reservoirs at acceptable levels outside a few South India locations. He sees the worries as overdone, citing microfinance deleveraging from ₹4.4 lakh Cr to ₹3.3 lakh Cr.

qa_highlights.question: Is the wholesale GS3 increase a risk to credit cost, and what is the SR/ARC position?
qa_highlights.answer: Sachinn Joshi said the small GS3 rise is a settlement transition already provided for and will reverse next quarter; the rest of the wholesale book (~₹2,000 Cr) is standard. SR PCR rose to 68% from 58%; credit cost guidance excludes wholesale slippage.

qa_highlights.question: How much AI spend is variable, and what is the opex trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management could not give the variable AI share on the call and offered to follow up offline. Head-count efficiencies are expected to show in FY29–FY30, with the next two to three quarters not very sharp.

Monsoon and El Nino effects on Farmer and Tractor portfolios, and on rural collections.

Gold and SME growth slowed in Q1 and recovery depends on the RBI tiered-loan guardrails and West Asia-linked sector stress.

But the NIMs, you can stay assured that if you looked at last almost 2.5 years and 3 years, we have been giving the guidance and we have stuck by that.

533520|2026-03.headline: Indiabulls FY26 PAT of INR346 crores; Q4 FY26 PAT INR195 crores (INR194.26 crores per correction) led by first real estate revenue recognition.

533758|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 volume fell ~20% QoQ to 745,000 tons, but EBITDA per ton held near INR5,500 and management reiterates 20% FY27 absolute EBITDA growth.

segments.commentary: Priced about 6-7% below APL Apollo brand at around INR58,000/ton; EBITDA spread INR0-1,000/ton depending on micro-market. Volumes fell due to the primary-secondary price gap (INR10-12/kg currently).

533758|2026-09.headline: APL Apollo Q2 FY27 volume hit 960,000 tons with EBITDA near Rs 6,000/ton; management guides FY27 EBITDA up 20%, with the 15% volume target conditional on Dubai and steel supply.

Management guided FY27 EBITDA growth of about 20% on an absolute basis and said Q2 EBITDA per ton of about Rs 6,000 is sustainable. segments.name: SG Premium

rows.why: Dubai runs at about 40% of past volume (~100k t/yr vs ~300k t capacity), with exports blocked and management unable to commit on timing; recovery is needed for the Rs 2,400 crore FY27 upside.

rows.label: Power cost to Rs 5/unit
rows.why: Power is at Rs 6.2-6.3/unit against a Rs 5 target next year, and freight is already down Rs 150/ton in the quarter.

tone.note: Management was confident on the APL Apollo brand, roofing, October trading and the 20% FY27 EBITDA growth, but evasive on company-wide volume, Dubai timing and SG Premium, while analysts pressed on the 4% H1 volume growth versus the earlier 15% target and the revised guidance.

533761|2026-03.headline: GPT Infra FY26 consolidated revenue rose 8.6% to INR1,290 crores, below guidance, while consolidated EBITDA grew 28.5% to INR174.2 crores; FY27 revenue growth guided at 27-30%.
533761|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone revenue grew 1.3% YoY to INR373.9 crores, while consolidated revenue grew 8.9% to INR414.7 crores; management attributed the March shortfall to West Bengal elections and labour migration. Margins improved, with standalone Q4 EBITDA up 27% to INR53 crores at 14% margin and consolidated Q4 EBITDA up 53% to INR59.2 crores, helped by the Ghana factory. The Alcon signalling EPC acquisition (INR151.83 crores cash) closed in the quarter and is being merged into GPT Infra with an appointed date of April 1, 2026. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 27-30%, order inflow of about INR3,000 crores and consolidated EBITDA margin of around 14%.

segments.name: Infrastructure
segments.commentary: Contributed more than 90% of FY26 revenue; key executing projects include Prayagraj Ganga Bridge, Kona Expressway and Raniganj. Alcon signalling will be reported within the infra line item.

segments.name: Concrete sleepers
segments.commentary: Management said the segment was profitable in FY26 on domestic demand and African operations. Q4 was loss-making in South Africa, Namibia and Ghana, which management attributed mainly to currency mark-to-market effects; Ghana production has started.

segments.name: Signalling (Alcon, acquired)
segments.commentary: Margin of about 20% vs 13-14% for traditional infra; FY27 revenue expected at INR120-130 crores. Order book is about INR90-100 crores; FY27 order inflow expected at INR150-200 crores against about INR500 crores of bids.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 27-30%, subject to Middle East war-related economic headwinds; long-term revenue growth target above 20%.
FY27 order inflow guidance of about INR3,000 crores across infra, signalling and sleepers.
Consolidated EBITDA margin guided at about 14% for FY27, with long-term standalone and consolidated margin above 13%.
West Bengal catch-up expected: April subdued again due to elections, Q1 not fully caught up, but first half expected to recover the shortfall.
Average capex of about INR70-75 crores a year for the next couple of years including the HAM equity share of INR55-60 crores; equipment purchases of INR40-50 crores a year.
Alcon and GPT merger (appointed date April 1, 2026) expected to complete in FY27, subject to regulatory approvals.
capex_capacity: Acquired Alcon Builders and Engineers (New Delhi EPC signalling) for INR151.83 crores cash; wholly owned subsidiary from January 1, 2026.
First HAM contract (elevated bypass, Jodhpur, NHAI), contract value about INR669 crores; GPT holds 51% in the SPV, which is already incorporated.
Steel girder fabrication factory at Singur, West Bengal, started during the year with about 10,000 tonnes per annum capacity; further expansion under review.
Ghana facility commercially operational, with first supply and invoice raised in March 2026.
demand_pricing: Order inflow of INR2,422 crores in FY26, and about INR500 crores of Alcon signalling bids in the last two months; Alcon contracts of INR70-80 crores individually.

Major wins: Northern Railway rail-cum-road bridge over Ganga at Varanasi, INR1,201 crores total (GPT share 40%, about INR481 crores); MCGM LBS Marg flyover, INR1,805 crores total (JV share 26%, about INR470 crores).
Price escalation formulas in all contracts, linked to SAIL/RINL steel, WPI for cement and fuel; NHAI and MoRTH moved to monthly escalation payments and allowed a 4-month force majeure extension.
Management said about 40% of revenue comes from West Bengal, and migrant labour returning from there was disrupted in March and April.

qa_highlights.question: Why did contract assets rise from INR336 crores to about INR514 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR60-65 crores is from Alcon (retention, unbilled revenue, escalation), with the rest from EPC milestone-based billing; contract assets are typically 6-8 months old and are targeted to fall to 3-4 months of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Where did the QIP proceeds go, given limited debt reduction?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt was cut by about INR125-130 crores from March 2024 to March 2025; FY26 debt rose on EPC working-capital drawdowns and internal accruals used for the Alcon purchase, with debt expected to return to the earlier level.

qa_highlights.question: Did West Bengal elections cause the revenue guidance miss, and does Alcon's INR140 crores contribute?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed March execution was hit by elections and labour migration; the Alcon contribution in FY26 was only Q4 numbers of about INR30 crores, since it was consolidated from January 1.

qa_highlights.question: Is labour back and is there execution risk to FY27 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: April was again subdued by elections, but May execution is strong and labour is back on site; new contracts won in December and January are expected to contribute heavily in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How will raw material inflation from the war affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Contracts carry escalation formulas; NHAI now pays escalation monthly, so a lag is possible, but management expects full-year margins to be maintained.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex plans and is Alcon consolidated separately?
qa_highlights.answer: Average capex about INR70-75 crores a year including the HAM share; Alcon is consolidated and, after the merger, will report within the infra segment rather than as a separate line.

risks_watch: Revenue growth of 27-30% in FY27 depends on recovering the March and April shortfall in the first half; April was subdued again by elections.
Middle East war effects on metal and fuel prices, currency and government payment timing; escalation may lag by a month.

Contract assets at about INR514 crores (consolidated) and debt increase in FY26 against the QIP deconsolidation narrative; working-capital conversion of 75-80% of contract assets in H1 FY27 is targeted.
Concrete sleeper segment losses in South Africa, Namibia and Ghana, driven by currency volatility.
Signalling order inflow of INR150-200 crores in FY27 against the INR500 crores of bids; execution of the Alcon merger subject to regulatory approvals.
Q4 revenue was 40% H2-weighted seasonality; management said it cannot be removed from the business.
533761|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on FY27 growth, margins and order inflow, with a clear explanation of the election-related shortfall. Management was more guarded when asked about faster growth, citing the Middle East war and reliance on government payments. Answers on debt reduction and contract-asset build-up were thinner and deferred to offline follow-up.
key_quotes: We are confident of achieving a long-term growth in the -- in revenue in excess of 20%, with revenue this year expected to cross 27% to 30% for the year, subject to the headwinds with respect to the economic conditions on account of the war in the Middle East.
The signaling business has a margin profile of almost 20% compared to the 13% / 14% for the traditional infra business that we were doing.
So we don't anticipate much of a -- so a lot of these contracts that you're referring to INR2,400-odd crores are contracts that we have received in the last financial year.

rows.why: FY27 revenue growth guided at 27-30% on an INR4,476 crore order book (about 3.5x FY26 revenue), Alcon signalling revenue of INR120-130 crore, and May execution described as strong with labour back on site.

rows.why: Debt rose in FY26 on EPC working-capital drawdowns and Alcon purchase funding (INR151.83 crore), reversing the INR125-130 crore cut from March 2024 to March 2025; management said debt will return to the earlier level, which is a rise rather than a reduction.

533761|2026-06.headline: GPT Infra Q1 FY27 standalone revenue fell 9% to INR282 crores on West Bengal labour disruption, while consolidated EBITDA margin rose to 15.7% on Alcon signalling.
533761|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue declined 9% YoY to INR282 crores due to labour unavailability in West Bengal during April-May elections, which management says has since normalised. Consolidated revenue fell 3.4% to INR302 crores, but consolidated EBITDA rose 28.4% to INR47.5 crores (15.7% margin), helped by the Alcon signalling business and African operations. Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth of about 30% and raised its FY27 EBITDA margin expectation to 14-15%, with 13-14% as the long-term range. Order book stood at INR4,303 crores and Q1 order inflow was only about INR130 crores against a INR3,000 crore annual target.

segments.name: Infrastructure
segments.commentary: Largest contributor at INR283 crores in Q1, driven by railway bridges and road projects (NHAI Ganga Bridge Prayagraj, Rupnarayan Bridge Kolaghat, Kona Expressway).

segments.name: Sleeper
segments.commentary: INR19 crores revenue in Q1, supported by domestic demand, export orders from India to Bangladesh and international operations; management cites 14-15% sleeper margin.

segments.name: Alcon (signalling)
segments.commentary: Acquired Q4 FY26; contributed about INR20 crores in Q1 and management guides INR100-120 crores for FY27, implying roughly INR70-80 crores incremental YoY per management.

segments.name: Power EPC (new)
segments.commentary: Entered with a ~INR53 crore contract from Power Grid Corporation of India for a Kurnool, Andhra Pradesh project; targets INR150-200 crores annual revenue in the next couple of years.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of approximately 30%, implying about INR1,700 crores total and roughly INR1,400 crores over Q2-Q4 (about INR150 crores per month).
FY27 EBITDA margin of 14-15%, 100-150 bps above the 13-14% long-term range, attributed to Alcon integration and better African operations.
FY27 order inflow target of INR3,000 crores; management said it expects to exceed this, as in FY26 (target INR2,000 crores, achieved INR2,400 crores).
Debt expected to reduce over FY27 with no net addition; debt-to-equity to move toward about 0.5x, partly funded by Alcon cash after merger.
Alcon to be merged into GPT Infra in ensuing quarters; African business expected to deliver strong inflows and a sizable South African order this quarter.
capex_capacity: Management did not discuss capex or new capacity additions on the call.
Alcon merger into GPT Infra expected in ensuing quarters, enabling bids for larger value contracts (INR1,500-2,000 crore EPC, 3-4 year execution).
Monsoon season in Q2 expected to affect execution pace.
demand_pricing: Order book INR4,303 crores as of date, down from INR4,480 crores; Q1 fresh inflow about INR130 crores.
Signalling bids of over INR500 crores submitted; under technical evaluation, none converted to orders yet. Company is not L1 in any contract currently.
Addressable market: Indian Railways outlay of about INR1 trillion over six years for signalling (Kavach, electronic interlocking, DDEI); ~USD1.5 billion market cited.
West Bengal: INR895 crores railway investments approved centrally and INR2,100 crores state connectivity projects announced, including Bhagirathi Bridge and Chingrighata-New Town Corridor.
Africa: concrete sleeper business in South Africa, Namibia and Ghana; new South African order expected in the current quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the 30% FY27 growth given Q1 was flat, and can 9M growth reach 40%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was planned as flattish; the INR4,300 crore order book and some late-FY26 orders, with revenue from H2, support about INR1,400 crores over the balance nine months.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 margins stay at the long-term 13-14% after 15.7% in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided FY27 EBITDA margin at 14-15%, with long-term range unchanged at 13-14%; standalone Q1 margin was about 13.7%.

qa_highlights.question: Contract assets and cash conversion?
qa_highlights.answer: Contract assets were about INR430 crores at March end, up about 5%; around INR200 crores has since been billed and received. Q1 operating cash flow not disclosed; to be given in the September quarter or half-year.

qa_highlights.question: Debt position and plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt has not risen materially versus March; management expects to reduce debt over FY27 and targets debt-to-equity near 0.5x from about 0.65x.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the Q1 standalone execution slip and when does it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Labour availability was affected for about half the quarter (April-May); workforce normalised from May, and management expects a monthly run rate of about INR150 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Alcon revenue contribution and signalling bid status?
qa_highlights.answer: Alcon contributed about INR20 crores in Q1 and is guided at INR100-120 crores for FY27; signalling bids worth over INR500 crores are under technical evaluation.

risks_watch: Execution ramp: FY27 30% growth needs about INR1,400 crores over Q2-Q4 versus INR282 crores standalone in Q1; monsoon season in Q2 adds risk.
Order inflow: Q1 inflow of about INR130 crores against INR3,000 crore annual target; order book fell from INR4,480 crores to INR4,300 crores.
Working capital: contract assets elevated, cash flow from operations weak in recent years; Q1 CFO not disclosed.
Alcon merger timing and integration, and conversion of over INR500 crores of signalling bids.
Power EPC: prior execution challenges in this segment; the new entry is small (INR53 crores) and margin target of 13-14% is unproven.
Subcontracting cost ratio moved from about 30% highs to about 20%; management says it depends on project cycle.

533941|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 63% YoY to Rs 78 crore and FY26 revenue reached Rs 255 crore (+58%), with PAT of Rs 19 crore.
533941|2026-03.overview: Thomas Scott reported Q4 FY26 revenue of Rs 78 crore (+63% YoY), EBITDA of Rs 11 crore (14.14% margin) and PAT of Rs 6 crore (7.71% margin), its 10th consecutive quarter of revenue growth. For FY26, revenue was Rs 255 crore (+58%), EBITDA Rs 33 crore (13.1% margin, +105 bps) and PAT Rs 19 crore (+51%). Management said some own-brand sales shifted to outright wholesale sales to marketplace distributors at 30-40% below retail, lowering reported revenue per unit while EBITDA margin was said to be neutral. Working capital, short-term borrowings and receivables drew the most scrutiny, with management attributing much of the stretch to a fire-related inventory loss and March-clustered sales.

FY26 licensed and other brands revenue

qa_highlights.question: Why did other current assets rise from about Rs 7 crore to about Rs 46 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly an insurance claim receivable of about Rs 22 crore from last year's fire, plus Rs 6-8 crore of statutory and financial deposits, rent deposits and supplier advances.

qa_highlights.question: Are the new footwear and premium categories margin accretive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said they will be margin and ROCE accretive, focused on premium brands with higher MRP, and run on partner manufacturing with minimal capital investment.

qa_highlights.question: Why did own-brand revenue fall QoQ in Q4 and how will the revenue mix look?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to outright wholesale sales to marketplace distributors at a lower price; it said the own brand still grows and that EBITDA margin is unchanged on those sales. It declined to give a mix forecast.

qa_highlights.question: How will working capital be funded and what is the sustainable debt level?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt-to-equity was about 0.3-0.4, expected to fall to about 0.2 after insurance recovery; management said current working-capital limits are sufficient and sales are concentrated in the last month of each quarter (70-75%).

qa_highlights.question: Is operating cash flow expected to turn positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Not in the near term: management said positive operating cash flow requires growth at roughly the 23-25% ROCE rate, and the focus remains growth without fresh equity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the receivables trend and is there bad-debt risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said receivable days fell YoY, over 90% of receivables are under six months, and uncollectable amounts are provided immediately; an exceptional provision of about Rs 1.06-1.206 crore was booked in the quarter related to the insurance claim.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity utilisation and expansion plan?
qa_highlights.answer: In-house factories are at full capacity; captive job-work capacity is used for the balance, and Sholapur is the main site for periodic expansion.

qa_highlights.question: How are the two fire incidents being handled and when will the insurance claim be received?
qa_highlights.answer: The first Gurgaon incident was minor; the second was major and is subject to insurance adjustment. Management gave no timeline for the claim, saying only that recovery is expected.

533941|2026-06.headline: Thomas Scott Q1 FY27 revenue rose 22% YoY to INR 66 crore and EBITDA margin was 13.07%, as management chose to hold prices over discounting.
533941|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR 66 crore (+22% YoY), EBITDA INR 9 crore (+43% YoY, margin 13.07%) and PAT about INR 5 crore (+54% YoY, margin 8.21%). Management said subdued price elasticity led it to protect realisations and shift spend from discounts to performance marketing, which it said lifted gross margins. Wholesale-style aggregator sales now make up about 40% of Thomas Scott brand revenue. Finance costs rose sharply on working capital tied to a fire-related insurance claim that is still pending.

segments.name: Licensed and other brands
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 38 crore, up 14% YoY, supported by marketplace relationships and premiumisation. Dockers licence agreements expected to contribute meaningfully in coming quarters.

segments.name: Contract manufacturing
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 4 crore, up 33% YoY, on higher capacity utilisation and marquee customer relationships.

segments.name: Women's wear (newer category)
segments.commentary: Piloted for about two quarters; management says most revenue so far came from testing. Cited as a growth pillar at around 13% of Q1 revenue per analyst question, not disputed.

Offline stores (Bangalore) are EBITDA positive but ROCE is below online opportunities, so capital is directed online; new stores will be selective.
demand_pricing: Price elasticity was subdued in Q1; management says demand exists but price cuts did not earn adequate ROI, so it chose performance marketing over discounts.
Management attributed cautious sentiment partly to global macro conditions, including LPG shortages; said August sentiment is positive.

Wholesale-style aggregator sales booked at B2B price, about INR 10 crore in Q1, equivalent to about INR 15 crore NSV per management; management says these are EBITDA-margin neutral.
Management claims demand exceeds supply capability.
Q1 is an end-of-season sale quarter in which the company chose not to discount heavily.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said unit economics are neutral to favourable versus men's wear, with better return-cost control. Core products such as bottomwear and basic tops show repeat behaviour similar to men's; no share target was given.

qa_highlights.question: Quick commerce strategy and economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Main partner is M-Now (Myntra) at neutral unit economics with no extra fee. Broader quick commerce strategy is still nascent; core categories to be evaluated over the next six to nine months.

qa_highlights.question: Bangalore store performance and expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Stores are EBITDA positive but ROCE is lower than online, so capital goes online. Offline may scale in FY28; new stores will be selective.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue growth slow in ROI for licensed and own brands?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is a margin-pressured end-of-season sale quarter; it chose not to match discounts and invested in marketing instead. Lost revenue could be recovered in festive H2.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company still on track for prior revenue run-rate and margins in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Targets unchanged: same growth rate as the last few years and healthy margins, with margin improvement sought while reserving margin for growth investment.

qa_highlights.question: Fire insurance claim and finance cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Insurance claim (about INR 21 crore of stock, fully insured) is in process; elevated working-capital loans raised to fund inventory are expected to fall once the claim is realised. Exception provisions are small (INR 3-4 lakh).

qa_highlights.question: Dockers deal: B2B or B2C, and effect on premiumisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Dockers agreement is B2C-focused; B2B is used for long-run sourcing orders. More than 94% of revenue is B2C. Dockers fits the premiumisation strategy.

risks_watch: Finance cost rising sharply on working capital; normalisation depends on timing of the insurance claim settlement, which is still in process.
Revenue growth is dependent on the timing of price reinvestment in H2 festive; if festive demand is weak, the growth catch-up may not happen.
Rising other expenses (marketing) and a higher CAC in Q1; watch whether gross margin gains hold as marketing spend rises.
Aggregator/wholesale channel share (about 40% of brand revenue) and its effect on reported revenue vs. NSV; the company reports B2B value, which understates headline sales.

Capacity is fully utilised, so growth depends on job-work and rented capacity.

534076|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 9% to INR 4,000+ crores, a record, but Q4 adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 12.1% and goodwill on Dalmia assets was impaired.
534076|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue from operations grew 9% YoY to INR 4,000 crores on 5% higher shipments of 523 kilotons, the company's highest ever. Q4 revenue was INR 932 crores, hit by geopolitical disruption and a soft cement cycle, with adjusted EBITDA of INR 113 crores (12.1% margin) and adjusted PAT of INR 39 crores before exceptionals. Full-year adjusted EBITDA was INR 477 crores at 11.9% margin versus 13.7% in FY25, and a goodwill impairment on the RHIM IR (Dalmia) assets was booked in the quarter. Management guided to about 13% EBITDA margin for FY27, with price increases of 1-3% from May and a strong coke oven order book.

financial_highlights.metric: Adjusted PAT before exceptional items (Q4 FY26)

segments.name: Dalmia assets (RHIM IR)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 1,153 crores vs INR 1,013 crores in FY25 (+14%); EBITDA margin 10.8% vs 11.5%. Goodwill impairment booked in Q4 on these assets only.

segments.name: Cement
segments.commentary: Cement fell to about 11% of revenue in FY26 from about 13% in FY25 as management chose not to chase low-margin business amid competitor overcapacity (Calderys, IFGL).

segments.name: Iron making / coke oven and DRI
segments.commentary: Secured a 30,000+ tonne order for 2 coke oven batteries with a large integrated steel customer, covering about 15-18 months; mines now transferred into company name, which management says lowers input cost versus buying at roughly double mining cost.

segments.name: Steel
segments.commentary: Largest segment; growth driven by ladle solutions, EAF projects, tundish and ladle slide gate solutions. India-wide steel capacity cited at about 165 million tonnes.

guidance_outlook: FY27 full-year adjusted EBITDA margin guided at about 13%, with Q1 FY27 expected to be stronger than the FY26 average.
Volume growth to outperform the market by 1-2 percentage points (management cited 6-7% market growth, implying about 9% company volume growth).
Price increases of 1-3% sought from May 2026 onwards, depending on segment, to offset input cost inflation; some double-digit increases reportedly secured in certain products.
FY27 capex of about INR 150 crores, of which maintenance capex is INR 40-50 crores; to be funded from balance sheet, with no large transactions planned.
Management stated no further restructuring is required.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex about INR 135 crores, focused on operational excellence, innovation, selective capacity, automation and sustainability.
FY26 spend on Dalmia asset modernisation about INR 100 crores; FY27 capex about INR 150 crores, which also includes Bhiwadi and Jamshedpur.
Two robotic systems operating in caster operations (India's first fully integrated caster robotics solution); further automation expected in coming years.
Coke oven batteries: 5 more expected in next 2-3 years, management expects to win at least 2 of them.
demand_pricing: Management says the refractory industry faces excess capacity, aggressive pricing, and rising raw material, freight and energy costs.
Magnesia-based products (fused magnesia, DBM) saw high-cost inventory and energy and freight increases from China, which hit Feb and March shipments.
Management says Q4 volumes were soft due to the seasonal cement lean period (October to January); Q3 was in line.
Management says the company's volume growth (about 5%) in FY26 was slightly below a market growth of about 6%.
Export volumes declined significantly; imports and new competitor capacity added pressure, in management's view.

qa_highlights.question: Is the restructuring complete, what was the goodwill impairment, and what is the FY27-FY28 roadmap?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said restructuring is complete and only the Dalmia assets were impaired, citing lower export volumes, INR/USD volatility on USD-denominated raw materials, and new competitor capacity. Growth is expected to outperform the market by 1-2%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the coke oven order a one-time project or recurring supply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said coke oven work is project-based but needs no capex; the 30,000+ tonne order covers 2 batteries, and at least 2 of 5 upcoming batteries are expected to follow, supporting the next 3-4 years.

qa_highlights.question: Did inventory cost benefits show up in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the benefit from high-cost alumina inventory was used up, but higher-cost magnesia inventory (fused magnesia, DBM) offset it; double-digit price increases in some cases are expected to offset this and add margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 EBITDA outlook and how is the 2% outperformance measured?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 full-year EBITDA margin guided at about 13%, with Q1 expected to be strong. Outperformance is measured on volume, not price.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Dalmia FY26 revenue and margin, and what is the cement strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Dalmia revenue was INR 1,153 crores (+14%) with a 10.8% margin. Cement share fell to about 11% from 13%; the company is shifting to solution-based selling to large cement customers.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the fixed-cost benefit from iron making is in the margin, and where does margin settle?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify the iron-making fixed-cost absorption separately. On margin, it said 13% is achievable with mines, order book and 4PRO levers, and that without these it could have dropped to 10-11%.

qa_highlights.question: How big are the price increases and what drives Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Price increases sought are 1-3% versus cost increases, effective from May. Q1 is also supported by pending price increases and the start of the cement season (May-September).

risks_watch: Goodwill impairment on Dalmia assets; management cites weaker exports, INR/USD volatility and new capacity.

534076|2026-06.headline: RHI Magnesita India Q1 FY27 revenue rose 6% YoY to INR1,014 crore and EBITDA rose 42% to INR147 crore, a 14.5% margin; management keeps the 13% FY27 margin guidance.

EBITDA grew 42% YoY to INR147 crore and margin expanded to 14.5% from 10.8%, which management attributed to steelmaking execution, price realisation and operating leverage. PAT nearly doubled to INR65 crore from INR35 crore. Management said price increases were largely war surcharges, and it kept FY27 guidance of 13% EBITDA margin and 7-8% volume growth, while stating 9% is a stretch. A leadership change was announced with Pankaj Malhan as MD and CEO, and Parmod Sagar continues as Chairman.

segments.commentary: Recovered in Q1 on seasonal maintenance demand; management said cement season is almost over by end-September.

Capex guidance of INR80-100 crore per year maintained, covering Dalmia plant modernisation, 4PRO machinery, robotics and maintenance.

534091|2026-03.headline: MCX FY26 consolidated revenue more than doubled to INR2,302 crore and PAT crossed INR1,300 crore, with ADT up ~2.5x.
534091|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a very strong year, with consolidated revenue from operations more than doubling to INR2,302 crore and EBITDA of INR1,774 crore. Average daily turnover across futures and options rose about 2.5 times, with bullion growing more than 4 times and energy growing strongly off a high base. Management said growth was both structural and cyclical, but declined to comment on April and May participation and said not every quarter will be a big jump over the prior quarter. Cost lines (product licence fees, other expenses, SGF contribution, software support) rose faster than revenue in Q4, and management said the focus is on efficiency rather than spending less.

financial_highlights.metric: Average daily turnover, futures and options (FY26)
Interest income on margin money (Q4 FY26)
financial_highlights.change: vs INR22 crore in Q4 FY25

financial_highlights.value: About 2% to 3% overall; double-digit share within energy

segments.name: Bullion
segments.commentary: Management said bullion grew more than 4 times and is one of two main volume drivers; market share was stated as unchanged over the last two years despite competitor launches.

segments.name: Energy
segments.commentary: Energy growth was described as good and strong over a very high base; FPIs are a significant contributor within energy, at double-digit share.

segments.name: Indices (BULLDEX / METALDEX)
segments.commentary: BULLDEX options drew strong interest in futures, so management is adding index futures alongside options and plans further work on METALDEX this year.

segments.name: Electricity derivatives
segments.commentary: Early stage; about 50 commercial participants onboarded and UCC numbers rising month on month. Revenue not tracked separately.

segments.name: Coal exchange (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Licence won for a separate coal exchange to operate as a subsidiary; SEBI approval and further regulatory steps are still required, so it is in early stage.

guidance_outlook: Management said it believes the coming year will be a strong year but would not guarantee sequential growth each quarter, citing cyclicality.
Focus over the coming months will be on efficiency rather than cost reduction; investment in technology and people will continue.
Colocation services can be launched at short notice if the regulator permits.
Management expects FPI participation to grow from the current 2% to 3% of overall ADT, with an onboarding pipeline described as strong.
Capital on hand is earmarked for organic and inorganic opportunities, new product segments and ancillary businesses; early-stage strategies were mentioned without detail.
capex_capacity: Product pipeline: management says it is prepared with the next set of products in energy, metals and other segments, with no launch dates given.
Index derivatives: METALDEX to be pursued further this year; index futures to be added alongside BULLDEX options.
Technology and people investments are continuing; no capex figure was disclosed.
Coal exchange is to be set up as a separate subsidiary, not inside MCX; no timeline given.
demand_pricing: Management attributed volume growth to bullion and energy, with bullion growing faster and the two alternating in strength over time.

Retail participation is growing steadily via digital brokers, the consolidated ledger and better user experience; management said it does not expect all equity investors to become commodity investors.
Mutual funds were cited as a future channel for commodity exposure after a regulatory change allowing more flexibility.

Competition: a large competitor has launched multiple bullion and energy products. Management said recent expiry-date changes in energy lead to shallow one-day-a-month activity, which it views as misaligned with global contract structuring.
RBI lending norms for prop traders may affect credit lines for some members across segments; RBI extended the timeline, and the impact was not quantified.
Management declined to comment on April and May participation, saying there is no dramatic cause for concern.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FPI contribution and status of allowing FPIs into gold and silver contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: FPIs contribute about 2% to 3% of overall ADT and are a double-digit share of energy. The consultation paper is still pending; management will await the outcome.

qa_highlights.question: Is the increase in UCC base-driven, and what is driving retail participation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management wants democratic, steady growth rather than aggressive push. Digital brokers, the consolidated ledger and UX improvements are cited; mutual funds and wealth channels are expected to add participation later.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a reason for the Q4 jump in other expenses and the margin shortfall, and are these one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed there were no one-offs. Costs are for growth, technology and people. Q4 other expenses were attributed to market development and professional charges.

qa_highlights.question: What is the interest income on margin money?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 FY26 interest income was INR59 crore, up from INR22 crore in Q4 FY25, due to higher cash placed with the subsidiary. The full-year figure was not given.

qa_highlights.question: Is SGF comfortable, and is there a policy on the share of transaction charges?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SGF is comfortable with a good cushion. No percentage of transaction charges has been published; SGF needs depend on volatility, margins, volume and OI together.

qa_highlights.question: Does interoperability with equity clearing corporations explain why liquidity is not shifting, and how do RBI norms affect BG and FD funding?
qa_highlights.answer: Management disputed the 55% to 60% BG share cited by the analyst and said FDs are the largest portion and fully funded. Interoperability is harder in commodities because products are not identical to equity instruments; the regulator decides.

risks_watch: RBI lending norms for prop traders and member credit lines; the extent of the impact is unquantified.
Competition from a large competitor in bullion and energy, and from equity exchanges entering commodities.
Energy expiry-date changes by competitors and their effect on liquidity.
Pending SEBI consultation on FPI participation in non-cash-settled commodity contracts (gold and silver).
Q4 cost growth ahead of revenue, with no clear guidance on the expense run rate.
Volume dip in April per analyst, which management did not comment on for the current quarter.
534091|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on FY26 scale and the structural growth story, but cautious on quarterly momentum and evasive on April–May participation, competitor threats and the prop-trader RBI norms. Management declined to answer questions on uncontrollable industry matters and on specific cost one-offs beyond a brief explanation.
key_quotes: It's been a good year with good results, and I'm very pleased to report this, very exceptional year, building strong momentum that we have seen in earlier quarters.
So, we do believe that we will have a strong year. Now will every year -- every quarter be a big jump over the previous quarter, perhaps not.
So, if you are asking whether our focus is going to be on margins in the coming months, our focus will be on efficiency.
From whatever we see, our bullion numbers remain untouched when it comes to market share over the last 2 years.

rows.why: No physical capacity is discussed; the only platform-type addition is colocation services, which depend on regulator permission, and no capex figure was disclosed.

534091|2026-06.headline: MCX Q1 FY27 total income rose 85% YoY to INR752 crores and PAT reached INR413 crores, though revenue fell sequentially from an exceptional Q4 FY26.
534091|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 total income of INR752 crores (+85% YoY), revenue from operations of INR702 crores (+88% YoY), EBITDA of INR544 crores (about 72% margin) and PAT of INR413 crores. Management described Q1 as a consolidation after an exceptionally strong Q4 FY26, with ADT at INR10.5 lakh crores and futures ADT up 47% YoY. Bullion options premium ratio fell sharply as volatility normalised, while notional volumes rose, and management said bullion volumes were softer in the quarter. Management said the RBI bank guarantee rule (in force from July) is not expected to be significantly detrimental, and that it is more a Q2 issue.

financial_highlights.metric: Bullion options premium ADT vs notional
financial_highlights.change: premium ADT down 27% QoQ, notional up about 116% QoQ

segments.name: Energy (crude, natural gas, electricity)
segments.commentary: Crude and natural gas form a large share of volume; crude options volume was flat QoQ despite three months of heightened prices. Electricity futures Q1 ADT about INR37 crores with about 55% ADT market share and about 1,630 lots open interest.

segments.name: Bullion (gold, silver)
segments.commentary: Gold options ADV about 300 metric tons (+100% QoQ) and silver about 9,400 metric tons (about +2% QoQ) per management. Silver all-variant options open interest rose to 583 tonnes from 522 tonnes; gold to 17.3 tonnes from 16.9. Management said bullion numbers were softer in the quarter.

segments.name: Indices and metals
segments.commentary: BULLDEX index product is being reworked in futures and options; management expects it to lift indices. Metals options headroom cited, particularly copper after warehouse and contract rationalisation, with no launch dates given.

guidance_outlook: Management expects growth momentum at the fundamental level to continue; Q4 FY26 exceptional numbers will weigh on YoY comparisons.
Management expects FY27 to be strong, but said macro-driven spikes are outside its control.
Bank guarantee regulation: not expected to be significantly detrimental; cost-of-funds impact on some member flows expected to be optimal as industry adapts.
Data services plans and more clarity on revenue from AMC use of MCX bullion price to be shared over the next couple of quarters.
Several indices products expected to hit the market over the next few months.
capex_capacity: Technology capacity: handled more than 3 billion transactions a day versus under 1 billion a year earlier, with capacity to handle more than double that.
MCX Coal Exchange of India incorporated; at a very early stage with procedural steps underway; not a derivatives initiative yet.
Silver 100 gram futures launched in the quarter in response to silver prices and received well.
Good Delivery norms expanded to include silver, with the country's first domestic silver refiner and three more domestic gold refiners empanelled.
demand_pricing: Bullion options: management attributed the premium ratio decline mainly to lower volatility in gold and silver; it said contract mix and participation shifts were not significant drivers.
Competition: challenger exchanges are active in adjacent equity segments; management said main head-on contracts have held, with some competitor expiry-date changes under review.

New members: 12 added in the quarter. FPIs: 35 added, taking the count to about 220, with FPIs about 2.5% of the INR10 lakh-plus crore base. FPI expansion to non-energy contracts awaits SEBI progress.
UCCs: flat QoQ after strong prior quarters; management said no target number was given, but FY26 closed at 20 lakh UCCs.
Uncertainty: management could not quantify the share of trades backed by bank guarantees.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the RBI bank guarantee rule on volumes, and why are gold and silver premiums falling while notional rises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the rule is more a Q2 issue, with no significant detrimental impact seen yet. The premium fall reflects normalising volatility; ADT grew from about INR3 lakh crores a year earlier to INR6.6 lakh crores in Q4 and INR10.5 lakh crores in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the sequential decline in SGF contribution (investor protection fund) differ from the revenue decline, and what drove the employee cost increase?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Chandresh Shah said SGF contribution follows SEBI's monthly methodology plus management's buffer choice. Employee cost rose from hiring, increments and higher variable pay in a subsidiary; a one-time 8-9% element will not recur.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the bullion premium decline is due to volatility, contract mix, or participation?
qa_highlights.answer: Praveen DG said volatility normalisation was the main driver; premiums for gold and silver are at similar levels and participation was stable, so contract mix and OTM shifts were not significant.

qa_highlights.question: Is technology capacity adequate for volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has handled more than 3 billion transactions a day, up from under 1 billion a year earlier, with capacity to handle more than double that. Sanjay Rajpal, the new Executive Director for Critical Operations, is focused on resilience and cost.

qa_highlights.question: What is the electricity futures market share and open interest?
qa_highlights.answer: Electricity futures Q1 ADT was about INR37 crores with about 55% ADT market share and about 1,630 lots open interest (over 70% market share in open interest).

qa_highlights.question: What is the float income and what is the revenue opportunity from AMC use of MCX bullion prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Float income was about INR30 crores. Management said the AMC benchmark use is at an early stage with no separate revenue quantified; data services plans will be shared over the next couple of quarters.

risks_watch: RBI bank guarantee rule (effective in July after a 90-day absorption window) could raise member cost of funds and affect prop-trading volumes; the impact is unquantified.
Sequential revenue decline from exceptional Q4 FY26; YoY comparisons will be tough in coming quarters.
Bullion premium ratio compression (1.03% to 0.35%) hurts transaction revenue per notional unit if volatility stays low.
Competition from challenger exchanges in commodity segments, including expiry-date changes.
Pending SEBI decisions on FPI participation in non-energy contracts, the commodity derivatives department, and open items on SBI position limits and co-location.
534091|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on structural growth and product pipeline, but cautious and non-committal on near-term volumes, bank guarantee impact and FPI timelines. Management repeatedly framed Q1 as a normalisation after Q4 and declined to quantify several questions (bank guarantee share, UCC targets, regulatory timelines).
key_quotes: So, what we are seeing this quarter, it's a normalization of that without some of those sort of very strong geopolitical factors playing in at that same extent, but with some of the fundamental and foundational growth elements still continuing to be strong.
We are not expecting this to have a very significant detrimental impact.
So, capacity-wise, very well positioned as we speak in terms of the growth that is coming our way, but we continue to look to drive resiliency, looking at driving scale.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q1 EBITDA margin was about 72% (EBITDA INR544 crores on INR752 crores income), but the bullion premium/notional ratio fell from 1.03% to 0.35% and employee costs rose, so margin direction depends on volatility and cost trends that management did not guide.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Technology already handles more than 3 billion transactions a day, with capacity to more than double; no physical or new-line capacity was announced, so no new capacity comes live in the window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: ADT reached INR10.5 lakh crores in Q1 (from INR6.6 lakh crores in Q4), futures ADT up 47% YoY and traded clients doubled to 13.72 lakh, but management called Q1 a consolidation, bullion volumes were softer, and the RBI bank guarantee rule is a Q2 risk with unquantified impact.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed; the only new spend cited is the early-stage MCX Coal Exchange incorporation, and technology headroom already exceeds double current throughput.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management expects FY27 on strong momentum but gave no numbers, and the Q4 FY26 base (ADT INR6.6 lakh crores) will weigh on YoY comparisons, so an upgrade needs a clearer volume trend.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Revenue fell sequentially from Q4 FY26, bullion premium ratio compressed to 0.35% from 1.03%, and the RBI bank guarantee rule (effective July) could raise member cost of funds, though management said it is not expected to be significantly detrimental.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management said several indices products will hit the market over the next few months (BULLDEX being reworked in futures and options), and silver 100 gram futures launched in Q1 and were well received; metals options have no launch date.

rows.label: RBI bank guarantee rule effect on member flows
rows.why: Rule in force from July with no quantified share of trades backed by bank guarantees; management expects it not to be significantly detrimental but calls it a Q2 issue.

rows.label: FPI expansion into non-energy contracts
rows.why: FPI count is about 220 (35 added in Q1) and FPIs are about 2.5% of the INR10 lakh-plus crore base, but expansion to non-energy contracts awaits SEBI progress with no timeline.

rows.label: Data services and AMC benchmark revenue
rows.why: Management will share data services plans and AMC use of MCX bullion price clarity over the next couple of quarters; no revenue quantified yet and float income was about INR30 crores in Q1.

tone.note: Management was confident on structural growth, technology capacity and the product pipeline, but cautious on near-term volumes, bank guarantee impact and FPI timelines; analysts probed the bullion premium compression, the sequential revenue decline and employee cost growth.
